_about: English for the Ricardo recipes that have no English page on ricardocuisine.com, read by `npm run convert:ricardo`. recipes: Ricardo id -> title, ingredient names in the order of the converted French recipe (quantities and units stay the French ones), steps. ingredients: French name -> English, for names the English pages could not give. Translated by hand, in Ricardo's English style (Canadian spelling).

576.title: Stuffed Squid
instructions: Rinse the squid thoroughly. Separate the head from the body. Remove the hard part (the beak). Dice the tentacles (head).
In a saucepan, sauté the tentacles in 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the oil. Add the garlic, olives, capers and sun-dried tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes over medium heat.

Deglaze with the wine and let reduce for about two minutes. Add the breadcrumbs and mix well. Stuff the squid bodies and close them with a toothpick. Pour the remaining oil into a saucepan and arrange the squid side by side. Add the tomatoes. Season with pepper. Cover and cook over low heat for about 40 minutes. Serve hot, garnished with parsley.

3432.title: Warm Oyster Mushroom and Turkey Confit Salad
instructions: Vinaigrette: In a bowl, combine the vinaigrette ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Salad: In a large skillet over high heat, brown the oyster mushrooms in the butter. Season with salt and pepper. Add the turkey and heat through.
Divide the mesclun among 4 plates. Top with the mushroom and turkey mixture. Drizzle with the vinaigrette. Serve immediately.

4133.title: Baked Spaghetti with Mushrooms
instructions: In a large pot of boiling salted water, cook the pasta until al dente. Reserve about 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the cooking water. Drain and lightly oil the pasta. Set aside.
In a large skillet, brown the mushrooms in 45 ml (3 tbsp) of the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate.

In the same pan, soften the carrot and onion in the remaining oil. Add the meat and brown over high heat, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until the cooking juices have evaporated. Season with salt and pepper. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and tomato paste. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat for about 10 minutes.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven's broiler.

Add the mushrooms and pasta to the sauce. Mix well and heat through. Add cooking water as needed. Adjust the seasoning. Transfer to one or more gratin dishes. Sprinkle with the cheese. Broil for about 5 minutes or until the cheese is golden.

4296.title: Birdseed Cakes
instructions: In a saucepan, slowly melt the suet, stirring frequently. Strain through a sieve. You will need 250 ml (1 cup) of melted fat.
Tie the sticks to the middle of each wire or piece of twine. Knot each end.

In a bowl, combine all the ingredients with the hot melted fat. Divide half the mixture among the pans. For each cake, lay a wire or piece of twine lengthwise on the mixture so that the knotted end hangs over the edge of the pan and the stick is pressed against the opposite side. Divide the remaining mixture among the pans and refrigerate until completely cold.
Unmould and hang. Keeps in the freezer.
For a ball shape, simply let the mixture cool until it can be shaped. With your hands, form three balls, each with a third of the mixture, working a piece of twine into the centre. Refrigerate.

4401.title: Artichokes with Tomato Vinaigrette
instructions: With the rack in the lowest position, preheat the oven to 200 °C (375 °F).
With scissors, trim the tip of each leaf. Cut off the top and the stem of each artichoke. Set aside in lemon water.

In a saucepan, brown the garlic in the oil. Add the onion and soften for about 5 minutes. Add the tomato and tomato paste and continue cooking for about 5 minutes. Add the white wine and the lemon slices. Stand the artichokes in the pan, tops up. Cover and cook for about 45 minutes or until the artichokes are tender. Let cool slightly.
In a bowl, combine the tomato sauce and the mayonnaise. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve the artichokes warm or cold.

4739.title: Strawberry Trifle
ingredients: slice of strawberry Bavarian cream cake
instructions: Pour about 30 ml (2 tbsp) of strawberry coulis into the bottom of a glass. Cut a slice of strawberry Bavarian cream cake. Remove the cake (the crust) and crumble it over the coulis. Top with 1 crushed ladyfinger. Cover with the rest of the Bavarian cream, softened with a fork. Garnish with 60 ml (1/4 cup) of whipped cream and fresh strawberries cut into quarters.

4931.title: Molasses Butter
instructions: In a bowl, cream the butter with an electric mixer. Gradually add the molasses, whisking until smooth. Press into a ramekin and keep refrigerated. Serve at room temperature on pancakes, buckwheat crêpes or toasted bagels.

5011.title: Braised Veal with Cocoa Sauce
ingredients: boneless veal shoulder, trimmed of fat
veal stock, demi-glace or beef broth
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F).
In a large ovenproof pot over high heat, brown the meat in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate.

In the same pot, soften the vegetables. Deglaze with the wine. Add the veal stock and the reserved meat and bring to a boil. Cover and bake for about 2 hours 30 minutes or until the meat falls apart with a fork. Remove the meat from the pot.
Whisk the cocoa and sugar into the cooking juices. Adjust the seasoning. Return the meat to the pot.
Serve the meat in pieces with mashed potatoes and nice carrots.

5477.title: Mango and Strawberry Smoothie
instructions: Mango smoothie: In a blender, purée all the ingredients until smooth. Pour the mango smoothie into a tall glass (about 310 ml or 1 1/4 cups).
Strawberry smoothie: In a blender, purée all the ingredients until smooth.
Gently pour the strawberry smoothie into the glass over the back of a spoon.
Drink with a straw.

5876.title: Chocolate Surprise Mini Cupcakes
ingredients: blue or red liquid food colouring
instructions: Cupcakes: In a bowl, combine the flour, baking soda and salt. Set aside.
In a saucepan, heat the milk with the cocoa, oil, butter and chocolate, whisking until smooth. Let cool slightly.

In another bowl, beat the eggs with the brown sugar using an electric mixer for 3 to 5 minutes or until foamy. On low speed, drizzle in the cooled chocolate mixture, alternating with the dry ingredients, until the batter is smooth. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line 28 medium muffin cups with 60 ml (¼ cup) paper liners.
Using a spoon, pour 30 ml (2 tbsp) of batter into each cup. Bake for about 15 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of a cupcake comes out clean. Let cool on a rack.

Buttercream: In the top of a double boiler, combine the sugar and egg whites. Gently heat the mixture, whisking constantly. When the sugar has completely dissolved and the mixture is hot, remove the top of the double boiler.
Beat the egg white mixture with an electric mixer until it has cooled and forms stiff peaks, about 15 minutes. Add the butter, one cube at a time, beating until the buttercream is smooth.
In a bowl, combine 180 ml (¾ cup) of the buttercream with the food colouring. Set aside. Add the vanilla to the remaining buttercream. Set aside.

With the tip of a small knife, make a small cross-shaped cut in the centre of each cupcake. Using a pastry bag fitted with a ½ cm (¼ inch) plain tip, fill each cupcake with about 5 ml (1 tsp) of the coloured buttercream by inserting the tip into the slit.
Using a pastry bag fitted with a larger plain or star tip, frost the cupcakes with the vanilla buttercream.

6091.title: Lactose-Free Ricotta Cheese
instructions: In a saucepan over medium heat, heat all the ingredients for 10 minutes or until a thermometer reads 90 °C (195 °F). The mixture must not boil or the curd will break apart. Remove from the heat. Let stand without stirring for 15 minutes or until a whitish curd forms on the surface and separates from the yellowish whey.
Line a sieve with four layers of cheesecloth.

Using a large spoon, transfer the curd to the sieve. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the cheese. Let drain for 12 hours in the refrigerator. For a drier ricotta, let it drain longer. Unmould onto a plate or transfer to a bowl.
The ricotta keeps for 1 week in the refrigerator.

6107.title: Churros
instructions: Cinnamon sugar: In a bowl, combine the sugar and cinnamon. Set aside.
Choux pastry: Preheat the oil in the deep fryer to 190 °C (375 °F). Line a baking sheet with paper towels.

In a saucepan, bring the water, brown sugar, oil and salt to a boil. Off the heat, add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough forms a ball and pulls away from the sides.
Return the saucepan to low heat and cook, stirring the dough, for 1 minute.
Remove from the heat and let cool for a few minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, beating vigorously with a wooden spoon or an electric mixer, until the dough is smooth.

Place the dough in a pastry bag fitted with a star tip. Pipe a 10 to 15 cm (4 to 6 inch) strip of dough. Cut it with scissors and let it drop gently into the hot oil. Watch out for splatters. Fry 3 or 4 churros at a time for 3 to 4 minutes or until golden brown. Drain on the paper towels. Repeat with the remaining dough.
Roll the churros in the cinnamon sugar. Serve warm with the spicy chocolate sauce, if desired.

6108.title: Spicy Chocolate Sauce
instructions: Place the chocolate in a bowl.

In a small saucepan, bring the cream to a boil. Pour the hot cream over the chocolate. Let melt for 2 minutes. Whisk the chocolate until the sauce is smooth. Add the spices and stir. Let cool slightly.
If desired, serve the spicy chocolate sauce with the churros or simply with ice cream.

6122.title: Maple Pecan Pie
instructions: Crust: In a food processor, combine the flour and salt. Add the butter and pulse a few seconds at a time until it is the size of small peas. Add the yogurt and water and pulse again until the dough just begins to form. Add more water as needed. Remove the dough from the food processor and shape it into a disk with your hands.
On a floured work surface, roll out the dough and line a 23 cm (9 inch) round tart pan with a removable bottom, 2.5 cm (1 inch) deep. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
With the rack in the lowest position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F).
Filling: In a saucepan off the heat, combine the brown sugar and cornstarch. Add the maple syrup and bring to a boil, whisking. Let cool slightly.
In a bowl, combine the eggs with the cooled syrup. Stir in the pecans. Pour into the crust. Bake for 35 minutes or until the filling is set. Let cool on a rack.

6126.title: Maple Leg of Lamb with Caramelized Vegetables
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
In a bowl, combine the spices, Dijon mustard, horseradish and 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the maple syrup. Set aside.
In a large skillet, brown the cut side of the vegetables in half the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Place the vegetables in a roasting pan or large baking dish.

In the same pan, brown the meat in the remaining oil. Season with salt and pepper. Place the leg of lamb on the vegetables in the baking dish and brush with the spice mixture. Add 500 ml (2 cups) of the broth, the vinegar, the garlic and the remaining maple syrup to the roasting pan.

Bake for about 1 hour or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the meat, without touching the bone, reads 52 °C (125 °F) for medium-rare. Transfer the leg of lamb to a serving dish with the vegetables. Cover with aluminum foil. Let rest for 15 minutes. The temperature will rise to about 58 °C (136 °F). Reserve 500 ml (2 cups) of the cooking juices for the sauce.
Sauce: Mash the flesh of four cloves of the garlic confit.

In a small saucepan, sauté the garlic purée in the butter for about 1 minute. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring. Add the remaining broth and the reserved cooking juices and bring to a boil, whisking. Let reduce until about 375 ml (1 ½ cups) of sauce remains. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice the leg of lamb. Serve topped with the sauce, with the caramelized vegetables and the garlic confit.

6133.title: Yellow Cake with Chocolate Frosting
instructions: Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Butter two 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans. Line the bottoms with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until foamy. Gradually add 125 ml (½ cup) of the sugar in a thin stream and beat until soft peaks form. Set aside.
In another bowl, cream the butter with the remaining sugar and the vanilla. Add the egg yolks and mix until smooth. On low speed, add the dry ingredients alternately with the buttermilk.

Stir a quarter of the meringue into the batter. Using a spatula, gently fold in the remaining meringue. Divide between the pans and bake for about 35 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Let cool slightly. Unmould and let cool on a rack.
Chocolate buttercream: In a bowl, mix the hot water and cocoa well. Set aside.

In the top of a double boiler, combine the sugar and egg whites. Gently heat the mixture, whisking constantly. When the sugar has completely dissolved and the mixture is hot, remove the top of the double boiler. Let cool slightly.

Beat the egg white mixture with an electric mixer until it has cooled and forms stiff peaks, about 15 minutes. Add the butter, one cube at a time, beating until the mixture is smooth and creamy. Stir in the cocoa mixture and the chocolate.

Trim the tops of the cakes to level them. Place one cake on a serving plate. Cover with about 180 ml (¾ cup) of the chocolate buttercream. Top with the second cake and frost entirely with the remaining chocolate buttercream.

6139.title: Basic Vinaigrette
instructions: Whisk all the ingredients together.

6142.title: Lemon Butter Frosting
instructions: In a bowl, combine the lemon juice, water and egg yolk. Set aside.
In a saucepan, melt 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the butter. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring. Add the lemon juice mixture and bring to a boil, whisking. Simmer gently for about 1 minute.
Pour into a bowl, cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface and let cool to room temperature.
Add the sugar and the remaining butter and beat with an electric mixer for about 5 minutes or until the frosting is smooth and creamy.
Delicious with the basic vanilla cake.

6147.title: Veal Bolognese Sauce
instructions: In a large saucepan, cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 1 minute. Add the carrots and cook for 2 minutes. Add the meat and break it up with a wooden spoon. Continue cooking over high heat for 5 minutes without stirring so it can brown.
Add the tomatoes, broth and tomato paste. Lower the heat and simmer gently for about 15 minutes. Off the heat, add the cheese and stir until completely melted. Season with salt and pepper.
The sauce is ready to be tossed with cooked spaghetti.

6148.title: Fattoush Salad
instructions: Pita croutons: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, toss the pita pieces with the oil. Sprinkle with salt and pepper and mix well. Spread on the baking sheet and bake the croutons for about 12 minutes or until golden. Stir twice during cooking. Let cool.
Vinaigrette: In a large bowl, whisk together all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Vegetables: Toss the vegetables and croutons with the vinaigrette in the bowl. Eat the salad right away, as the pita quickly absorbs the vinaigrette.

6149.title: Chicken and Black Bean Tacos
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a saucepan, gently heat the chicken, beans and salsa together. Season with salt and pepper.
Place the shells on the baking sheet. Divide the cheese among the shells. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes or until the cheese has melted.
Place the lettuce, tomato, avocado, sour cream and lime wedges in individual serving bowls. Place the hot shells on a serving plate.
Put the toppings, shells and chicken mixture in the middle of the table. Everyone fills their tacos as they like.

6156.title: Baked Leek and Spinach Risotto
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F).
Place the sausages in a baking dish. Oil them. Set aside.

In a large ovenproof saucepan, soften the leek in half the butter. Season with salt and pepper. Add the rice and cook for 1 minute, stirring to coat well. Add the white wine and reduce until almost dry. Add the broth and bring to a boil. Cover. Place in the oven with the sausages. Bake for about 20 minutes or until the rice is al dente and the sausages are cooked.
Add the spinach, Parmesan and remaining butter to the risotto and stir vigorously for 1 minute. Adjust the seasoning.
Slice the sausages into rounds. Place them on the risotto and garnish with spoonfuls of fresh ricotta.

6161.title: Maple Apple Verrines
instructions: Maple Syrup Jelly: In a bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the water and let bloom for 5 minutes. Set aside.
In a saucepan, bring the remaining ingredients to a boil. Add the gelatin and stir until dissolved. Divide the jelly among six pretty glasses or small canning jars. Refrigerate for about 4 hours.

Maple Candied Apples: In a large skillet, bring the maple syrup and apples to a boil. Simmer, stirring often, until the apples are tender and the juice is syrupy. Let cool slightly and refrigerate until completely cold, about 2 hours. Drain the apples.
Crumble: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a food processor, combine the dry ingredients. Add the butter and pulse until the mixture resembles coarse sand.
Spread on the baking sheet. Bake for about 10 minutes. Stir and continue baking for about 7 minutes or until the crumble is golden brown. Let cool completely.
Whipped Cream: In a bowl, whip the cream and maple syrup until soft peaks form. Add the sour cream and whisk until smooth.
Assembly: Spread the whipped cream over the maple syrup jellies. Top with the apples. Garnish with the crumble.

6162.title: Spiced Apple Glazed Ham
instructions: With a knife, remove the rind from the ham. Trim the fat, leaving only a thin layer about 1 cm (1/2 inch) thick.

Place the ham in a large pot with 1 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick and half the ginger. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes. Drain in a colander. Return the ham and spices to the pot. Cover again with cold water. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes. Drain. For the third time, add the apple juice, ham and spices. Cover with water. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes. Drain the ham, keeping 750 ml (3 cups) of the cooking broth. Discard the spices.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place the ham in a large baking dish, fat side up. Score the fat in a crisscross pattern to form diamonds. Pour 500 ml (2 cups) of the cooking broth into the bottom of the baking dish. Set aside.

In a small saucepan, prepare the glaze. Combine the apple jelly, cider vinegar, 1 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, the remaining ginger and the garlic. Bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes or until the glaze thickens. Keep warm.

Using a brush, brush the surface of the ham with a third of the glaze. Bake for 45 minutes or until the ham is well browned. Brush during cooking: a first time after 10 minutes, then again after 20 minutes. Add cooking broth as needed.
Slice thinly and serve with the cooking juices.

6166.title: Garlic and Herb Chicken Drumsticks with Asparagus, Fennel and Fresh Fig Salad
instructions: Chicken: In a glass baking dish or large freezer bag, combine all the marinade ingredients. Add the chicken drumsticks and coat them well with the marinade. Cover the dish or seal the bag. Refrigerate overnight or for 8 hours.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium. Oil the grate.
Grill the drumsticks for about 10 minutes per side or until the meat comes away easily from the bone.
Salad: Meanwhile, place the asparagus and fennel on a baking sheet and brush them with oil. Salt and pepper.

Grill the vegetables on each side until slightly al dente. On a serving platter, arrange the grilled vegetables and figs, then top with pieces of mozzarella. Drizzle with lemon juice and a little olive oil. Season with pepper. Serve with the garlic and herb chicken drumsticks.

6173.title: Salmon Pie (The Best)
instructions: Filling: In a saucepan of salted water, cook the potatoes and garlic for about 15 minutes or until the vegetables are very tender. Drain. Using a potato masher, mash with 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the butter. Salt and pepper. Set aside.

Meanwhile, in a skillet, soften the leek in the remaining butter. Add the cream and salmon and continue cooking, stirring often, until the salmon is cooked and the cream has reduced almost completely. Add to the mashed potatoes and mix well to flake the salmon. Adjust the seasoning. Set aside.

Béchamel: In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Sprinkle with the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the milk and bring to a boil, stirring with a whisk. Simmer for about 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the cheese. Cover and set aside.
With the rack in the lowest position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

On a floured work surface, roll out the two discs of dough and line a 23-cm (9-inch) pie plate with one of them. Make incisions in the second sheet. Spread the salmon mixture out in the bottom crust. Cover with the bechamel.
Brush around the dough with milk and cover with the second sheet of dough. Crimp the edges and brush with milk.
Bake for about 45 minutes or until the crust is golden brown. Let rest for 15 minutes before serving.

6175.title: Shortcrust Pastry
instructions: In a food processor, combine the flour, baking powder and salt. Add the butter and pulse for a few seconds at a time until the butter is the size of peas. Add the milk and egg. Pulse again until the dough just begins to form. Add milk, as needed. Remove the dough from the food processor and shape it into two disks with your hands (see note). Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate the dough for at least 30 minutes.

6176.title: Lactose-Free Strawberry Ice Cream
instructions: In a bowl, combine the strawberries and 55 g (¼ cup) of the sugar. Let marinate for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a saucepan off the heat, whisk together 55 g (¼ cup) of the sugar and the cornstarch. Add the egg yolks and whisk vigorously. Add the milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan. Remove from the heat. Whisk until the mixture cools to lukewarm. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.
In another bowl, beat the egg whites until foamy. Gradually add the remaining sugar and beat until the meringue forms stiff peaks. Gently fold into the lukewarm egg yolk mixture.
Add the strawberries and their juice. Gently stir in the whipped cream. Pour into a 2-litre (8-cup) container. Cover and freeze for 8 hours or overnight.
Let soften for 5 to 10 minutes before serving.

6183.title: Lemon Iced Rooibos Tea
instructions: In a saucepan, bring 500 ml (2 cups) of the water, the sugar and the lemon to a boil.
Off the heat, add the tea bags and let steep for 5 minutes. Strain through a sieve. Pour into a pitcher with the remaining water (1.5 litres/6 cups) and let cool completely.
Serve with ice cubes.

6187.title: Duck Breasts with Watermelon Salad and Sweet-and-Sour Raisins
instructions: Sweet-and-Sour Raisins: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Let the raisins rehydrate for about 15 minutes. Drain. Set aside.
Duck: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium. Oil the grate.
Using a sharp knife, trim the fat from the duck breasts, leaving only a thin layer.

Place the duck on the grill, fat side down. Cook for about 10 minutes. Increase the heat of the burners and turn the duck breast. Continue cooking for about 5 minutes for medium rare. Transfer to a plate and tent with aluminum foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Melon Salad: In a bowl, gently toss the melon with the watercress, pine nuts, oregano and raisins. Salt and pepper.
Slice the duck breasts and divide them among four plates. Serve with the melon salad and drizzle with olive oil.

6188.title: Cantaloupe and Grilled Zucchini Salad
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the pancetta slices on the baking sheet. Bake for about 15 minutes or until crisp. Drain on paper towels. Crumble coarsely. Set aside.
Preheat the barbecue to high or use a ridged grill pan to cook the zucchini. Oil the grate.
On a baking sheet, oil the zucchini ribbons. Grill on each side.
Divide the zucchini and cantaloupe ribbons among four plates. Salt and pepper. Top with the crumbled pancetta and serve with lemon wedges.

6191.title: Coconut Tapioca with Strawberries and Watermelon
instructions: In a saucepan off the heat, combine the coconut milk, milk, sugar and tapioca, then let stand for about 5 minutes.
Heat and bring to a boil, stirring constantly, and simmer for about 2 minutes.

Remove from the heat, cover and let stand for about 20 minutes, stirring a few times. Add the strawberry purée and mix well. Transfer to a bowl, cover and refrigerate for about 4 hours or until the tapioca is well chilled.
When ready to serve, combine the strawberries and watermelon. Divide the cold tapioca among dessert cups and top with the fruit mixture.

6259.title: Sushi Pizza
instructions: Preheat the oil in the fryer to 375 °F (190 °C). Line a plate or baking sheet with paper towels.
Place the breadcrumbs in a bowl. In another bowl, prepare the tempura batter according to the package directions.

With your hands, shape the rice into two patties about 2 cm (3/4 inch) thick. Brush the patties with the tempura batter, then coat them with breadcrumbs. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes or until the patties are golden brown. Drain on the paper towels.
In a bowl, place the imitation crab, salmon, green onion and tempura crunch. Add half the tobiko and half the mayonnaise. Season to taste with sriracha sauce and mix well.
In a small bowl, combine the remaining mayonnaise with a little sriracha sauce.
Cut the patties into six wedges. Spread a little spicy mayonnaise on each wedge. Top with the crab and smoked salmon mixture. Garnish the bites with the remaining tobiko.

6308.title: Honey Rosemary Chicken Legs
ingredients: large rectangles of heavy-duty aluminum foil
instructions: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. To cook in the oven, place the rack in the middle position and preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F).

Place a chicken leg on two stacked sheets of aluminum foil. Top with a sprig of rosemary and drizzle with honey. Salt and pepper. Seal the packets tightly and place them on the barbecue grill. Cook for about 15 minutes per side or until the chicken is cooked and the meat comes away easily from the bone. To cook in the oven, place the chicken directly on a baking sheet and bake for about 45 minutes.

6310.title: 5-Minute Coconut Milk Pangasius
instructions: In a saucepan, combine all the ingredients except the lime juice. Salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer gently for about 5 minutes. Add lime juice to taste. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve on jasmine rice with green vegetables and lime wedges.

6323.title: Bacon-Crumb Crusted Pork Tenderloins
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil or parchment paper.
In a food processor, finely chop the frozen bacon slices. Add the breadcrumbs and chives and pulse for a few seconds. Set aside on a plate.
In a bowl, whisk together the mustard and honey. Set aside.

Brush the meat with the mustard mixture. Salt and pepper. Roll the pork tenderloins in the breadcrumb mixture, pressing firmly. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, depending on the size of the tenderloins, for pink meat. If needed, brown under the broiler for a few minutes. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Slice thinly. Serve with green vegetables and the vanilla and pink peppercorn mashed potatoes.

6324.title: Vanilla and Pink Peppercorn Mashed Potatoes
instructions: Split the vanilla bean in half. With the tip of a knife, remove the seeds.
In a saucepan, gently heat the milk with the vanilla seeds and pod until the milk is hot. Remove the vanilla pod.
Meanwhile, in a saucepan, cook the potatoes in salted water until very soft, about 15 minutes. Drain.
With a potato masher, crush the potatoes with the butter. With an electric mixer, mash the mixture with the vanilla milk and pink peppercorns. Adjust the seasoning.

6327.title: Vanilla Frosting
instructions: With an electric mixer or a stand mixer, beat the butter, sugar, cream, vanilla and salt for 2 minutes or until fluffy and smooth. Add boiling water, 15 ml (1 tablespoon) at a time, beating 30 seconds between each addition. Spread about 180 ml (3/4 cup) of frosting between each layer of a vanilla cake and 430 ml (1 3/4 cups) over the outside of the cake.

6328.title: The Perfect Vanilla Cake
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line two 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans with parchment paper and butter them. Set aside.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, beat the eggs, sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer until the mixture turns pale, doubles in volume and falls from the whisk in a ribbon, about 10 minutes. Drizzle in the oil while beating.

At low speed, add the dry ingredients alternately with the milk until smooth. Divide the batter between the two pans and bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool for 15 minutes. Unmould and let cool completely on a wire rack.
On a work surface, slice a thin layer off the top of the cakes to level them, then cut them in half horizontally. Set aside.
Delicious with vanilla frosting.

6330.title: Pear and Caramel Trifle
instructions: Pastry Cream: In the microwave, heat the milk and cream. Set aside.
In a saucepan, combine the sugar and flour. Add the egg yolks and whisk until smooth. Gradually add the hot cream mixture, whisking.
Bring to a boil over medium heat while whisking. Remove from the heat at the first sign of a boil. Add the vanilla.
Place plastic wrap directly on the surface of the hot pastry cream. Cool and refrigerate for about 2 hours or until completely chilled.

Caramelized Pears: In a large skillet, heat the water and sugar until golden. Over high heat, sauté the pears for 4 to 5 minutes. Set aside on a plate. Let cool and refrigerate until completely chilled.

Caramel Sauce: In a saucepan, bring the water, sugar, and syrup to a boil. Cook without stirring until the mixture turns golden brown. Off the heat, gradually add the cream. Bring to a boil, stirring until the mixture is smooth. Transfer to a bowl and let cool completely.
Assembly: In a bowl, whip the cream, sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form.

In a glass serving bowl of about 3 litres (12 cups), assemble the trifle by layering half of each component (except the caramel, which is divided into four): pastry cream, ladyfingers, pears, caramel and whipped cream. Repeat with the rest, finishing with the whipped cream, a quarter of the caramel and the almonds. Serve the remaining caramel on the side.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

6331.title: Profiteroles
instructions: Choux Pastry: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a saucepan, bring the milk, water, butter, sugar and salt to a boil. Remove the saucepan from the heat and add the flour all at once. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough forms a smooth ball that pulls away from the sides.
Return the saucepan to the stove and cook over low heat while stirring the dough for about 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let cool for a few minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, beating vigorously with a wooden spoon or an electric mixer after each addition, until the dough is smooth.
Using a pastry bag fitted with a round tip of about 1 cm (1/2 inch) and filled with the choux pastry, pipe 16 golf ball-sized puffs onto the baking sheet. Flatten the peaks with a wet fingertip.
Bake in the middle of the oven until the crust is golden brown, about 40 minutes. Turn the oven off and let dry for about 15 minutes with the door ajar. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
Chocolate Sauce: In a saucepan, bring the cream to a boil. Remove from the heat and add the chocolate. Let rest for 2 minutes. Whisk until smooth. Keep warm.
Cut the tops off the cooled puffs. Fill with a scoop of ice cream. Close. Cover with the hot chocolate sauce.

6334.title: Mini Po' Boy Sandwiches
instructions: Tartar Sauce: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Keep refrigerated.
Fried Oysters: Preheat the deep fryer to 180°C (350°F). Lay several layers of paper towel on a tray.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven's broiler.
In a bowl, combine the cornmeal and cayenne pepper. Season with salt. Dip the oysters in the cornmeal mixture to coat them well.

Lower half the oysters into the deep fryer and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, depending on their size, until golden. Drain and place the oysters on paper towels. Repeat with the remaining oysters. Season with salt.
Sandwich: Meanwhile, toast the bread, cut side up, under the broiler for 2 to 3 minutes.

Spread the toasted side of each piece of bread with tartar sauce. Top with lettuce, tomato and fried oysters. Close the baguette and press firmly. Cut into pieces about 5 cm (2 inches) long and insert a toothpick in each bite.
Serve as an appetizer or for lunch.

6336.title: Rustic Apple and Summer Berry Pie
instructions: Crust: In the bowl of a food processor, place the flour, salt and sugar. Pulse for a few seconds. Add the butter and pulse a few seconds at a time until pea-sized pieces form. Add the eggs and water. Pulse again until the dough just begins to form. Add water, if needed. Remove the dough from the food processor and form into a disc. Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate.
On a floured work surface, roll out the dough into a disk of about 46 cm (18 inches).

Place the rack in the middle position. Place a pizza stone on it. Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). If you don't have a pizza stone, use the back of a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, without preheating it in the oven.
Filling: In a bowl, combine the sugar and tapioca. Add the berries and mix well. Let rest for 10 minutes.

Sprinkle the pizza peel with cornmeal. Place the crust on it. Cover the bottom with apple slices over about 30 cm (12 inches). Add the berry filling and fold the dough over the fruit. You can turn the edge of the dough up slightly to keep the filling from running out. Bake for about 40 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown.
Serve the pie with vanilla ice cream.

6337.title: Barbecue-Baked Blueberry Pudding Cake
instructions: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high.
Fruit: In a bowl, combine the sugar and cornstarch. Add the blueberries and stir to combine. Spread in a 20 cm (8 inch) square disposable aluminum pan. Press lightly and set aside.

Dough: In a bowl, combine the flour, sugar, and baking powder. Drizzle in the butter and mix. Add the ginger ale and stir with a wooden spoon until smooth. Spread over the fruit. Reduce the barbecue heat to medium-low. Place the pudding on the barbecue grill and close the lid. Cook for about 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the batter comes out clean. To bake in the oven, place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Bake the pudding in a Pyrex dish for about 1 hour 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the batter comes out clean.
Let cool for 15 minutes and serve with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

6339.title: Tomcod à la Meunière (Pan-Fried in Butter)
instructions: Pat the tomcod dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, place the flour. Dredge the fish in flour. Shake to remove any excess.

In a large non-stick skillet, melt the butter until foamy. Brown the fish on both sides until the backbone comes away easily. Season generously with salt and pepper. Serve immediately. Serve with lemon wedges, if desired.

6342.title: Jerusalem Artichoke Gratin
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

In a bowl, combine the cream, egg, garlic and nutmeg. Add the Jerusalem artichokes. Salt and pepper. Spread in a 20 cm (8 inch) square Pyrex baking dish. Bake for about 50 minutes or until tender. Serve as a side with pork or beef.

6343.title: Cauliflower Purée
instructions: In a saucepan, soften the onion in half the butter. Add the cauliflower, garlic and milk. Salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer gently for about 15 minutes or until the cauliflower is tender. Drain well, keeping the milk for another use, such as cream of cauliflower soup.
In a food processor, purée the cauliflower until smooth with about 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the cooking milk and the remaining butter. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve with pork, beef or chicken.

6344.title: Roasted Celery with 20 Cloves of Garlic
ingredients: fleur de sel or sea salt
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
On a baking sheet, toss the celery, garlic and oil. Season with salt. Bake for 10 minutes. Stir and continue cooking for about 10 minutes. Sprinkle with the celery leaves and adjust the seasoning.
Serve with pork, beef or chicken.

6345.title: Maple Pecan Biscotti
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a food processor, combine the flour, 125 ml (½ cup) of the maple sugar and the baking powder. Add the butter and pulse until it has a coarse texture. Add the egg and vanilla. Blend gently.
Place the dough in a bowl and finish mixing it with your hands, adding the pecans.
On a floured work surface, roll the dough into a 30-cm (12-inch) long log. Place the log on the baking sheet. Bake for 30 minutes. Transfer to a work surface.
Let the log cool for about 10 minutes. Brush with milk and sprinkle with the remaining maple sugar (30 ml/2 tbsp). Using a bread knife, cut the log on the diagonal into 2 cm (¾ inch) thick slices.
Place the slices on the baking sheet and bake for 20 minutes, turning them halfway through, until the biscotti are golden. Let cool on a wire rack.

6348.title: Oysters with Pink Grapefruit
instructions: Cut the grapefruit into segments. To do this, peel the grapefruit down to the flesh. Cut off both ends of the fruit. Place one of the cut sides on a cutting board so the fruit is stable. Slide a very sharp knife between the flesh and the peel to remove it, along with the white pith. Then hold the fruit in your hand and insert the knife blade between the membranes to lift out the segments of flesh: the suprêmes. Work over a bowl to catch the juice.

Cut the segments into small pieces. Place in a bowl. Squeeze the rest of the grapefruit over the bowl to get the juice. Add the remaining ingredients except the oysters. Refrigerate while you prepare the oysters.
Shuck the oysters and remove the shellfish from their shells. Place the oysters on a platter covered with crushed ice or salt. Spoon the filling into the dough. Serve immediately.

6353.title: Olive Oil Roasted Baby Vegetables
ingredients: mini bell peppers in assorted colours
baby pattypan squash in assorted colours
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In a baking dish of about 33 x 23 cm (13 x 9 inches), combine all the ingredients except the chives. Salt and pepper. Bake for about 45 minutes or until the vegetables are tender. Sprinkle with chives.
Serve with duck, poultry or beef.

6356.title: Honey-Roasted Figs with Caramelized Almond Ice Cream
instructions: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Ice Cream: In a hot skillet over medium heat, cook the almonds and honey, stirring, until the honey caramelizes and turns slightly darker. Pour and spread the mixture in a thin layer on the baking sheet. Place the baking sheet in the freezer for 15 to 30 minutes or until the nougatine has hardened. Break the nougatine into pieces and set aside eight small shards on parchment paper, in the cold, for decoration.

In a food processor, blend the ice cream and almond butter until smooth. Add the nougatine pieces and pulse a few seconds at a time until the almonds are finely chopped. This step must be done quickly. Pour into an airtight container. Freeze for about 2 hours or until the ice cream is firm.
Roasted Figs: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

With a knife, cut a cross in the top of each fig and stand them upright in a 20 cm (8 inch) square Pyrex dish. Add the thyme sprigs and pour the honey over the figs. Bake for about 20 minutes or until the figs are puffed and split open by the heat. Baste the figs with honey several times during cooking.
Serve one fig per person with a scoop of the caramelized almond ice cream. Drizzle with honey and decorate with a shard of nougatine. Garnish with the thyme.

6358.title: Frozen Maple Parfait with Praline Pecans
instructions: Maple Caramel: In a saucepan, bring both syrups to a boil. Cook without stirring until a candy thermometer reads 132 °C (270 °F). Off the heat, gradually add the cream. Beware of splattering. Bring to a boil, stirring until the mixture is smooth. Remove from the heat and pour into a large bowl (the caramel will cool faster). Place in the freezer and stir often until the caramel has cooled, 15 to 20 minutes.
Line a lightly oiled 20 cm (8 inch) square Pyrex dish with plastic wrap. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Praline Pecans: In a small saucepan, bring both syrups to a boil. Cook without stirring until the syrup starts to caramelize, about 1 minute. Add the pecans and coat them well. Spread on the baking sheet. Allow to cool. Chop and set aside.

Ice Cream: In a bowl, whip the cream and sugar with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. On low speed, add to the ice cream and mix just until smooth. Stir in the pecans. Spread half this mixture in the dish. Drizzle half the caramel over it in a spiral. Gently spread the remaining frozen mixture on top. Finally, drizzle the remaining caramel in a spiral. Run a knife through the frozen mixture to create a marbled effect. Freeze for 6 hours or overnight.
When ready to serve, let soften for 5 minutes. Unmould and cut into squares or slices.

6361.title: Mushroom Duxelles
instructions: In a skillet, brown the mushrooms and shallot in the butter. Salt and pepper. Deglaze with the wine. Bring to a boil and reduce until almost dry. Add the chives.
Serve on the brie cream.

6362.title: Potage Choisy (Lettuce Soup)
instructions: In a saucepan over medium-high heat, soften the onion in the butter. Add the potatoes, broth and milk. Salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. Add the lettuce. Bring to a boil and continue cooking for 1 to 2 minutes.
In a blender, purée the soup until smooth. Adjust the seasoning. Serve warm or cold.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Garnish with the sour cream.

6363.title: Cabbage and Beet Soup
instructions: In a saucepan, brown the onion in the oil. Add the brown sugar and cook for one minute, stirring. Deglaze with the vinegar. Add the remaining ingredients except the parsley. Salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for about 25 minutes or until the vegetables are tender. Add the parsley and adjust the seasoning.

6365.title: Three-Cheese Stuffed Cabbage
ingredients: Riopelle cheese or other triple-cream brie
Oka, d'Iberville or other washed-rind cheese, rind removed, cubed
top part of 1 small butternut squash
Valbert cheese or other firm cheese
instructions: In a large pot of boiling salted water, blanch the cabbage leaves for about 4 minutes or until tender. Drain and rinse under cold water. Set aside.
In a skillet, soften the leek in the butter. Add the wine and reduce until almost dry. Add the brie and the washed-rind cheese. Stir until the cheese has melted. Salt and pepper. Set aside.

In the same pot, place the potatoes, milk, thyme and garlic. Salt and pepper. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat for about 5 minutes or until the potatoes are al dente. Stir a few times so the milk doesn't stick. Remove the thyme and the garlic clove. Drain the potatoes and return the milk to the pot. Add the squash and bring back to a boil. Add milk, as needed. Simmer over medium heat until al dente. Drain and set aside.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line the bottom of a 23-cm (9-inch) springform pan with parchment paper.

Place a large cabbage leaf in the bottom of the pan. Line the sides of the pan with six leaves, letting them hang over the edge. Place another leaf in the bottom. Add two thirds of the potatoes. Salt and pepper. Press lightly and spread the leek and cheese mixture over them. Add the remaining potatoes, then the squash. Finish with the firm cheese and top with a cabbage leaf. Fold the leaves toward the centre and finish with a cabbage leaf.

Brush with butter. Wrap the pan in two sheets of aluminum foil. Place the pan on a baking sheet. Bake for about 1 hour and 30 minutes. Remove from the oven. Place a plate on top. Let stand for 15 minutes.
Unmould and serve with a green salad.

6367.title: Buttered Sugar Snap Peas
ingredients: sugar snap peas or snow peas
instructions: In a pot of boiling salted water, blanch the sugar snap peas. Drain.
In a skillet, sauté the peas in the butter and water for about 2 minutes. Salt and pepper.

6368.title: 4-Hour Milk-Braised Pork
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In a large ovenproof pot, brown the pork in the butter. Salt and pepper. Add the milk. Bring to a boil. Add the vegetables and nutmeg. Cover and bake for 2 hour and 30 minutes. If the milk seems to curdle at the start of cooking, don't worry. The liquid will be strained.
Uncover and continue cooking for about 1 hour 30 minutes or until the sauce has reduced by a little more than half. Turn the pork every 20 minutes.
Remove the roast from the pot. Set aside. Strain the liquid. Whisk the sauce and adjust the seasoning.
Serve the roast on a large platter with the sugar snap peas all around. Slice the roast and serve with the sweet potato purée.

6370.title: Buckwheat Honey Glazed Lamb Shanks
ingredients: sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large skillet, brown the shanks in the oil and butter. Salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate.
Deglaze the skillet with the vinegar and brandy. Reduce by half.

Add the broth and honey and bring to a boil. Salt and pepper. Return the shanks to the skillet. Add the orange, onion and garlic. Bake for 1 hour, basting the meat often. Add the remaining vegetables around the shanks, pressing them into the broth. Continue cooking for about 45 minutes or until the meat is well caramelized. Cover and continue cooking for 30 to 45 minutes or until the meat comes away easily from the bone and the vegetables are tender.
Delicious with mashed potatoes.

6371.title: Portuguese-Style Cod Casserole
instructions: If, like the Portuguese, you're using a 3-litre (12-cup) clay pot, soak it in water with its lid for about 15 minutes. If you're using another type of dish, place the rack in the middle of the oven and preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F).
In a skillet, brown the onions in the oil until well caramelized. Salt and pepper. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Set aside.

Spread a quarter of the potatoes over the bottom of the dish. Top with half the tomatoes and olives. Salt and pepper. Cover with another quarter of the potatoes. Sprinkle with the onion mixture. Add a third quarter of the potatoes, then spread the fish over them. Salt and pepper. Top with the remaining potatoes, tomatoes and olives. Add the broth.

Cover and place the clay pot in the centre of the cold oven (important). Set the oven temperature to 200 °C (400 °F). Bake for about 1 hour 15 minutes (about 1 hour for a ceramic or glass dish) or until the potatoes are tender. Let rest for 15 minutes before serving.

6373.title: Chocolate Carrot Cake
instructions: Carrot Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Butter two 20-cm (8-inch) in diameter springform pans. Line the bottoms with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, beat the eggs, sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer for about 10 minutes or until the mixture turns pale and doubles in volume. Gently stir in the melted butter with a spatula. Gently fold in the dry ingredients using a whisk. Add the carrots and chocolate.

Spoon the batter into the prepared pans. Bake for about 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Run a thin blade around the cake to release it from the pan. Unmould and cool completely on a rack.
White Chocolate Ganache: Melt the chocolate in a double boiler. Off the heat, add the sour cream and stir until smooth. Let cool for about 2 hours or until the cake has cooled completely.

Beat the chocolate mixture with an electric mixer for about 2 minutes, until it starts to firm up slightly. If needed, place it in the refrigerator for a few minutes. Spread the ganache over the top of both cakes. Stack the two cakes.

Candied Carrots: In a saucepan, bring the orange juice and sugar to a boil. Add the carrots. Simmer for about 8 minutes, depending on their thickness, or until the carrots are tender and translucent. Let cool completely in the syrup. Drain, and place a rolled carrot slice to mark each slice of cake.

6374.title: Tiramisu Without Mascarpone
ingredients: coffee liqueur or crème de cacao
instructions: In a bowl, dissolve 30 ml (2 tablespoons) sugar in the coffee. Refrigerate.
In a food processor, process the cream cheese, ricotta and liqueur until very smooth. Set aside.

In a large bowl, beat the egg whites until they form soft peaks. Gradually add the remaining sugar, beating until stiff peaks form. Using a spatula, gently fold the cheese mixture into the egg whites.

Quickly dip the ladyfingers in the coffee to soak them. Place half the ladyfingers in the bottom of a glass serving bowl of about 3 litres (12 cups). Cover with half the cheese filling and continue with the remaining ladyfingers and filling. Dust the top with cocoa through a sieve. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.

6375.title: Portuguese Caramel Flan
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F).

Caramel: In a saucepan, bring the sugar and water to a boil. Cook without stirring until the mixture turns golden brown. Immediately remove from the heat. Using a silicone brush, coat the inside of a Bundt pan about 8 cm (3 1/2 inches) deep or with a 1.5-litre (6-cup) capacity. Work quickly at this stage so the caramel doesn't harden.

Flan: In a saucepan, bring 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the sugar and the water to a boil. Cook without stirring until the mixture turns golden brown. Off the heat, gradually add the cream. Beware of splattering. Bring to a boil, stirring until the mixture is smooth. Add the milk and mix well. Set aside.

In a bowl, whisk the eggs and egg yolks with the remaining sugar. Whisk in the hot milk mixture. Strain through a sieve. Pour into the prepared pan. Prepare a water bath: place a cloth in a large baking dish, set the pan on it and fill the dish halfway up with steaming water. Bake for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until the flan is jiggly. Remove the pan from the water bath. Let cool. Refrigerate for about 3 hours or until completely chilled. Dip the pan in a bath of boiling water for a few seconds, then turn out onto a serving plate.

6376.title: Brown Sugar Chiffon Cake with Vanilla Mango Salad
instructions: Chiffon Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 170 °C (325 °F).
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt.
In another bowl, beat the egg whites and cream of tartar until soft peaks form. Gradually add half the brown sugar and beat until the meringue forms stiff peaks. Set aside.
In another bowl, whisk together the remaining brown sugar, egg yolks, oil, water and vanilla. Add the dry ingredients and mix gently.

With a spatula, stir a quarter of the meringue into the batter. Add the rest and gently fold it in. Pour into an unbuttered 25 cm (10 inch) tube pan that is not non-stick. Bake for 55 minutes to 1 hour or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Turn the pan upside down immediately and let cool upside down for 3 hours. Unmould.
Vanilla Mango Salad: With the tip of a knife, split the vanilla bean in half lengthwise to open it. Remove the seeds.

In a saucepan, bring the water, 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the sugar and the vanilla seeds and pod to a boil. Add the mangoes. Remove the saucepan from the heat and let cool. Drain, and keep the syrup for a fruit salad.
In a bowl, whip the cream and the remaining sugar until stiff peaks form. Keep refrigerated.
Serve a slice of cake with the whipped cream and a little mango salad.

6380.title: Pont-Neuf Potatoes
instructions: Cut the potatoes into sticks 1.5 cm (3/4 inch) thick.
In a bowl, cover the potatoes with cold water. Let stand for about 5 minutes. Drain and pat the potatoes dry with a clean towel.
In a large, deep skillet or a large pot, melt the duck fat. Fry the potatoes over high heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring gently and often, until golden. Drain on paper towels. Season with salt.
Delicious with veal medallions with coffee and cognac sauce, or with duck breasts with spice and whisky sauce.

6382.title: Béchamel
instructions: In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Whisk in the milk. Stir until it comes to a boil. Add the nutmeg. Salt and pepper. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring often so the sauce doesn't stick to the bottom.

6383.title: Prime Rib with Béarnaise Sauce
ingredients: white part of three small leeks
instructions: Roast: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Season the roast with salt and pepper on all sides and place it bone side down in a roasting pan.
In a bowl, combine the mustards, butter and brown sugar. Brush over the meat. Insert a meat thermometer in the centre of the roast. Bake for 20 minutes.

Toss the carrots, leeks and onions with oil. Salt and pepper. Spread the vegetables around the roast and add the chicken broth. Continue cooking for about 1 hour 10 minutes or until the thermometer reads 54 °C (129 °F) for rare or 63 °C (145 °F) for medium. Set aside on a plate. Cover with aluminum foil and let stand for about 15 minutes.
Béarnaise Sauce: In a saucepan, bring the vinegar, shallot and pepper to a boil. Reduce until only 30 ml (2 tablespoons) of liquid remain.
In a double boiler, whisk the egg yolks and the vinegar reduction until thick and foamy. Remove the bowl from the double boiler. Drizzle in the butter, whisking constantly. Add the tarragon.
Remove the string and slice the roast. Serve with vegetables of your choice, the béarnaise sauce and good mashed potatoes.

6384.title: Caramel Nut Tart
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

Shortbread: In the bowl of the food processor, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Add the butter and pulse until the mixture has the texture of sand. Add the egg and water. Pulse again until the dough just begins to form. Remove the dough from the processor. With your fingertips, press the dough into a 23 cm (9 inch) tart pan with a removable bottom, 3 cm (1 1/4 inches) deep. Bake for 25 minutes or until the crust is golden. Allow to cool.

Filling: In a saucepan, bring the water and sugar to a boil. Cook without stirring until the mixture turns golden brown. Off the heat, gradually add the cream. Beware of splattering. Bring to a boil, stirring until the mixture is smooth. Stir in the butter and nuts. Let cool for about 30 minutes. Pour into the crust and refrigerate until completely cold.

6440.title: Curried Tofu Stir-Fry
instructions: In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the tofu on each side in half the oil (30 ml/2 tbsp). Set aside on a large plate.
In a saucepan, soften the onion, garlic and vegetables in the remaining oil (30 ml/2 tbsp) and cook for 5 minutes. Add the tofu and curry powder. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the remaining ingredients. Mix well. Continue cooking until the vegetables are al dente. Salt and pepper. Divide the tofu stir-fry among bowls. Serve with white rice, if desired.

6455.title: Tropical Smoothie
instructions: In a blender, purée all the ingredients until smooth. Serve immediately.

6456.title: Apple Blueberry Muffins
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line 12 muffin cups with paper or silicone liners.
In a bowl, combine the almond flour, oats, brown sugar, flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.

In another bowl, combine the eggs, yogurt and apple. Stir into the dry ingredients until just moistened. Using a spatula, gently fold in the blueberries. Spread into the prepared pans. Sprinkle with the almonds.

Bake for 23 to 25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of a muffin comes out clean. Let cool on a wire rack. Although they are best the day they are made, the muffins keep for 2 days in an airtight container at room temperature.

6458.title: Lemon Yogurt Loaf
instructions: Lemon Loaf: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Butter and line a 23 x 13-cm (9 x 5-inch) loaf pan with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour and baking soda. Set aside.
In another bowl, combine the yogurt with the lemon zest and juice.

In a third bowl, cream the butter and sugar with an electric mixer. Add the eggs, one at a time, and beat until smooth. Add the dry ingredients alternately with the yogurt mixture until smooth. Pour into the prepared pan. Bake for about 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the loaf comes out clean. Let cool completely before removing from the pan.
Topping: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients with a whisk. Serve with the lemon loaf.

6496.title: Chocolate Banana Sauce
instructions: In a blender, purée all the ingredients until smooth. Refrigerate for 1 hour or until completely chilled.
Serve on a scoop of ice cream, pancakes or white cake, or in a smoothie.

6500.title: Mustard Veal Roast with Leeks
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
On a work surface, cut the leeks into rounds about 2.5 cm (1 inch) thick.
Spread the leeks in a large baking dish. Add the cream and 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the butter. Salt and pepper. Cover with a sheet of aluminum foil. Set aside.
Brush the roast with 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the mustard. Salt and pepper.

In an ovenproof non-stick skillet, brown the roast on all sides in the oil. Bake at the same time as the leeks for about 45 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the roast reads 52 °C (125 °F). Uncover the leeks and continue cooking for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, set the roast aside on a plate for about 15 minutes. For pink meat, the internal temperature should reach 55 °C (130 °F).

Meanwhile, in a saucepan, melt the remaining butter (60 ml/1/4 cup). Add the toasted flour and the garlic. Cook, stirring, for about 2 minutes or until the garlic starts to brown. Add the broth and the remaining mustard (15 ml/1 tbsp). Bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Simmer over medium heat for about 10 minutes or until the sauce has thickened.
Slice the roast. Top with the sauce and serve with the leeks and steamed potatoes, if desired.

6555.title: Mario Pelchat's Tourtière
instructions: In a large bowl, place the cubed meat, 2 of the onions and the allspice. Stir to combine. Salt and pepper. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 24 hours.

Meanwhile, in a large pot, place the pheasant, 1 onion, the carrot, celery and Bovril. Salt and pepper. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for about 2 hours or until the pheasant is cooked. Remove the pheasant and take the meat off the bones. Cut into cubes and set aside. Strain the broth and set aside.
On a floured work surface, roll out half the dough at a time to a thickness of 3 mm (1/8 inch).
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a 10-litre (40-cup) roasting pan, line the bottom and sides with one sheet of dough, letting the excess hang over the top.
Add the pheasant to the meat mixture. Spread a third of the meat over the bottom of the roasting pan. Add a third of the potatoes. Salt and pepper. Continue with the remaining ingredients.

Pour in broth up to the level of the filling (you may have some broth left over). Sprinkle with the contents of the onion soup packet. Top with the second crust. Fold the excess dough over to seal in the meat and potatoes.
Make a hole in the centre of the dough. Make a tube with aluminum foil. Insert the tube into the hole to form a chimney.
Bake for 2 hours. Reduce the oven's temperature to 120 °C (250 °F). Continue cooking for 10 hours.

6568.title: Cassoulet with Meatball and Pork Hock Stew
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large skillet, melt the excess fat surrounding the duck confit. Brown the sausages and duck legs. If needed, add a little duck fat or olive oil. Set aside.
In a 2 to 2.5-litre (8 to 10-cup) baking dish, combine and spread the stew, beans, cherry tomatoes and roasted pepper. Salt and pepper. Top with the sausages and duck legs.
Bake for about 30 minutes or until the tomatoes have softened.

6579.title: Raspberry Shirley Temple
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the jam and lemon juice. Strain the mixture through a sieve to remove the small seeds. You'll get a raspberry syrup.
Put a few ice cubes in 4 glasses. Divide the raspberry syrup among them, about 30 ml (2 tbsp) per glass.
Gently pour the soft drink into the glasses. Add two straws to each glass.

6581.title: Maxime Boivin's Lemongrass Tom Collins
instructions: Lemongrass Syrup: In a small saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil and simmer until the sugar has dissolved. Pour into a bowl. Refrigerate until the syrup has completely chilled. The lemongrass syrup keeps for about 3 months in the refrigerator.
Tom Collins: In a tall glass, pour the gin, lemongrass syrup, lemon juice and club soda.
Fill the glass with ice cubes and garnish with a lemon wedge.

6584.title: Kale Coleslaw
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, vinegar, oil and mustard. Salt and pepper.
Add the remaining ingredients. Stir to combine. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to soften the kale. Adjust the seasoning.

6593.title: Dairy-Free, Gluten-Free Mashed Potatoes with Duck Fat
instructions: Place the potatoes and garlic in a pot. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Simmer for about 20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. Drain. Return the sauce to the pot.
Using a potato masher or an electric mixer, mash the potatoes with the duck fat until smooth. Gradually add the broth. Salt and pepper.
Serve with the gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free and egg-free sausage and cranberry turkey roast and the sherry sauce.

6595.title: Roasted Sausages with Warm Beets and Caramelized Apples
instructions: On a work surface, peel 2 apples and cut them into wedges. Place them in a bowl. Dice the third apple and place it in another bowl. Drizzle the apple wedges and dice with the lemon juice.
In a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the apple wedges in the butter. Add 5 ml (1 tsp) of the maple syrup and continue cooking until caramelized. Salt and pepper. Transfer to a plate.
In the same skillet over medium heat, cook the sausages in 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the oil for 12 to 15 minutes or until well browned.

Meanwhile, in another skillet, brown the garlic in the remaining oil. Add the beets and cook for 5 minutes or until hot. Add the remaining maple syrup and the vinegar. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the spinach and cook until just wilted. Salt and pepper.
On a serving platter, arrange the vegetables, apple wedges and sausages. Top with the diced apple.

6608.title: Lemon Raspberry Cake
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Butter a 20 cm (8 inch) square pan and line it with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, cream the butter with the sugar and zest using an electric mixer. Add the egg and beat until the mixture is smooth. Add the dry ingredients alternately with the milk and lemon juice.
In a small bowl, combine the jam and raspberries. Add 125 ml (½ cup) of the cake batter and mix vigorously. Set aside.
Spread the remaining cake batter in the pan. Drop the raspberry batter randomly on top. Using the tip of a small knife, swirl through both batters to create a marbled effect.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool. Unmould and cool completely. Freeze at this stage if desired.

6610.title: Rösti Quiche
instructions: Rösti Crust: Place the rack in the lowest position of the oven. Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Butter a 25 cm (10 inch) quiche pan with a removable bottom.
In a bowl, sprinkle the potatoes with flour. Drizzle with the melted butter and mix well. Salt and pepper. Spread over the bottom and up the sides of the pan. Press evenly.

Bake for about 40 minutes or until the potatoes are cooked in the centre and golden around the edges. Let cool. At this stage, the baked crust can be refrigerated overnight and baked the next morning with the filling.
Filling: In a non-stick skillet, brown shallots in butter. Add the ham and cook for 2 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until just wilted. Set aside.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk and cream. Add the ham mixture and the cheese. Pour into the crust. Place the dish on a baking sheet.
Bake for about 30 minutes or until the filling is firm. Let rest for 10 minutes.

6621.title: Chicken Fricassée with Olives
instructions: In a large non-stick skillet, brown the thighs in half the oil (30 ml/2 tbsp). Salt and pepper. Add the peppers, onion and garlic. Continue cooking until the vegetables are tender. Add the tomatoes, broth, harissa and olives. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for about 30 minutes or until the chicken falls apart with a fork.
In a pot, cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain and oil lightly.
In another skillet, brown the zucchini in the remaining oil (30 ml/2 tbsp). Add the zucchini and pasta to the chicken. Adjust the seasoning.

6635.title: Date and Dark Beer Cake
ingredients: guinness beer or a local stout
guinness beer or a local stout
instructions: Beer Caramel Sauce: In a small saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil, stirring until smooth. Set aside.
Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Butter a 20 cm (8 inch) square glass baking dish. Set aside.
In a saucepan, bring the beer and water to a boil. Remove from the heat. Add the dates, baking soda and vanilla. Stir to combine. Set aside.
In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder.

In another bowl, cream the butter and brown sugar with an electric mixer. Add the egg and pulse until the mixture is well blended. On low speed, add the flour mixture alternately with the date mixture. Spoon the batter into the prepared pan.

Bake for 50 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Using a fork or a skewer, prick the entire surface of the cake. Gently pour half the caramel sauce over it. Let cool. Cut into squares.

When ready to serve, top with the remaining caramel sauce and a scoop of ice cream, if desired. The cake keeps for 3 to 4 days at room temperature. The caramel keeps for one week in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

6645.title: Patrice Demers's Chocolate and St-Henri Coffee Cream Puffs
ingredients: milk chocolate or a mix of dark and milk chocolate
instructions: Craquelin: Using an electric mixer, cream the butter with the brown sugar. With a spatula, add the flour and salt. With your hands, finish mixing the dough until smooth.
Using a rolling pin, roll out the dough between 2 sheets of parchment paper to a thickness of about 2 mm (1/8 inch). Refrigerate for 1 hour.

Using a round cookie cutter about 6 cm (2 1/2 inches) in diameter, or the same size as the cream puffs, cut out the craquelin rounds and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Keep the craquelin rounds in the freezer.
Choux Pastry: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper.
In a saucepan, bring the milk, water, sugar, salt and butter to a boil.
When the butter has melted, remove the saucepan from the heat. Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough is smooth and pulls away easily from the sides.
Return the saucepan to low heat and cook, stirring the dough, for about 2 minutes to dry it out well.
Remove from the heat and let cool for a few minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing vigorously with a wooden spoon, an electric mixer or a food processor until the dough is smooth.
Using a pastry bag fitted with a fairly large plain tip, pipe 6 cm (2 1/2 inch) puffs onto the baking sheet, spacing them apart (see note).

Place a craquelin round on top of each puff. Place in the oven. Immediately lower the oven temperature to 190 °C (375 °F). Cook for 15 minutes. Then lower the oven temperature to 180 °C (350 °F) and continue baking for 15 minutes. If needed, lower the temperature to 165 °C (325 °F) and finish baking for a few more minutes. Let cool.
Chocolate Coffee Chantilly: In a bowl, place the chocolate.
In a saucepan, bring 250 ml (1 cup) of the cream and the corn syrup to a boil. Remove from the heat, add the coffee beans, cover and let infuse for 5 minutes.

Strain through a sieve directly over the chocolate. Let stand for 1 minute. Using an electric mixer, beat the mixture. Gradually pour in the remaining cold cream (500 ml/2 cups). Pour into a container. Cover and let set for 12 hours in the refrigerator.
Whip the chocolate cream until soft peaks form. It's important not to overwhip the cream, as it could become grainy.
Cut the pastries in half horizontally. Place the cream in a pastry bag fitted with a star tip and pipe it onto the bottom halves of the puffs. Close the choux.

6646.title: Razak's Pressure Cooker Barley and Legume Soup (Ash-e Jow)
instructions: Soup: In the pressure cooker over medium-high heat, brown the onion in the oil. Add the garlic and turmeric. Salt and pepper. Continue cooking over medium heat for 2 more minutes, stirring constantly. Add the lentils and barley and coat them well with the onion mixture. Add the broth.
Close the cooker and bring to pressure over high heat. Reduce the heat to medium (or just enough to maintain the pressure) and continue cooking for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a food processor or with a knife, finely chop the spinach, cilantro and parsley. Set aside.
Remove the pressure cooker from the heat and let the pressure drop on its own, or cool the cooker under cold water before opening. Add the spinach, herbs, chickpeas and kidney beans. Stir to combine.

Close the cooker again and bring to pressure over high heat. Reduce the heat to medium (or just enough to maintain the pressure) and continue cooking for 10 minutes. Remove the pressure cooker from the heat and let the pressure drop on its own, or cool the cooker under cold water before opening. Set aside.
Topping: In a small skillet over medium-high heat, brown the garlic in the oil. Transfer to a bowl. Add the mint and mix thoroughly.
Open the pressure cooker and adjust the seasoning. Divide among bowls. If desired, serve with a little yogurt or a lemon wedge and the mint topping.

6649.title: Orange-Braised Endives with Bread Crouton Salad
instructions: Braised Endives: In a large non-stick skillet, bring the orange juice, butter, honey, turmeric and onion to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes. Add the endives and continue cooking until the liquid has completely evaporated and the endives start to brown. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
Bread Crouton Salad: Meanwhile, in another skillet, brown the bread sticks in the butter. Set aside in a large bowl.
In the same skillet, brown the bacon pieces until crisp. Remove them with a slotted spoon. Add them to the bread with the orange and herbs.
Divide the endive and onion ring mixture among 4 plates. Top with the bread salad and a drizzle of the endive cooking juices.

6651.title: Chicken, Prosciutto and Pickled Cauliflower Piadina
instructions: In a skillet over high heat, brown the chicken tenders in the oil. Salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate.
In the same skillet over medium heat, cook the spinach for a few seconds or until just wilted. Over a colander, lightly press the spinach to remove the excess water. Set aside with the chicken.
On a work surface, thinly slice the chicken. On half of the bread, layer the prosciutto, cheese, chicken, spinach and cauliflower. Fold the bread in half.
Place the sandwich in the same skillet over medium heat. Heat until the cheese has melted slightly, turning it once.

6668.title: Homemade Caramel
instructions: In a saucepan, bring the sugar and water to a boil. Cook without stirring until the mixture turns golden brown. Remove from the heat and gradually add the cream and salt. Beware of splattering.
Bring to a boil and simmer until the caramel is smooth. Add the butter and stir until melted. Transfer to a bowl and let cool completely.

6678.title: Citrus Slush
instructions: In a food processor, finely crush the ice.
Add the citrus syrup and water. Blend for about 1 minute or until smooth. Divide the slush among the glasses.

6679.title: Citrus Syrup
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Let cool. Pour into an airtight container and refrigerate for 1 hour or until the syrup is completely cold.
You have enough citrus syrup to make slush for 4.

6684.title: Chocolate Iced Coffee (Shokolad-Gliase)
instructions: In a bowl, place the chocolate.
Pour the hot coffee over the chocolate. Let melt for 2 minutes. With a whisk, stir until the ganache is smooth. Refrigerate for about 1 hour or until the mixture is completely cold (see note).
Just before serving, in a bowl, whip the cream with the sugar until soft peaks form. Set aside.
Add the milk to the cooled coffee mixture. Pour into 2 tall glasses filled with ice cubes. Cover with whipped cream.

6690.title: Chocolate Babka
instructions: Brioche: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook, combine the flour and salt. Make a well. Pour in the milk. Add the sugar and yeast. Mix well. Add the eggs. Knead the dough for 2 minutes. Gradually add the butter and knead the dough for 2 to 3 minutes or until smooth and sticky. Place in an oiled bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise for 1 hour in a warm, humid place.
Chocolate Filling: Butter a 24 x 10 cm (9 ½ x 4 inch) loaf pan with a 1.5-litre (6-cup) capacity. Set aside.
In a bowl, combine the butter, cocoa and corn syrup. Set aside.

Remove the dough from the bowl and place it on a floured work surface. Roll the dough into a 50 x 20-cm (20 X 8-inch) rectangle. Spread the chocolate filling over the entire surface. Sprinkle with the chocolate chips. Roll both ends inward, toward the centre. Place the dough in the pan. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise for 20 to 30 minutes in a warm, humid place or until the dough rises 5 cm (2 inches) above the rim of the pan. The room temperature and the yeast can make the rising time longer.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Egg Wash: In a bowl, combine the egg and water. Using a pastry brush, brush the surface of the dough.
Bake for about 35 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown. Let cool.

6692.title: Chocolate Pots de Crème
instructions: In a bowl, place the chocolate. Set aside.

In a saucepan off the heat, combine the sugar and cornstarch. Add the egg yolks and stir thoroughly with a whisk. Stir in the milk and cream. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring and scraping the bottom of the saucepan, and simmer until the mixture thickens.
Strain and pour over the chocolate. Let melt for 1 minute. Whisk until smooth.
Pour into 6 ramekins of about 125 ml (½ cup) each. Cover with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 2 hours or until the cream is completely cold.
When ready to serve, top with whipped cream, if desired.

6693.title: Chocolate, Marshmallow and Pecan Cake (Mississippi Mud Cake)
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Butter a 43 x 30 cm (17 x 12 inch) baking sheet and line it with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Set aside.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs, brown sugar and cocoa. Drizzle in the butter. Add the dry ingredients alternately with the milk and vinegar. Spread the batter on the baking sheet.
Bake for about 18 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool in the pan.

Candied Pecans: Meanwhile, in a saucepan, bring the brown sugar and water to a boil. Simmer over medium heat for 1 minute. Using a wooden spoon, add the pecans and cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly, until the sugar crystallizes around the nuts. Spread on parchment paper. Allow to cool. Coarsely chop the pecans. Set aside.
Marshmallow: In a saucepan off the heat, sprinkle the gelatin over the water. Let bloom for 5 minutes. Add the sugar and heat over low heat until the gelatin and sugar have dissolved.

Pour into a bowl. Add the corn syrup and vanilla. Beat with an electric mixer until the mixture has the texture of a soft meringue and forms soft peaks. Spread the marshmallow over the cake. Sprinkle with the candied pecans.

Ganache: In a bowl, pour the hot cream over the chocolate. Let melt for 2 minutes. Using a whisk, stir until the ganache is smooth. Let cool for 15 minutes. Using a spoon, drizzle the ganache randomly over the cake. Let cool completely.
This cake keeps for 2 to 3 days at room temperature.

6698.title: Savoury Potato and Bacon Pie
