instructions: Crust: In a food processor, combine the flour and salt. Add the butter and pulse for a few seconds at a time, until the butter is the size of peas. Add the sour cream and mix until the dough just begins to form. Remove the dough from the food processor and form into a disc with your hands.

On a floured work surface, roll out the dough and line a 28-cm (11-inch) in diameter and 2,5-cm (1-inch) deep tart pan with a removable bottom. Fold the excess dough into the crust. Refrigerate for 30 minutes or freeze for 15 minutes.
Filling: On parchment paper, weave the bacon into a square lattice, overlapping the slices (see note). Keep refrigerated.
With the rack in the lowest position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a pot of boiling salted water, cook the potatoes until very tender, about 10 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, in a skillet, brown the onions in the butter. Remove from the heat and set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs and milk. Stir in the cheeses, potatoes and onions. Salt and pepper. Spoon into the crust.

Cover with the bacon lattice, flipping it over with the help of the parchment paper. Remove the parchment paper from the top. Place the dish on a baking sheet. Bake for 40 minutes or until the crust and bacon are well browned. If needed, finish under the broiler for about 3 minutes and, when it comes out of the oven, blot any excess fat on the bacon with paper towels.

6703.title: Beef Burgers with Pepper Confit and Jalapeño Cream Cheese
ingredients: flat hamburger buns or buns of your choice
instructions: Pepper Confit: In a large saucepan over high heat, sauté the peppers, onion and garlic in the oil until the peppers are tender and golden. Add the ketchup and harissa. Salt and pepper. Continue cooking for about 2 minutes. Set aside.
Jalapeño Cream Cheese: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Set aside.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
With your hands or a burger press, shape the meat into 4 large patties.
Grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Salt and pepper. Quickly toast the buns on the grill.
Spread the inside of the buns with the cream cheese mixture. Place a patty on the bottom half of each bun. Top with the pepper confit and lettuce. Close up the sandwiches.

6714.title: Smoked Ribs (2)
instructions: Preheat the electric or charcoal smoker 300°F (150°C). Add the chips and let smoke for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the paprika, salt and pepper.

Rub both sides of the ribs with the dry rub. Place on the smoker rack, bone side down. Close the lid and cook for 45 minutes. Using a brush, generously baste with beer and turn the ribs over. Close the lid and continue cooking for 45 to 60 minutes or until tender, turning and basting them every 15 minutes.
The smoked ribs are delicious served with Alabama white barbecue sauce and potato salad.

6715.title: Smoked Turkey for Sandwiches
instructions: Preheat the electric or charcoal smoker 300°F (150°C). Add the chips and let smoke for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, rub the turkey breast with salt and pepper. Place in the smoker, skin side down. Close the lid and cook for about 1 hour 30 minutes, turning it every 30 minutes, or until a meat thermometer inserted in the meat reads 74 °C (165 °F). Make sure that the temperature remains stable at 300°F (150°C) while cooking. Remove the meat from the smoker. Cover with plastic wrap while the breast is still hot. Refrigerate for 4 hours or overnight.
On a work surface, thinly slice the meat against the grain. Serve in sandwiches with tomato slices, lettuce and mayonnaise.

6716.title: Rum-Flambéed Pineapple
instructions: On a work surface, peel the pineapple and cut lengthwise into 4 long quarters. Remove and discard the pineapple core from the quarters. Set aside.

In a large skillet, heat the syrup with the butter and the vanilla pod and seeds for about 5 minutes or until the mixture caramelizes slightly. Add the pineapple, rounded side down, and brown for 2 minutes. Turn over and add the rum. Flambé. Cover and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes or until the caramel is smooth. Remove the vanilla pod.
Serve hot, drizzled with the caramel. Top with a scoop of ice cream, if desired.

6718.title: Barbecued Mussel Spaghetti
ingredients: thin slices of mild or hot pancetta
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the oil, lemon juice, green onions and garlic. Salt and pepper. Set the sauce aside.
In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta until al dente. Drain and toss with the sauce. Set aside.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the pancetta slices on the barbecue for 2 minutes per side or until crisp. Crumble and add to the pasta mixture.

Place the mussels and tomatoes on the barbecue grill. Close the lid and cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until the mussels open and the tomatoes are charred. Add the mussels and tomatoes to the pasta. Sprinkle with the basil. Adjust the seasoning.

6719.title: Salt and Lemon Rubbed Chicken
instructions: On a work surface, with a chef's knife or kitchen shears, remove the chicken back bone and open it flat.

Sprinkle the salt over the chicken skin. Rub the outside (covered in salt) and the inside of the chicken with the cut side of the lemon for 3 minutes. Let rest for 15 minutes. Oil the chicken and season it with pepper.
Preheat one side of the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Place the chicken flat on the off section of the grill, skin side down. Close the lid.
Cook for about 45 minutes. Turn the chicken and continue cooking for about 35 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the thigh, without touching the bone, reads 180°F (82°C).
Serve with a little piri-piri sauce, if desired.

6720.title: Corn Relish
instructions: Place all the ingredients in a saucepan. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat for 25 minutes, stirring a few times. Pour into airtight containers or hot sterilized jars. Let cool and refrigerate.
Serve with burgers, pork chops or grilled chicken.

6721.title: Red Pepper Relish
instructions: In a food processor, finely chop the peppers and apples.
Transfer the vegetables to a saucepan. Add the lemon and vinegar. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring a few times.
Remove the lemon. Add the sugar and continue cooking for about 10 minutes or until the mixture has thickened. Pour into airtight containers or hot sterilized jars. Let cool and refrigerate.
Serve with burgers, or on grilled fish or meat.

6724.title: Sesame Lamb Chops (Abbacchio a Scottadito)
instructions: Cut the rack into chops between each rib. Rub the chops with the garlic, thyme and pepper. Place in a glass dish. Drizzle with oil and season with salt. Let marinate for about 10 minutes at room temperature.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the chops for 2 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer to the desired doneness. Brush with honey and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Place on a serving platter.
Serve piping hot as an appetizer.

6725.title: Salmon Grilled on a Salt Block
instructions: Salmon: In a small bowl, combine the butter, herbs and lemon zest. Spread this mixture on the flesh side of the salmon. Place the salmon fillets, skin side down, on the salt block.
Place the salt block on the barbecue grill. Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Cook for 12 to 15 minutes or to the desired doneness.
Sauce Vierge: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Serve with the salmon.

6726.title: Grilled Bacon and Herb Cod Roast
instructions: Shallot Vinaigrette: In a small saucepan, brown the shallots in the oil. Deglaze with the vinegar and reduce until almost dry. Set aside. Add the parsley just before serving.
Cod Roast: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Spread the fish with the sun-dried tomato pesto. Salt and pepper. Cut in half lengthwise along the line of the bones. Stack the two pieces of fish to form a roast that is as even as possible.

On a work surface, lay the bacon slices vertically, overlapping them. Place the fish on the bottom third of the bacon slices. Roll up the fish, wrapping it tightly. Insert toothpicks through each slice to hold them in place and keep the pieces together during cooking.
Reduce the barbecue heat to medium. Cook the fish for 4 to 5 minutes per side or until the bacon is well grilled. Turn the fish carefully to keep the fillet whole. Gently transfer to a plate.
Garnish with herbs. Drizzle the fish with the shallot vinaigrette. Cut the roast between the bacon slices to make nice medallions.

6728.title: Barbecued Rabbit Legs with Vegetable Sauce Vierge
ingredients: store-bought sliced pickles or Quick Pickles
instructions: Rabbit: In a glass dish, combine the lemon juice, salt and thyme. Add the rabbit legs and coat them well. Drizzle with olive oil. Cover and refrigerate for 12 hours.
Vegetable Sauce Vierge: In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
Garnish: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Layer two large sheets of aluminum foil. Place the leeks on it. Add the oil and mustard. Season with salt and pepper and mix well. Fold and tightly close the papillote. Set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium.
Drain the rabbit legs. Place on the grill and cook for 10 minutes.

Place the foil packet on the grill next to the meat. Cook for about 15 minutes or until the leeks are tender and the meat is cooked (it will stay firm and won't come off the bone). Set aside. Grill the asparagus for about 5 minutes or until al dente.
Divide the leeks and asparagus among the plates. Top with the rabbit legs and drizzle with the sauce.

6729.title: Grilled Polenta with Rabbit and Cherry Tomatoes
instructions: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Trim both ends of the polenta, then cut it into 12 slices 1 cm (½ inch) thick. Brush both sides of the polenta slices with half the oil. Set aside.
Stack two sheets of aluminum foil. Place the rabbit, tomatoes, olives, shallot and remaining oil (30 ml/2 tbsp) on them. Salt and pepper. Fold and tightly close the papillote.

Place the foil packet on the grill and reduce the barbecue heat to medium. Cook for 15 minutes or until the filling is hot and the tomatoes have burst. Meanwhile, grill the polenta slices for about 3 minutes per side.
Place the polenta slices on a serving plate. Top with the rabbit mixture. Garnish with a basil leaf.

6734.title: Cheese Buns (Pão de Queijo)
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

In a saucepan, bring the water, oil and salt to a boil. Remove from the heat. Add the tapioca flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough forms a smooth ball that pulls away from the sides.
Add the eggs one at a time, stirring well after each addition, until the dough is smooth. Stir in the cheese.
Using an ice cream scoop of about 30 ml (2 tbsp), shape balls of dough and divide them among the baking sheets, spacing them apart.
Bake one sheet at a time for 30 minutes or until the buns are just golden. Eat warm or at room temperature.

6735.title: Caipirinha
instructions: In a fairly wide, not too tall glass, place the lime wedges and sugar. Using a small pestle or the handle of a wooden spoon, crush the lime wedges with the sugar to extract as much juice as possible.
Add the alcohol and mix well. Fill the glass with ice cubes. Stir from time to time to bring up the sugar, which tends to settle at the bottom of the glass.

6736.title: Brazilian Fish Stew (Moqueca)
instructions: Off the heat, spread the onion in a large non-stick skillet. Drizzle with the oil. Spread the tomato slices on top. Salt and pepper. Drizzle with half the wine. Cover and cook over medium heat until the onion is tender and the tomatoes have softened.
Meanwhile, on a work surface, brush the fish with the tomato paste. Salt and pepper.
Place the fish on the vegetables, add the remaining wine and sprinkle with the cilantro. Cover the skillet and simmer for about 10 minutes or until the fish is cooked.
Serve with white rice.

6737.title: Cilantro-Lime Chicken Skewers
instructions: In a mini food processor, purée the cilantro, green onions, garlic, lime zest and juice, and oil until smooth. Pour into a glass dish.

On a work surface, lay two chicken thighs flat. Thread two skewers through them side by side. Repeat with the remaining chicken. Place in the dish and coat well with the marinade. Refrigerate for 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Remove the chicken skewers from the marinade. Salt and pepper. Grill the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes on each side or until cooked through.

6738.title: Grilled Shrimp with Cashew Sauce
instructions: In a saucepan, brown the onion in the oil. Add the garlic, ginger and jalapeño and continue cooking for about 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes, coconut milk and cashews. Simmer for 10 minutes or until the sauce has thickened. Add the cilantro and lime juice, and season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
In a blender, purée the sauce. Set aside half the sauce for serving and the other half for cooking the shrimp.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Thread 3 or 4 shrimp onto each skewer. Salt and pepper.
Grill the shrimp for 2 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Brush the shrimp with sauce while they cook.
Serve the shrimp with the remaining cashew sauce and sprinkle with fresh cilantro.

6741.title: Raspberry Iced Tea
instructions: In a saucepan, bring 500 ml (2 cups) of the water, the sugar, lemon and raspberries to a boil.
Off the heat, add the tea bags and let steep for 5 minutes. Strain through a sieve. Pour into a pitcher with the remaining water and refrigerate until completely cold.
Serve with fresh raspberries and ice cubes.

6745.title: Raspberry, Peach and Passion Fruit Salad
instructions: In a bowl, combine the peaches, passion fruit and sugar. Let stand for about 10 minutes or until the sugar has dissolved. Add the raspberries and stir gently.
Serve on its own, with cookies, or with ice cream.

6746.title: Pre- or Post-Game Triple-Decker Sandwich
instructions: Spread two slices of bread with cream cheese. Arrange the cucumber slices on one slice of bread and cover with the other slice.

Spread the mustard on this second slice. Layer the ham, turkey and lettuce on top. Close the sandwich with the last slice of bread. Press the sandwich to flatten it a little, then cut it into triangles.

6747.title: Soccer Cake
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Butter a 33 x 23 cm (13 x 9 inch) non-stick metal pan with straight sides. Line the pan with a strip of parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and baking soda.

In another bowl, beat the butter and brown sugar well with an electric mixer. Add the cocoa and vanilla. Add the eggs one at a time and keep beating until the mixture is smooth. On low speed, add the dry ingredients alternately with the sour cream. Add the chocolate.
Using a spatula, spread the batter evenly in the pan. Bake for 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean.
Line a rack with parchment paper. Turn the cake out onto the rack. Leave the pan over the cake so it stays moist. Let cool completely at room temperature, about 3 hours.
Frosting: In a small bowl, combine the water and food colouring.
In another bowl, beat the butter with an electric mixer. Add the colouring mixture and the icing sugar and beat until smooth. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the frosting.

Transfer the cake to a serving plate. Using a spatula, cover the top of the cake with 75 ml (1/3 cup) of the frosting. Using a pastry bag fitted with a grass tip (see note) or a fork, cover the cake with small upright strands of the remaining frosting to look like grass.

6748.title: Léo's Macaroni and Cheese
instructions: In a pot of boiling salted water, cook the macaroni until al dente. Drain and toss with a little oil. Place the macaroni in a 33 x 23 cm (13 x 9 inch) ovenproof baking dish.
Place the rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).

In a large skillet, brown the onion and mushrooms in the butter (or duck fat). Add the duck, cream of mushroom soup, milk and Parmesan. Season lightly with salt (careful: the duck and the mushroom soup are already salty), add pepper and mix well. Add the mixture to the dish of macaroni and stir well.
Sprinkle the macaroni with mozzarella. Bake for about 15 minutes. Finish under the broiler for 2 to 3 minutes or until the cheese is golden.

6750.title: Bánh Mì Rolls
ingredients: round sheets rice paper, 9 inches in diameter
instructions: Vietnamese-Style Pork: In a non-stick skillet, brown the meat and green onions in the olive oil and sesame oil, leaving the meat in large pieces. Add the remaining ingredients and stir to combine. Adjust the seasoning. Transfer to a bowl and refrigerate for 30 minutes or until the meat has cooled.
Softening the Rice Paper: In a large shallow dish of hot water, dip one rice paper sheet at a time until it just starts to soften, about 5 seconds. Remove from the water and place on a work surface.

Assembly: Place 45 ml (3 tbsp) of rice vermicelli on it. Add 45 ml (3 tbsp) of the cooled pork. Top with pickled carrots and cucumber. Fold both sides of the rice paper toward the centre. Tightly roll the rice paper around the filling.
Serve immediately or wrap each roll in plastic wrap. Serve with the hoisin mayonnaise.

6751.title: Pickled Carrots
instructions: In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients. Let marinate for 15 minutes. Drain.

6752.title: Hoisin Mayonnaise
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the mayonnaise and hoisin sauce. Refrigerate.

6759.title: Niçoise Salad Stuffed Buns
ingredients: anchovy paste or 1 small anchovy fillet
round buns or square ciabatta rolls, plain or with olives
instructions: Dressing: In a large bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Stuffed Buns: On a work surface, slice the tops off the buns with a bread knife. Scoop out a little of the soft bread inside and keep it for another use. Set aside.

Place the egg in a small saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Continue cooking over low heat for 6 minutes. Add the beans, season with salt and cook for 4 minutes. Drain. Cool the egg and beans under cold water. Peel the egg.
Cut the egg into eight wedges. Place in the bowl with the vinaigrette. Add the remaining ingredients and stir to combine. Salt and pepper.
Stuff the buns with the salad, pressing lightly. Put the tops back on.

6761.title: Trout Cannelloni with Fennel Salad
ingredients: fresh lasagna sheets, about 23 x 15 cm (9 x 6 inches) each
instructions: Tarragon Sauce: In a bowl, whisk together the broth, cream and egg yolks.
In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the flour and cook, whisking constantly, for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in the cream mixture and whisk until the mixture thickens. Simmer for 2 minutes. Add the tarragon. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
Cannelloni: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In a large skillet, soften the leek in the butter. Add the trout and cook for 2 minutes, flaking it with a fork. Add the cream and continue cooking until it has almost completely reduced. Off the heat, add 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the tarragon sauce. Salt and pepper.
In a pot of boiling salted water, cook the pasta for 2 to 4 minutes or until al dente. Immediately plunge them into ice water. Drain and rinse well under cold water.
Spread the pasta sheets on a clean towel and pat them dry. Spread the trout filling over the first half of each pasta sheet. Roll up each sheet to enclose the filling.

Spread a third of the sauce in a baking dish of about 33 x 23 cm (13 x 9 inches). Place the cannelloni in the dish and top with the remaining sauce. Cover with aluminum foil. Bake for about 25 minutes or until hot.
Fennel salad: In a bowl, combine the fennel, oil and lemon juice. Salt and pepper.
Cut the cannelloni in half. Serve two cannelloni halves per plate. Garnish with the fennel salad, lemon zest and fresh herbs.

6771.title: Boucar Diouf's Chicken Yassa
ingredients: skinless and boneless chicken breast halves
instructions: In a bowl, combine the chicken, onion, mustard, spices, lime juice, garlic, chicken concentrate and half the oil (15 ml/1 tbsp). Let marinate for 10 minutes.

In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the chicken and marinade in the remaining oil (15 ml/1 tbsp). Salt and pepper. Pour in the water and simmer for 15 minutes. Add the peppers and continue cooking for 5 minutes or until the chicken is cooked and the peppers are al dente.
Serve with basmati rice.

6772.title: Chocolate Pineapple Trifle
instructions: Chocolate Pudding: In a bowl, place the chocolate and butter. Set aside.
In a saucepan off the heat, whisk together the sugar and cornstarch. Add the egg yolks and mix until smooth. Add the milk.

Bring to a boil over medium-low heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the saucepan, until the mixture thickens. Pour into the bowl and stir until the chocolate and butter have melted. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the cream to keep a skin from forming. Let cool. Refrigerate for 4 hours or until the pudding is completely cold.

Pineapple Compote: On a work surface, cut 6 slices about 5 mm (1/4 inch) thick from one end of the pineapple. Set them aside to make the flowers. Cut the rest into small pieces, discarding the core. You will have about 750 ml (3 cups).

Meanwhile, in a saucepan, combine the sugar and cornstarch. Add the pineapple pieces and bring to a boil. Simmer over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring a few times, or until the compote thickens. Transfer to a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the compote. Let cool. Refrigerate for 2 hours or until completely chilled.
Chocolate Crumble: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.
In a bowl, combine the crumbs and butter. Spread on the baking sheet. Bake for about 12 minutes, stirring halfway through, or until crisp. Let cool completely.
Whipped Cream: In a bowl, whip cream with icing sugar until stiff peaks form.

Assembly: In a tall, straight-sided glass jar of about 2 litres (8 cups), spread half the chocolate pudding. Cover with half the compote, half the cream and half the crumble. Repeat. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

Flowers: Using flower-shaped cookie cutters of different sizes, cut 6 flowers from the reserved pineapple slices. Lay them flat on a work surface. Insert the skewers at the base of the slices, up to the centre.
When ready to serve, stick the flowers in the jar.

6773.title: White Chocolate Cheesecake in a Jar
ingredients: fresh raspberries or other fresh berries
instructions: Crumble: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.
In a bowl, combine the crumbs with the butter. Spread onto the baking sheet. Bake for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring halfway through, or until the crumble is golden. Let cool completely.
Divide the crumble among 6 cups or jars of about 250 ml (1 cup). Set aside.

Filling: In a microwave-safe bowl or a small saucepan, heat 45 ml (3 tbsp) of the cream. Add the chocolate to the hot cream. Let melt for 2 minutes off the heat without stirring. Using a spatula, stir until smooth. Let temper.
In a bowl, whip the remaining cream (75 ml/1/3 cup) with the icing sugar until stiff peaks form.

In a food processor, process the cream cheese until just smooth. Drizzle in the chocolate mixture. Scrape down the sides a few times with a spatula, then gently fold the mixture into the whipped cream.
Spread the mixture over the crumble. Cover with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 1 hour or overnight. The crumble and the cheese filling can be made ahead. When ready to serve, garnish with raspberries.

6775.title: Quinoa Salad with Green Vegetables
instructions: In a large pot of boiling salted water, cook the quinoa for 10 minutes. Add the beans and continue cooking for 2 minutes. Add the zucchini and peas. Cook for 2 minutes or until the quinoa and vegetables are cooked but still slightly crunchy. Drain and cool the quinoa and vegetables under cold water.
In a bowl, combine the lemon juice, oil and basil. Salt and pepper.
Add the quinoa, vegetables and remaining ingredients. Adjust the seasoning.

6778.title: Stir-Fried Noodles with Toasted Ginger
instructions: In a large skillet, soften the peppers and onion in 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the oil. Add the meat and continue cooking over high heat, breaking it up, until well browned. Season with pepper. Add the broccoli and corn. Cover and continue cooking over medium-high heat for about 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until the broccoli is al dente. Transfer to a large bowl.
In the same skillet, brown the ginger and garlic in the remaining oil (30 ml/2 tbsp). Remove from the heat. Add the soy sauce, brown sugar and curry powder and mix well. Stir into the meat mixture.

Meanwhile, in a pot of boiling unsalted water, cook the noodles for about 4 minutes. Drain. Using scissors, cut the noodles here and there to make them shorter and easier to toss with the other ingredients. Add them to the rest of the ingredients in the bowl. Adjust the seasoning.

6781.title: Breaded Chicken Cutlets alla Parmigiana
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a shallow bowl, place the flour. In another shallow bowl, lightly beat the egg. In a third shallow bowl, place the breadcrumbs.
Dredge the cutlets in the flour. Shake to remove any excess. Dip the chicken in the beaten egg and let the excess drip off. Coat with the breadcrumbs.

In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, heat the butter and oil. Brown two cutlets at a time. Add oil during cooking as needed. Drain cutlets on paper towel before placing them on a baking sheet.
Spread the tomato sauce over the cutlets and top with the cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes or until cheese has melted. Serve with a green vegetable and buttered noodles.

6785.title: Duck Leg Confit
instructions: In a bowl, combine the salt, pepper, juniper berries and garlic. In a large 33 x 23 cm (13 x 9 inch) baking dish, place the duck and sprinkle with the salt mixture. Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 24 hours.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).

Drain the duck legs and pat them dry. Return them to the baking dish. Pour in the duck fat. Add the thyme. Cover with aluminum foil. Place the dish on a baking sheet. Bake for 3 hours or until the meat comes away from the bone.

6787.title: Peanut Butter Banana Cheesecake
ingredients: sheets heavy-duty aluminum foil, 45 cm wide
instructions: Graham Crust: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line the bottom of a 20 cm (8 inch) springform pan with parchment paper. Butter the inside of the pan.
In a bowl, combine the cookie crumbs, butter and sugar. Press lightly into the bottom and up the sides of the pan. Bake for 12 minutes. Let cool.
Wrap the outside bottom and sides tightly with aluminum foil. Double the foil. Reduce the oven temperature to 165 °C (325 °F).
Peanut Butter Banana Filling: In a bowl, whisk together the peanut butter and cocoa. Set aside.

In a food processor, combine the cream cheese and brown sugar. Add the eggs and cream. Mix until the filling is just smooth. With a spatula, scrape down the sides a few times. Remove 375 ml (1 1/2 cups) of the mixture, add it to the peanut butter mixture and whisk well. Pour over the crust.
Add the banana to the mixture in the food processor and process until smooth. Gently pour over the peanut butter filling.
Prepare a water bath: Place the cheesecake in a large baking dish and pour hot water into the dish up to one third of the cake pan.

Bake for about 1 hour 20 minutes or until the temperature in the centre of the cake reads 65 °C (150 °F). Remove the cake from the water and aluminum foil. Let cool for about 1 hour. Cover and refrigerate for 6 to 8 hours or until completely chilled.
Run a thin blade between the pan and the cheesecake, then unmold. Sprinkle peanuts around the edge of the cake when ready to serve.

6788.title: Cookie Dough Cheesecake
ingredients: sheets heavy-duty aluminum foil, 45 cm wide
instructions: Cookie Dough: In a bowl, cream the butter with the brown sugar and salt. Stir in the flour. With your hands, shape the dough into about 24 balls of 5 ml (1 tsp) each. Refrigerate while you prepare the crust and filling.
Chocolate Chip Cookie Crust: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line the bottom of a 20 cm (8 inch) springform pan with parchment paper.
In a food processor, finely grind the cookies to get 310 ml (1 1/4 cups) of crumbs.
In a bowl, combine the crumbs and butter. Press loosely into the bottom of the pan. Bake for 10 minutes. Let cool.
Tightly wrap the base and outer sides of the pan with aluminum foil, letting it hang upward. Double the foil. Adjust the oven temperature to 325°F (170°C).

Mini Chocolate Chip Filling: In a food processor, cream the cheese and sugar. Add the sour cream and eggs. Mix until the filling is just smooth. With a spatula, scrape down the sides a few times. Pour over the crust. Scatter the cookie dough balls in the filling. Sprinkle with the chocolate chips.
Prepare a water bath: place the cake in a large baking dish. Pour hot water into the dish to a third of the way up the pan.

Bake for 1 hour or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the cake reads 65 °C (150 °F). Remove the cake from the water and aluminum foil. Let cool for 1 hour. Cover and refrigerate for 6 to 8 hours or until completely chilled.
Run a thin blade between the sides of the pan and the cake to unmould.

6790.title: Red Velvet Cheesecake
instructions: Red Velvet Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter the sides of an 8-inch (20 cm) springform pan and line the bottom with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and baking soda. Set aside.

In another bowl, combine the sugar, oil, food colouring, cocoa, vinegar and vanilla with an electric mixer. Add the egg and beat until the mixture is smooth. At low speed, add the dry ingredients alternately with the buttermilk. Pour into the prepared pan.
Bake for about 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool completely.
Run a thin blade between the pan and the cheesecake, then open the pan hinge. Insert a 10 cm (4-inch) wide strip of parchment paper between the pan and the cheesecake. Close the hinge.
No-Bake Cheese Filling: In a food processor, cream the cheese with 250 ml (1 cup) of the icing sugar. With a spatula, scrape down the sides a few times. Transfer to a large bowl.

In another bowl, whip the cream with the remaining icing sugar (60 ml/1/4 cup) until stiff peaks form. Gently fold into the cheese mixture. Pour over cake. Decorate with the gel food colouring, to taste. Cover and refrigerate for about 4 hours or until completely chilled.

6795.title: Oysters with Orange Mignonette
instructions: Remove the zest from the orange. Place 15 ml (1 tbsp) in a bowl and keep the rest for another use.

Cut the orange into segments. Work over a bowl to catch the juice. Cut the segments into small pieces and set aside. Squeeze the rest of the orange over the bowl to get the juice, and use it in other recipes.
Add the lemon juice and red onion to the bowl with the zest. Set aside.
Shuck the oysters and remove the shellfish from their shells. Place the oysters on a serving platter covered with crushed ice or coarse salt.
Spoon the red onion mixture over each one. Place 2 or 3 pieces of orange on each oyster and finish with pepper, to taste. Serve with Aperol Spritz.

6811.title: Brown Gravy
instructions: With the rack in the lowest position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
On a work surface, cut the celery, carrots and onions into small pieces. Place them in a large roasting pan. Add the chicken wings, garlic and olive oil. Stir to combine.

Roast for 45 minutes, stirring after 20 minutes. Remove from the oven and transfer the contents of the roasting pan to a large pot. Deglaze the roasting pan with 250 ml (1 cup) of the broth to collect the cooking juices from the bottom of the pan. Set aside. Add the Marsala and cognac to the pot. Cook over medium-high heat for 5 minutes or until the alcohol has evaporated.

In a large bowl, whisk together the remaining broth (1.75 litres/7 cups), the toasted flour and the tomato paste. Pour the purée back into the pan. Add the reserved pan juices. Bring to a boil. Simmer over medium heat for about 1 hour or until the sauce has thickened well and reduced by half.
Remove the wings. Take the meat off the bones and keep it for another use, if desired.
Strain the sauce through a sieve, pressing on the vegetables to get as much sauce as possible. Adjust the seasoning. Skim off the fat, if desired. Freeze in containers or resealable bags.
Serve as a sauce with turkey, roast chicken or red meat.

6812.title: Slice-and-Bake Pecan Cookies
instructions: In a bowl, combine the flour and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, cream the butter and icing sugar with an electric mixer. Add the egg and beat until the mixture is smooth. With a wooden spoon or on low speed, add the flour mixture until the dough is smooth. Add the pecans. Divide the dough in half.

On a work surface, spread out a sheet of plastic wrap. Shape one batch of dough into a 20 cm (8 inch) log. Close the plastic wrap and form a long square log. Repeat with the second batch of dough. Freeze on a flat surface for 4 hours or until ready to bake.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
On a work surface, unwrap the log. Cut the dough into slices 5 mm (1/4 inch) thick. Place the cookies on the prepared baking sheets.
Bake one sheet at a time for 12 to 14 minutes or until the cookies are golden. Let cool completely on the baking sheet.
The cookie dough keeps for about 3 months in the freezer. For best results, place the logs wrapped in plastic wrap in a resealable bag.

6815.title: Beets and Green Beans with Bacon
instructions: Place beets in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and simmer gently for about 1 hour or until tender. Drain and place in cold water. Peel and cut each beet into 8 wedges. Place on a large serving platter.

Meanwhile, in a skillet, brown bacon in 15 ml (1 tablespoon) of oil until crisp. Remove the bacon pieces with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Remove the hot fat, keeping only 15 ml (1 tbsp). Add the green beans and heat them through in the fat. Place the beans on the beets. Sprinkle with the bacon.
In a small bowl, combine the balsamic vinegar and the remaining olive oil (15 ml/1 tbsp). Salt and pepper. Drizzle over salad. Adjust the seasoning.

6817.title: Roasted Garlic Butter
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
Slice off the top of the garlic heads. Wrap in aluminum foil and bake for about 30 minutes or until the garlic is tender. Let cool slightly.
Squeeze the garlic cloves into a bowl to extract the pulp. Refrigerate for about 15 minutes or until completely cold.
Add the butter and chives to the bowl of garlic. Salt and pepper.

On a slightly damp work surface, lay 2 sheets of plastic wrap. Spread the butter along one end of each sheet of plastic wrap, horizontally. Roll up into a log about 2.5 cm (1 inch) in diameter. Close the log by twisting both ends of the plastic wrap. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or freeze.
Using a hot knife, slice the butter into rounds of the desired thickness.

6822.title: Mashed Potatoes (2)
instructions: Place the potatoes in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil. Simmer for about 20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. Drain. Return to the pot.
Using a potato masher or an electric mixer, mash the potatoes until smooth. Add the milk. Adjust the seasoning. Serve with a small round of roasted garlic butter and pink peppercorns, if desired.

6828.title: Curried Rabbit Skewers with Lime Cucumbers
ingredients: Lebanese cucumbers, cut into thin ribbons on a mandoline
instructions: In a small saucepan over medium heat, brown the garlic in 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the oil. Add the curry powder and cook for 1 minute. Off the heat, add the honey and lemon juice. Pour into a bowl. Add the yogurt and mix well. Set aside half the yogurt sauce for serving.
In a bowl, combine the rabbit cubes, salt and remaining yogurt sauce. Coat them well with the mixture. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 12 hours or overnight.
Preheat the barbecue to medium. Oil the grate.
Thread the meat onto the skewers. Grill the skewers for about 5 minutes per side or until the rabbit is no longer pink.
On a plate, gently toss the cucumbers with the remaining oil (15 ml/1 tbsp), the lime juice and the basil. Salt and pepper.
Divide the cucumber ribbons among 4 plates, twisting them. Place 3 rabbit skewers on each plate and serve with the reserved yogurt sauce.

6860.title: Tomato-Braised Vegetables
instructions: In a saucepan over high heat, brown the eggplant in the oil. Using a slotted spoon, remove the eggplant and drain on paper towels. Set aside.
In the same saucepan, soften the pepper, onion and garlic in the hot oil. Add oil, if needed.
Add the tomatoes, beans and the reserved eggplant. Cover and simmer over medium-low heat, stirring a few times, for about 15 minutes or until the vegetables are tender. Salt and pepper.

6866.title: Fruity Sparkling Cider
instructions: In a blender, purée the mango and orange juice until smooth. Strain through a sieve.
Place about 30 ml (2 tbsp) of mango purée in each of 8 champagne flutes. Slowly pour in the cider. Stir to combine. Serve immediately.

6867.title: Veggie Hot Dogs
instructions: Carrot Salad: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Salt and pepper. Let marinate for about 10 minutes. Drain the salad.
Hot Dogs: In a skillet over medium heat, brown the hot dogs on all sides in 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the oil. Set aside on a plate.
In the same skillet, toast the buns on both sides in the remaining oil. Add broth, if needed.
Spread the buns with baba ghanoush and add a hot dog. Top with the tomato, carrot salad and leaf lettuce.

6873.title: Eggplant Tartine with Sun-Dried Tomato Mâche Salad
instructions: Sandwiches: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Place the bread on a baking sheet. Brush one side of the bread slices with 45 ml (3 tbsp) of the oil. Salt and pepper. Bake for about 10 minutes or until the bread is lightly toasted. Set aside.
Meanwhile, in a well-oiled ridged grill pan over medium heat, grill the eggplant. Set aside on a plate.
In a bowl, combine the remaining oil (15 ml/1 tbsp) and the sun-dried tomato pesto. Using a brush, brush the grilled eggplant with the oil mixture. Salt and pepper.
Generously spread the bread slices with ricotta. Place them on the plates. Top with a slice of grilled eggplant and a slice of tomato. Salt and pepper.
Salad: In a bowl, whisk together the oil, vinegar, sun-dried tomato pesto and garlic. Add the mâche and toss gently.
Top the warm sandwiches with the salad. Serve immediately.

6878.title: Saffron Seafood Casserole
instructions: Casserole: In a large skillet or saucepan, lightly brown the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the white wine and simmer for about 2 minutes. Add the broth and bring to a boil.
Add the clams and saffron. Cover and simmer for about 5 minutes or until the clams open.
Add the mussels, langoustines, asparagus, tomatoes and parsley. Cover and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes or until the mussels open. Discard any that remain closed. Salt and pepper.
If desired, drain the seafood and keep it warm. Off the heat, add the butter to the broth, whisking constantly until smooth and creamy. Return the seafood to the sauce and mix well.
Olive Oil Croutons: Meanwhile, in a skillet, brown the bread on both sides with the garlic clove in the oil until it has absorbed all the oil. Salt and pepper.
Divide the seafood casserole among shallow bowls. Serve with the olive oil croutons.

6879.title: Hazelnut, Orange and Chocolate Cake (Dobos Torte)
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter two 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans and line them with parchment paper.
In a bowl, cream the butter, sugar, extract and remaining egg yolk until frothy.

In another bowl, beat the eggs, orange zest and sugar until the mixture falls in a ribbon, about 10 minutes. Using a spatula or a whisk, gently fold in the oil alternately with the dry ingredients and the milk. Spoon the batter into the prepared pans.
Bake for about 35 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Allow to cool. Cut the cakes in half horizontally to make 4 layers.

Chocolate Buttercream: In a bowl, cream the butter with the icing sugar and cocoa. Add the cream, 15 ml (1 tbsp) at a time, until the mixture is smooth and fluffy. Drizzle in the chocolate and stir it in.

Assembly: Place one cake layer on a serving plate. Spread about 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the buttercream over the top of the layer. Repeat with the remaining cake layers and buttercream. Cover the entire cake with the remaining buttercream. Garnish the edges with the chopped hazelnuts.

6884.title: Wheat Berry Stew with Mushrooms, Roasted Vegetables and Toasted Hazelnuts
ingredients: carrots of various colours, leaves removed and peeled
instructions: Wheat Berries: Place the soft wheat berries in a large bowl. Cover with cold water and let soak for 12 hours or overnight at room temperature. Add water as needed so the grains are always well covered. Rinse and drain.

In a large saucepan over medium-high heat, brown the garlic in the oil. Add the onions and mushrooms. Continue cooking, stirring often, until well caramelized. Salt and pepper. Deglaze with the white wine and reduce until almost dry. Add the water and wheat berries. Cover and cook for 1 hour. Remove the lid and continue cooking for about 30 minutes or until the liquid has been completely absorbed and the wheat is cooked but still slightly firm to the bite. Adjust the seasoning.
Vegetables: Meanwhile, place the rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to 210 °C (425 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

On the baking sheet, coat the carrots and squash with 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the oil. Salt and pepper. Cover with a sheet of aluminum foil. Bake for 30 minutes. Remove the foil, stir the vegetables and continue cooking for about 15 minutes or until well roasted. Keep warm.
In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the oyster mushrooms in the remaining oil (30 ml/2 tbsp). Add shallot and cook for about 1 minute. Salt and pepper.
Divide the wheat berry stew among 4 plates. Add the roasted vegetables and oyster mushrooms. Garnish with parsley and toasted hazelnuts.

6901.title: Cauliflower, Ham and Egg Gratin with Bread Lace
ingredients: thin slices of stale white bread
instructions: Gratin: In a large saucepan, soften the cauliflower and leek in the butter. Cover and continue cooking over medium heat for about 5 minutes or until the cauliflower is al dente, without letting it brown. Salt and pepper.
Off the heat, add the ham and mix. Spoon into a 13 x 9-inch (33 x 23 cm) baking dish. Gently arrange the egg wedges on top. Set aside.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

Béchamel: In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Sprinkle with the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the milk and bring to a boil, stirring with a whisk. Simmer over medium heat for about 2 minutes or until the sauce thickens. Remove from the heat and stir in the cheese. Salt and pepper. Spread the béchamel over the gratin.
Topping: Using a brush, brush the bread slices with oil.
Cover the gratin with the bread slices. Bake for about 20 minutes or until the bread is golden and the gratin is bubbling.

6902.title: Pissaladière
instructions: In a large skillet over medium heat, brown the onions and garlic in the oil, stirring often, until very well cooked. Add the capers and anchovy paste. Continue cooking for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F (225°C).

Sprinkle the cornmeal over a 43 x 30 cm (17 x 12 inch) baking sheet. Place the dough on it and spread it out well with your fingers until it covers the entire sheet. Lightly oil the dough. Let bloom for 10 minutes.
Spread the onion mixture over the dough, then the olives. Bake for about 25 minutes or until the crust is golden and crisp. As soon as it comes out of the oven, sprinkle with parsley.

6903.title: White Fish with Ginger Broth and Swiss Chard
instructions: Separate the Swiss chard stems from the leaves. Thinly slice the stems. Coarsely chop the leaves to get about 2 litres (8 cups). Set aside.

In a wok or a large, deep skillet over medium heat, soften the chard stems, shallot, garlic and ginger in the oil. Add the broth, soy sauce, fish sauce, lime juice and sambal oelek. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the chard leaves to the broth. Stir. Cover and cook for a few seconds, until just wilted.

Season the fish very lightly with salt, as the broth is already salty. Place the fish on the chard and cover. Continue cooking for about 3 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fillets, until the fish is cooked, basting it with broth halfway through. Season with pepper.
Divide the chard leaves and stems among shallow bowls. Place the fish on top. Pour the broth into the bottom of the bowls. Drizzle the fish with olive oil, if desired.

6942.title: Cilantro Sauce
instructions: In a food processor, purée the cilantro, green onions, garlic, chili pepper, ginger and cumin.
Transfer to a bowl. Add the oil, water, lime juice and tomato. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with lentil and squash curry or butter chicken.

6968.title: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone mats.
In a bowl, combine the oats, flour, raisins, baking soda, cinnamon and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, cream the butter with the brown sugar and honey using an electric mixer (beat for 2 to 3 minutes or until fluffy and pale). Add the egg and beat until the mixture is smooth. At low speed or with a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients.
Using an ice cream scoop of about 60 ml (1/4 cup), shape balls of dough and place 6 balls on each baking sheet.
Bake one sheet at a time for about 15 minutes or until the cookies are lightly golden. Let cool on a wire rack.

6986.title: Petit Beurre Cookies
instructions: In a bowl, combine the flour and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, cream the butter, sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer. Add the egg and beat until smooth. At low speed or with a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients. Shape the dough into 2 discs. Cover in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 1 hour.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

On a lightly floured work surface, roll out one disk of dough at a time to a thickness of about 5 mm (1/4 inch). Cut out cookies using cookie cutters. Prick the surface of the cookies a few times. Reuse the scraps. Scatter on the baking sheets.
Bake, one sheet at a time, for about 12 minutes or until lightly browned. Allow to cool.

6987.title: Chocolate-Covered Petit Beurre Cookies
instructions: On a baking sheet, divide the tempered chocolate among 6 chocolate bar moulds. Refrigerate for 30 minutes or until the chocolate has completely set.
Gently unmould the chocolate bars and place them on the cookies while they are still slightly warm (the chocolate will set onto the cookie). Let cool completely at room temperature, about 1 hour.

6988.title: Pan-Fried Green Vegetables with Red Wine
instructions: Red Wine Reduction: In a saucepan over medium heat, bring all the ingredients to a boil. Simmer for about 10 minutes or until the wine is syrupy. Strain the reduction through a sieve. Set aside.

Croutons: Meanwhile, in a large skillet over medium heat, lightly brown the garlic in the oil. Add the bread and continue cooking, stirring often, until the bread starts to brown and crisp up. Set aside on paper towel.

Vegetables: In the same skillet over medium-high heat, brown the bacon with the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the beans and broccoli and brown them. Add the kale and continue cooking for about 5 minutes or until it starts to soften. Add oil, if needed. Season lightly with salt and pepper (the reduction already contains pepper).
On a large serving platter, spread the vegetables, top with the croutons and drizzle with the red wine reduction.
Delicious with pork and mushroom stuffed turkey, grilled red meat or sausages.

7011.title: Sauerkraut Soup
instructions: In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, brown the bacon, onion and garlic in the oil. Transfer to the slow cooker. Add the remaining ingredients and stir to blend. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on Low for 6 hours. It can be maintained on Warm for up to 4 hours.
Serve with a slice of country bread or sliced grilled sausages, if desired.

7013.title: Spiced Pineapple Cocktail
instructions: Spiced Syrup: In a small pot, bring all of the ingredients to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat. Strain and let cool.

Cocktail: Cut the top off the pineapple. With a knife, cut around the inside of the pineapple, leaving about 1 cm (1/2 inch) of flesh, without piercing the skin. With a spoon, gradually scoop out the flesh to hollow the pineapple. Cut the flesh into pieces and discard the core.
In a blender, purée the pineapple pieces and water until smooth. Strain through a sieve. You will get about 250 ml (1 cup) of pineapple juice.
In a shaker, vigorously shake the pineapple juice, tequila, lime juice, spiced syrup and ice cubes. Pour into the hollowed-out pineapple. Serve with two straws and ice cubes.

7018.title: Queso Dip
instructions: In a saucepan, soften the onion, garlic and pepper in the oil. Add the cheese and cream. Stir until the cheese has melted and the sauce is smooth. Remove from the heat.
Add the tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve warm or cold with corn chips. The dip keeps for 2 to 3 days in the refrigerator.

7023.title: Crème Caramel
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
On a work surface, set out 6 ramekins of 125 ml (1/2 cup) each.
Caramel: In a saucepan over medium-high heat, heat the sugar and water without stirring until an amber caramel forms. Divide the caramel among the ramekins. Allow to cool.
Custard: In a saucepan, bring the milk, sugar and vanilla to a boil. Stir until the sugar has dissolved.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, beat the eggs. Gradually whisk in the warm milk mixture. Pour into the ramekins.

Prepare a water bath: place a cloth in the bottom of a large baking dish. Place the ramekins in the dish and fill the dish with hot water until it reaches halfway up the ramekins. Cover loosely with a sheet of aluminum foil, without sealing it. Bake for about 30 minutes or until the edges of the custard are set but the centre is still slightly jiggly.
Remove the ramekins from the baking dish. Let the custards cool slightly, preferably on a rack, covered with a clean towel. Cover each ramekin with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 8 hours.
When ready to serve, run a knife blade all around the ramekins. Turn out the custards and serve cold.

7026.title: Fish and Vegetables in Court-Bouillon
ingredients: skinless brook trout or Arctic char fillet
instructions: On a work surface, cut all the vegetables into slices about 5 mm (1/4 inch) thick.

Spread the vegetables in the bottom of a large non-stick skillet. Add the broth and wine. Salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer over medium-high heat for about 5 minutes or until al dente.

Season the fish with salt and pepper. Place them on the vegetables. Bring to a boil. Cover and continue cooking for about 3 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fillets, or until the fish is cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Serve the fish with the vegetables and broth in shallow bowls. Drizzle with olive oil and garnish with a few fennel fronds, if desired.

7028.title: Chili con Carne
instructions: In a large pot over medium-high heat, brown the meat in the oil, a third at a time. Salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate.

Add the bacon and brown it in the hot fat. Add the onions, garlic and chili pepper. Add oil, if needed. Continue cooking until the vegetables are tender. Return the meat to the pot. Sprinkle with the chili seasoning, corn flour and cumin. Stir to coat the meat well and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring. Deglaze with the beer. Add the broth and bring to a boil.
Simmer, uncovered, over low heat for about 3 hours or until the meat falls apart with a fork and the sauce has thickened, stirring a few times during cooking.
Serve with corn muffins, if desired.

7029.title: Corn Muffins
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line 8 muffin cups with paper or silicone liners.
In a bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cayenne pepper. Set aside.
In another bowl, whisk together the oil, brown sugar and egg. Add the dry ingredients alternately with the buttermilk. Stir in the corn kernels.
With a 75 ml (1/3 cup) ice cream scoop, spoon batter into cups.
Bake for about 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

7030.title: Sabayon with Spiced Sugar Caramelized Fruit
instructions: Fruit: Place the rack in the top position of the oven. Preheat the oven's broiler. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
In a shallow dish, combine the sugar, cayenne pepper and ginger. Set aside 45 ml (3 tbsp) of the spiced sugar for the sabayon.
Press one side of the fruit slices into the remaining sugar. Place on the baking sheet, sugared side up.
Bake for 3 to 5 minutes or until the fruit is caramelized. Set aside.

Sabayon: In the top of a double boiler, off the heat, whisk the egg yolks, clementine juice, wine and reserved spiced sugar. Set over the simmering water and whisk constantly for 5 to 7 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Arrange the caramelized fruit and raspberries in one or two large shallow dishes and top with the sabayon. Lightly caramelize with a kitchen torch, if desired. Serve immediately.

7042.title: Chicken and Black Bean Enchiladas
instructions: Sauce: In a bowl, whisk together the broth and corn flour. Set aside.

In a small saucepan over medium heat, soften the green onions and garlic with the spices in the oil. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Deglaze with the vinegar. Whisk in the broth mixture. Bring to a boil and simmer over low heat for about 15 minutes, stirring a few times, or until the sauce thickens. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
Enchiladas: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large non-stick skillet over high heat, brown the chicken in the oil. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes. Salt and pepper.

Meanwhile, in a bowl, mash half the black beans with a fork or a potato masher. Stir the whole and mashed black beans into the chicken. Add the broth and bring to a boil. Simmer over medium-high heat for 12 to 15 minutes, or until the chicken and beans have absorbed all the broth. Remove from the heat. Add the tomato and cilantro. Adjust the seasoning.
Spread 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the sauce in a 28 x 20 cm (11 x 8 inch) baking dish.

On a work surface, lay the tortillas flat. Place about 150 ml (2/3 cup) of the chicken mixture in the centre of each one, then roll up. Place the rolls in the baking dish, seam side down. Pour the remaining sauce over all the rolls. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for about 25 minutes or until the enchiladas are hot and the cheese has melted. Let cool for 10 minutes before serving.

7043.title: Roasted Vegetable Salsa
instructions: With the rack in the highest third position, preheat the oven's broiler. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
On the baking sheet, place the tomatoes, green onions and chili pepper. Season with salt and pepper. Place the tomatoes and chili pepper cut side down on the baking sheet.
Bake for about 10 minutes or until the vegetables are blackened. Let cool.

In a food processor, finely chop the green onions and chili pepper. Add the tomatoes and pulse just enough to chop them. Transfer to a bowl. Add the cilantro, lime juice and cumin. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve warm or cold with corn chips. The salsa keeps for about 1 week in the refrigerator.

7048.title: Santa Fe Salad
instructions: Dressing: In a large bowl, whisk together all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Salad: In a small bowl, combine the sour cream, cheese and chili powder. Set aside.

In the bottom of a clear bowl about 20 cm (8 inches) in diameter with a 3-litre (12-cup) capacity, spread the lettuce, then the tomatoes. Drizzle with a third of the dressing. Continue with the onion and beans. Drizzle with a third of the dressing. Add the sour cream mixture, corn and avocados. Drizzle with the remaining dressing. Top with the corn chips. Let rest for 15 minutes before serving.

7050.title: Crunchy Cereal Ice Cream Squares
instructions: Line a 20 cm (8 inch) square pan with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.
Press the ice cream into the bottom of the pan in a thin, even layer. Freeze for 4 hours or until the ice cream is firm.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.
In a bowl, combine the cereal, brown sugar and graham cracker crumbs. Add the butter and mix to coat the dry ingredients. Spread on the baking sheet.
Bake for about 15 minutes or until golden, stirring halfway through. Allow to cool.
Line another 20 cm (8 inch) square pan with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides. Press half the crunchy mixture into the bottom of the pan.
Unmould the frozen ice cream square and place it on the crunchy layer. Cover with the remaining crunchy mixture and press down. Cover with plastic wrap and freeze for 2 hours.
Cut into 16 squares.

7086.title: Onion and Fig Compote
instructions: In a small saucepan over medium heat, soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the remaining ingredients and continue cooking, stirring a few times, for about 20 minutes or until the liquid has evaporated and the mixture is jammy.
Transfer to a bowl and let cool slightly. Cover and refrigerate for 6 hours.
Spread on a biscotti cracker. Top with a slice of prosciutto and a slice of cheese.

7087.title: Smoked Meat Canapés
instructions: In a bowl, mix the butter and mustard until smooth.
Warm the meat in the microwave for a few seconds. Cut the meat into strips. Set aside.
Spread each cracker with the mustard butter. Top with strips of smoked meat and garnish with pickle slices.

7088.title: Herb Roast Chicken with Fried Shallot Salad
instructions: Chicken: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

Place the chicken on a plate. Sprinkle the salt over the skin and rub it in, especially on the breasts and thighs. Let marinate for 15 minutes. Brush with the oil. In a small bowl, combine the green onions and herbs. Spread over the chicken. Place in a Dutch oven or baking dish. Season with pepper.
Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the thigh, without touching the bone, reads 82 °C (180 °F).

Sauce: Meanwhile, in a saucepan over high heat, melt the butter. Add the flour and mix well until the mixture turns amber. Add the veal stock and bring to a boil, whisking. Add the garlic, honey and vinegar. Simmer for about 30 minutes or until the sauce has thickened. Salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Salad: In a small saucepan, heat about 2.5 cm (1 inch) of canola oil. Line a plate with paper towels. Set aside.
Dredge the shallots in the flour and shake to remove any excess. Fry the shallots until crisp and lightly golden brown. Drain on the paper towels. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the oil, vinegar, mustard, capers and green onion. Add the lettuce and fried shallots. Stir to blend gently.
Assembly: Skim the fat from the chicken cooking juices and add them to the sauce. Serve the chicken with the sauce and salad.

7092.title: Blueberry, Pineapple and Coconut Crisp
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a bowl, combine the coconut, 55 g (1/4 cup) of the sugar and the flour. Add the butter and stir until the mixture is just moistened. Set the crisp topping aside.
In a 20 cm (8 inch) square pan with a capacity of about 2 litres (8 cups), combine the remaining sugar (55 g/1/4 cup) and the cornstarch. Stir in the fruit.
Spread the fruit evenly over the bottom of the pan. Cover with the topping. Bake for about 45 minutes or until the topping is golden brown (allow 1 hour for frozen blueberries).
Serve warm or cold. Serve with vanilla ice cream, if desired.

7095.title: Ginger-Lemongrass Ground Pork Skewers
ingredients: disposable wooden chopsticks or flat wooden skewers
instructions: Ginger-Lemongrass Sauce: In a saucepan over medium heat, soften the ginger, lemongrass, shallots and garlic in the oil for 3 minutes. Add the brown sugar and continue cooking for 1 minute. Add the fish sauce, sambal oelek and cashews. Bring to a boil and simmer for 2 minutes. Set aside.
Skewers: In a bowl, combine the meat, egg, breadcrumbs, baking powder and 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the ginger-lemongrass sauce until the mixture is sticky.
With a 1/4-cup (60 ml) ice cream scoop or measuring cup, form 12 meatballs. With lightly oiled hands, press the meat into a sausage shape around each skewer. Set aside.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the skewers for about 4 minutes per side or until the meat is well browned on all sides.
Serve the skewers with the remaining sauce on the side. Serve with the carrot juice couscous and the corn and herb coleslaw.

7100.title: Sausage and Citrus Skewers
ingredients: italian sausages, mild or spicy, cut into 12 slices, each about 1-inch long
mini bell peppers in assorted colours
instructions: Skewers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium-high. Oil the grate.
On a work surface, thread 4 sausage pieces onto 2 skewers, alternating with 4 mini peppers, 4 citrus wedges and 2 sage sprigs. Continue with the remaining ingredients. Brush the kebabs with oil.
Grill the skewers for 8 to 10 minutes per side or until the sausages are cooked through.
Dressing: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Using a brush, brush the skewers with the dressing once they are cooked.
Serve with a green, couscous or tomato salad. Drizzle the sausages with the juice of the grilled citrus.

7101.title: Spinach and Grilled Chicken Salad with Pomegranate and Pine Nuts
instructions: Chicken: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine all the ingredients.
Grill the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through. On a work surface, thinly slice the chicken. Keep warm.
Salad: In a large bowl, combine the lemon juice, oil and honey. Salt and pepper.
Add the remaining ingredients and the cooked chicken. Coat well with the dressing. Adjust the seasoning. Serve immediately.

7102.title: Grilled Beef Sirloin Roast
instructions: Roast Beef: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Place the roast on a plate. In a coffee grinder or a mortar, grind the salt and spices to a fine powder. Coat the roast with the spiced salt and brush with oil.

Reduce the barbecue heat to medium-high. Place the roast on the grill and brown it on all sides. Close the lid. Cook for about 25 minutes, turning it a few times, or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the roast reads 48 °C (118 °F) for rare. Place on a plate, cover with aluminum foil and let rest for about 10 minutes.

Sauce: Meanwhile, in a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the onion in the butter. Sprinkle with the flour, mix well and continue cooking for about 1 minute. Add the cream, broth, Worcestershire sauce and pepper. Season with salt. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Simmer for about 2 minutes.
Remove the string. Thinly slice the roast and serve with the sauce. Delicious with the beer-steamed potato and Brussels sprout foil packet.

7103.title: Classic Surf and Turf
instructions: Roast Beef: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). In a large ovenproof skillet over high heat, brown the roast on all sides in the oil. Salt and pepper.
Roast for about 25 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the roast reads 48 °C (118 °F) for rare. Set aside.
Béarnaise Sauce: In a bowl, melt the butter with the shallot and pepper in the microwave. Let steep for 5 minutes. Strain through a sieve. Set aside.
In the top of a double boiler, off the heat, whisk the egg yolks, water and vinegar. Set over the simmering water and whisk constantly until thick and foamy.

Remove the bowl from the double boiler. Drizzle in the melted butter in a thin stream, whisking constantly. Season with salt. Set aside at room temperature. When ready to serve, return the sauce to the double boiler for a few seconds, whisking just to warm it, and add the tarragon.

Garnish: In a large non-stick skillet over high heat, bring the broth, potatoes and pearl onions to a boil. Cover and simmer for about 10 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. Add the asparagus and green onions. Continue cooking for about 2 minutes or until al dente. Add the lobster claws and pieces. Continue cooking for about 1 minute or until hot. Salt and pepper.

Cut the roast into thin slices. Drain and divide the lobster garnish among the plates. Top with the béarnaise sauce. Place 2 or 3 slices of filet mignon on each plate and finish with the lobster claws.

7104.title: Beer-Steamed Potato and Brussels Sprout Foil Packet
instructions: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium.

Layer two large sheets of aluminum foil. Place them in a shallow dish (see note). In the centre, place the potatoes, Brussels sprouts, onions, garlic and butter. Drizzle with the beer. Salt and pepper. Close and tightly seal the papillote.
Place the foil packet on the grill. Close the lid and cook for 20 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.
Remove from the grill. Open the foil packet and gently toss the bean mixture.

7105.title: Salsa Verde Pork Chops with Cherry Tomato Stuffed Cucumbers
ingredients: soft goat cheese or cream cheese
instructions: Pork Chops: In a large dish, combine the pork chops with half the salsa verde (60 ml/¼ cup) and the olive oil. Salt and pepper. Cover and let marinate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium-high. Oil the grate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Grill the meat for about 5 minutes per side or until the desired doneness. Let rest for 5 minutes.

Stuffed Cucumbers: Meanwhile, on a work surface, cut a thin slice lengthwise from each side of the cucumbers so they stand steady when laid flat. Cut the cucumbers in half lengthwise. Using a small spoon, scoop out the seeds. Pat the inside of the cucumbers dry with paper towels.

Spread the cheese in the cucumber cavities. In a bowl, combine the tomatoes, shallot and oil. Salt and pepper. Spoon the tomato mixture into the cucumbers. Garnish with pieces of pancetta and thyme leaves.
Serve the cherry tomato stuffed cucumbers with the pork chops and the remaining salsa verde.

7106.title: Glazed Veal Patties with Asian Slaw
instructions: Coleslaw: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Veal: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium-high. Oil the grate.

In a bowl, mix all the ingredients well with your hands. Shape into 12 small patties. Lightly brush with olive oil. Grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side or until the meat is cooked through. Keep warm.

Sauce: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the hoisin sauce, water and sambal oelek. Using a brush, glaze the patties with the sauce once they are cooked. Sprinkle them with sesame seeds. Serve with the slaw and top with the remaining sauce.

7109.title: Olive and Preserved Lemon Stuffed Pork Tenderloins
instructions: Preserved Lemon Mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

Pork Tenderloin: On a work surface, butterfly the pork tenderloins. To do this, slice each tenderloin in half through its thickness without cutting all the way through, then open them like a book. Salt and pepper. Spread the olives, pistachios, chives and lemon over them. Close.

Slide pieces of string under the tenderloins, letting them hang over each side. Lay the thyme sprigs on top of the tenderloins. Tie and cut any excess string. Oil the meat with 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the oil. Salt and pepper.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine the fennel and the remaining oil (30 ml/2 tbsp). Salt and pepper. Reduce the heat to medium. Grill the fennel on each side until tender. Set aside.
Grill the pork tenderloins for about 15 minutes, turning them regularly, or until pink in the centre. Set aside on a plate. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Remove the string. Slice the pork tenderloins. Serve with the preserved lemon mayonnaise and grilled fennel.

7119.title: Cola Ribs
instructions: Ribs: In a small bowl, combine all the dry ingredients. Set the dry rub aside.

On a work surface, using paper towels, peel away the white membrane from the back of the ribs. Place the ribs on a plate and rub the dry rub over both sides of the meat. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour or overnight.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (170°C).

Wrap the ribs in a large sheet of aluminum foil lined with a sheet of parchment paper, no more than two racks at a time. The parchment paper keeps the bones from piercing the foil. Seal the jar. Place on a baking sheet. Bake for about 2 hours, or until the meat is tender.

Cola Sauce: Meanwhile, in a saucepan over high heat, soften the onion, garlic and chili powder in the butter for 2 minutes. Add the remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil and simmer over low heat for 40 minutes or until the sauce has reduced by half. Salt and pepper.
In a blender, purée the sauce until smooth.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium. Oil the grate.
Unwrap and drain the ribs. Grill for about 8 minutes, brushing regularly with half the sauce and turning them halfway through, or until well caramelized. Serve with the remaining sauce.

7123.title: Tonic Cocktail
instructions: In a large pitcher, combine the orange juice, gin, cane syrup and 6 rosemary sprigs, lightly crushed. Marinate for 12 to 24 hours in the refrigerator.
Strain the mixture and discard the steeped rosemary sprigs.
When ready to serve, pour 90 ml (3 oz) of the mixture and 45 ml (1 ½ oz) of tonic water into each glass. Garnish with a rosemary sprig and fill the glass with ice cubes.

7124.title: Passion Cocktail
instructions: In a large pitcher, combine the passion fruit syrup, vodka and lime juice. Set aside in the refrigerator.
When ready to serve, pour 75 ml (2 ½ oz) of the mixture and 45 ml (1 ½ oz) of tonic water into each glass. Garnish with 2 lime wedges and fill the glass with ice cubes.

7130.title: Grilled Pineapple with Coconut Milk
instructions: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

Pour the coconut milk into a bowl. On a plate, combine the brown sugar and cinnamon. Dip a pineapple slice in the coconut milk, allow the excess to drip off, and press into the brown sugar and cinnamon mixture. Repeat with the remaining pineapple slices.
Grill the slices for 4 or 5 minutes on each side, or until the sugar has caramelized. Serve the pineapple slices hot or warm. Sprinkle with shredded coconut if desired. Serve with ice cream.

7131.title: Chestnut Raspberry Tartlets
instructions: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high.

On a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, place the muffin halves, cut side up. Spread the chestnut spread on each muffin half and drizzle with maple syrup. Be careful not to spill any on the baking sheet. Sprinkle with the pecans.

Place the baking sheet on the grill and close the lid. Cook for 5 to 8 minutes or until the muffins are very crisp and the topping is hot. Keep a close eye on the tartlets as they cook. Remove from the grill.
Top with raspberries. Dust with icing sugar. Serve with ice cream, if desired.

7137.title: Fish Stock
instructions: Rinse the fish trimmings under cold water. Drain.

In a saucepan over medium heat, soften the leek, onion, celery and garlic with the fish trimmings, bay leaf and thyme in the butter for 5 minutes. Generously season with salt. Pour in the water and lemon juice. Bring to a boil and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, skimming a few times during cooking.
Line a sieve with two layers of cheesecloth. Strain the broth. The stock is ready to use, refrigerate or freeze. Compost the trimmings and aromatics.

7147.title: Lychee Raspberry Cake
instructions: Fruit Purées: Drain the lychees in a sieve set over a bowl. Set aside 250 ml (1 cup) of the lychee syrup for the cake.
In a blender, purée the lychees and the remaining syrup until smooth. Set aside.
In a blender, purée the raspberries until smooth. Strain through a fine sieve. Set aside.
Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter two 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans and two 15 cm (6 inch) springform pans and line them with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, cream the butter and sugar with an electric mixer until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time and beat until smooth and fluffy. Add the dry ingredients alternately with the lychee syrup and milk. Divide the batter among the 4 pans so that each has about 2.5 cm (1 inch) of batter.
Bake all the cakes for 35 to 40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool completely.

Lychee Frosting: Meanwhile, in a saucepan over medium heat, melt 60 ml (¼ cup) of the butter. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the lychee purée and bring to a boil, whisking. Simmer over low heat for 1 minute.
Pour into a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface to keep a skin from forming, and let cool to room temperature.
Add the sugar and the remaining butter. Beat with an electric mixer for about 5 minutes or until the frosting is smooth and creamy. Set aside.
Raspberry frosting: Repeat steps 8, 9 and 10 with the raspberry purée instead of the lychee purée. Set aside.
Assembly: On a work surface, slice the tops off the cakes with a bread knife.

Place one large cake on a plate. Spread 125 ml (½ cup) of the raspberry frosting over the entire surface. Top with the second large cake. Cover the centre (the size of the small cake) with 75 ml (1/3 cup) of the raspberry frosting. Place a small cake on top. Spread 75 ml (1/3 cup) of the raspberry frosting over the entire surface. Add the last small cake.

Cover all the tiers completely with a thin layer of the lychee frosting. Refrigerate for 30 minutes or until the frosting is firm. Cover completely with the lychee frosting a second time, setting aside about 250 ml (1 cup) of frosting for the flowers.
Press cookie cutters of different sizes onto the cake to mark the outlines of the flowers.

Transfer the remaining raspberry frosting and lychee frosting into two pastry bags fitted with two small star tips. Fill the flower petals with the raspberry frosting and the centres with the lychee frosting.

7159.title: Chipotle Popcorn
instructions: Popcorn: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350 °F (180 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.

In a large saucepan over medium-high heat, heat the oil. Add the kernels and coat well with the oil. Cover. Over medium heat, pop the corn kernels, shaking the saucepan regularly. The popcorn is ready when you no longer hear kernels popping. Set aside.
Chipotle Seasoning: In a large bowl, combine the oil, chipotle sauce, salt and spices. Add the popcorn and stir to coat. Spread the popcorn on the prepared sheet.
Bake for about 5 minutes or until the popcorn has completely absorbed the spice mixture. Allow to cool.
The popcorn keeps for 2 to 3 weeks in a cool, dry place.

7166.title: Bean Salad with Chicken and Grapes
instructions: In a saucepan of salted boiling water, cook the beans al dente. Plunge into ice water for a few seconds. Drain. Set aside in a bowl.
Meanwhile, in a small saucepan over medium heat, soften the shallot in the oil. Add the curry powder and mix well. Transfer to the bowl with the beans. Let cool.
Stir in the remaining ingredients. Salt and pepper.

7178.title: Roast Turkey with Pastis and Maple Sauce
instructions: Turkey: Place the turkey, breast side up, in a large glass dish. Season the inside of the turkey with 15 ml (3 tsp) of the salt. Sprinkle the remaining salt rub over the breast and legs of the turkey. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 3 days.
With the rack in the lowest position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In a bowl, combine the mustard and maple syrup. Place the turkey in a large roasting pan, breast side up. Pat the skin of the turkey dry with paper towels. Brush it with the mustard and maple syrup mixture.

Bake for 1 hours 30 minutes. Raise the oven temperature to 200 °C (400 °F). Arrange the vegetables around the turkey. Continue cooking for about 1 hour or until a thermometer inserted in the thigh, without touching the bone, reads 82 °C (180 °F). Transfer the turkey to a serving dish and let rest, uncovered, for about 30 minutes.
Sauce: In a bowl, dissolve the cornstarch in the broth.

In a large skillet over medium heat, soften the shallots in the butter. Add the maple syrup and continue cooking for about 4 minutes or until it starts to caramelize. Deglaze with Pastis. Add the broth mixture and bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Reduce by half. Add the parsley.
Serve the turkey with the vegetables and the tarragon mashed potatoes. Drizzle with the sauce.

7179.title: Tarragon Mashed Potatoes
instructions: In a pot of boiling salted water, cook the potatoes for about 20 minutes or until tender. Drain.
