Using a potato masher, coarsely mash the potatoes with the butter and pastis. Add the cream and tarragon. With an electric mixer, beat until smooth. Salt and pepper.
Delicious with roast turkey, or with fish.

7181.title: Pumpkin Pie (The Best)
instructions: Crust: In a food processor, combine the flour, sugar and salt. Add the butter and pulse until the butter forms pea-sized pieces. Add the yogurt and pulse again until the dough just begins to form. Remove the dough from the food processor and form into a disc with your hands. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
With the rack in the lowest position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).

On a lightly floured work surface, roll out the dough and line a 23 cm (9 inch) pie plate. Trim the excess dough to 1 cm (½ inch) outside the pie plate. Fold the dough under to form a double thickness. Flute the edge (with your fingers, form a series of curves to decorate it). Set aside.
Filling: In a bowl, combine the cornstarch and spices. Whisk in the eggs. Add the pumpkin purée and sweetened condensed milk. Mix until smooth and pour into the crust.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until the filling is slightly jiggly in the centre. Let cool on a wire rack.
In a bowl, whip cream with sugar until stiff peaks form. Using a pastry bag fitted with a star tip, decorate the edge of the pie or top each slice when ready to serve.

7184.title: Fruit Plum Pudding
instructions: Fruit: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Cover with plastic wrap and let macerate for 12 hours or overnight at room temperature. Drain (see note).
Cake: Butter a 25 x 10 cm (10 x 4 inch) loaf pan with a 1.5-litre (6-cup) capacity. Line with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.
In a bowl, combine the flour, almond powder, baking powder and spices. Set aside.

In another bowl, cream the butter and brown sugar with an electric mixer. Add the eggs and beat until smooth. On low speed or with a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients and the drained fruit. Spoon the batter into the prepared pan.
Place in the slow cooker. Pour cold water into the slow cooker, halfway up the sides of the pan.
Place a clean, dry towel over the slow cooker insert, without touching the batter, and set the lid on top to hold it in place. This keeps water from dripping onto the surface of the cake.
Cook on low for 4 hours or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Remove from the slow cooker and let cool completely on a rack before unmoulding.

Sauce: In a small saucepan over medium-high heat, bring all the ingredients to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes. Pour into a sauce boat or a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and let cool slightly. Store at room temperature.
The cake keeps for about 2 weeks at room temperature. It can also be frozen.

7185.title: Hot Cider
instructions: On a work surface, stick a clove into the peel of each orange cube. Place in the slow cooker. Add the remaining ingredients.
Cover and steep on low for 4 hours. It can be maintained on Warm for up to 12 hours.

7188.title: Three-Citrus Vodka
instructions: Over a saucepan, remove long strips of zest from the grapefruit, orange and lime with a vegetable peeler. Then squeeze the juice from the citrus fruits.
Bring the citrus zest and juice to a boil with the sugar, stirring until the sugar has dissolved. Let the syrup cool.
In a bottle or an airtight glass container, combine the syrup and vodka. Let macerate in a cool, dark place for 7 days.
Strain the alcohol through a sieve lined with a coffee filter or cheesecloth. Store in the freezer until ready to serve.

7196.title: Cranberry Raspberry Trifle
instructions: Raspberry Pastry Cream: In a pot off the heat, combine the sugar with the cornstarch. Add the eggs and egg yolks. Whisk well. Stir in the raspberry purée and lemon juice. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring continuously while scraping the bottom and sides of the pan, until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat.

Strain the custard through a sieve into a bowl, if needed. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Cool and refrigerate for about 2 hours or until completely chilled. When ready to use the custard, stir with a spatula to soften it. Cranberry and Raspberry Compote

Cranberry and Raspberry Compote: In a saucepan over medium heat, bring the cranberries, sugar and water to a boil. Simmer for about 10 minutes or until the compote is syrupy. Let cool slightly, then refrigerate for 30 minutes or until completely cold. When assembling, stir in the raspberries.
Assembly: In a bowl, whip the cream, sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.

In the bottom of a glass serving bowl of about 3 litres (12 cups), spread 125 ml (½ cup) of the whipped cream. Stand 16 ladyfinger halves against the sides of the bowl and arrange 8 ladyfinger halves, quickly dipped in the milk, on top of the cream. Cover with half the raspberry pastry cream, half the whipped cream and half the cranberry and raspberry compote, then finish with the remaining ladyfinger halves dipped in the milk. Continue with the remaining raspberry pastry cream and whipped cream. Refrigerate for 12 hours.
When ready to serve, drain the remaining cranberry and raspberry compote and arrange it in a ring on top of the trifle.

7207.title: Spiced Beef Fajitas
instructions: Beef: In a small bowl, combine the brown sugar, spices, salt and pepper.
On a plate, coat and rub the flap steaks with the spice mixture.
In a cast-iron skillet over high heat, cook one steak at a time in 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the oil for about 3 minutes per side for rare, or longer to the desired doneness (see note). Set aside on a plate.
Vegetables: In the same cast-iron skillet, wiped clean, over medium-high heat, cook the vegetables in the oil for about 5 minutes or until al dente. Salt and pepper.
Assembly: On a work surface, thinly slice the meat against the grain.
Serve the meat and vegetables in the cast-iron skillet in the middle of the table with the toppings, and let everyone fill their own tortillas.

7209.title: Multicoloured Layer Cake
ingredients: each of the following gel food colourings: royal blue, mint green, lemon yellow and red
instructions: Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350 °F (180 °C). Butter two 8-inch (20-cm) springform pans and line the bottom with parchment paper. Set aside.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, beat the eggs with the sugar and vanilla using an electric mixer for about 10 minutes or until the mixture triples in volume and falls from the whisk in a ribbon. Drizzle in the oil while beating.

At low speed, add the dry ingredients alternately with the milk until the batter is smooth. Divide the cake batter among 4 bowls, about 400 ml (1 2/3 cups) of batter per bowl. Add one food colouring per bowl and mix well. Cover two bowls and set them aside on the counter. Pour the other two batters into the two pans.
Bake both pans at the same time for about 25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Let cool for 15 minutes. Unmould and let cool completely on a wire rack.
Wash the pans and dry them well. Butter both pans and line the bottoms with parchment paper. Pour the other two cake batters into the pans.
Bake both pans at the same time for about 25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Let cool for 15 minutes. Unmould and let cool completely on a wire rack.
Vanilla Frosting: In a bowl, beat the butter with the vanilla using an electric mixer until creamy.
On low speed, gradually add the icing sugar and beat until the frosting is smooth and fluffy. Add a little milk if the frosting is too thick. The more the frosting is beaten, the whiter it will be.

Assembly: Cut off the top of each cake to level them. Cover each cake with about 125 ml (½ cup) of the vanilla frosting. Place the blue cake on a serving plate. Stack the green cake, the yellow one, then the red one on top. Frost the entire cake with the remaining frosting.
Make a circular band on top of the cake with the multicoloured candies.

7210.title: Rainbow Cake
instructions: Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350 °F (180 °C). Butter two 8-inch (20-cm) springform pans and line the bottom with parchment paper. Set aside.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, beat the eggs with the sugar and vanilla using an electric mixer for about 10 minutes or until the mixture triples in volume and falls from the whisk in a ribbon. Drizzle in the oil while beating.
At low speed, stir in the dry ingredients alternately with the milk until smooth. Spoon the batter into the prepared pans.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool for 15 minutes. Unmould and let cool completely on a wire rack.
Frosting: In a bowl, beat the butter with the vanilla using an electric mixer until creamy.
On low speed, gradually add the icing sugar and beat until the frosting is smooth and fluffy. Add a little milk if the frosting is too thick.
Assembly: Cut off the top of each cake to level them before decorating with the frosting.

Set aside 1 litre (4 cups) of the frosting for the colours. Frost one cake with about 180 ml (¾ cup) of the white frosting. Top with the second cake. Cover the cake with the remaining white frosting to trap the crumbs and give it a more finished look. Refrigerate the cake while you make the colours.
For the red, place about 250 ml (1 cup) of frosting in a bowl. Add the cocoa (it makes the red more intense; otherwise the colour will be pinker) and the red food colouring. Mix well (see note).
For the other colours, divide the remaining frosting among 5 other bowls, about 150 ml (2/3 cup) of frosting per bowl. Add one food colouring per bowl and mix.
Frost the top of the cake with 125 ml (½ cup) of the red frosting.
Press the end of a plain piping tip into the cake from top to bottom to mark where each of the six rainbow colours of frosting will start.
Fill a pastry bag fitted with a large plain round tip with the purple frosting and pipe a dot at the base of the cake.
Using a small metal pastry spatula or a small coffee spoon, press lightly on the frosting to spread it horizontally over about 2.5 cm (1 inch).
Pipe another dot of frosting and repeat, turning the cake, to form a band of colour all around the cake. Continue with the other colours.

7213.title: Pasta with Candied Peppers and Asparagus
instructions: In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, cook the peppers, onions and garlic in the oil for about 15 minutes or until the onions and peppers are translucent and soft. Salt and pepper. Add the harissa. Stir to combine.

Meanwhile, in a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta until al dente. About two minutes before the end of cooking, add the asparagus. Keep 125 ml (½ cup) of the cooking water aside. Drain.
Add the pasta, asparagus, cooking water and Parmesan to the skillet with the pepper mixture. Stir to combine and adjust the seasoning. Salt and pepper.

7238.title: Gluten-Free Gnocchi with Sage Butter
instructions: Gnocchi: In a bowl, whisk together the eggs and potato starch. Add the mashed potatoes, Parmesan and nutmeg. Stir well with wooden spoon. Salt and pepper. Transfer the dough to a pastry bag fitted with a plain tip about 1 cm (½ inch) in diameter.

Over a large pot of simmering salted water, pipe out a 2.5 cm (1 inch) length of dough. Cut it off with a knife and let it drop gently into the water. Cook a third of the dough at a time. When the gnocchi rise to the surface, simmer for about 4 minutes or until cooked through. Using a slotted spoon, drain the gnocchi and keep them warm in a large, lightly oiled dish. Continue with the remaining dough.

Sage Butter: In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, fry the sage in the butter until crisp. Set the sage aside. In the same skillet, add the gnocchi to the melted butter and toss gently. Salt and pepper.
When ready to serve, garnish with Parmesan, if desired, and the fried sage.

7274.title: Homemade Rustic Pasta (Pici)
instructions: In a bowl or a food processor, combine the semolina, flour and salt. Add boiling water and pulse again until dough just begins to form.

On a lightly floured surface, knead dough for about 5 minutes. If you make dough entirely by hand, knead for at least 10 minutes. Cut the dough in half. Roll one piece of dough at a time into a 15-cm (6-inch) wide rectangle that is about 3-mm (1/8 inch) thick. Wrap the remaining piece of dough in plastic wrap to keep it from drying out. With a knife, cut dough into thin 3-mm (1/8-inch) wide and 15-cm (6-inch) long strips. Repeat with the other piece of dough.
On a work surface, roll each strip of dough with your fingers to give it a slightly rounded shape.
Place pasta on a baking sheet covered with fine wheat semolina or unbleached all-purpose flour. Coat thoroughly. At this stage, the pici can be frozen.
In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook pici for about 5 minutes or until they are tender, but still slightly firm. Drain and oil lightly.
Delicious with garlic chili tomato sauce or Bolognese sauce.

7280.title: Berry Jelly Roll
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Butter a 43 x 30 cm (17 x 12 inch) baking sheet and line it with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides. Set aside.
In a bowl, combine the flour and salt. Set aside.

In a large bowl, beat the eggs, sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer until the mixture triples in volume and forms a ribbon as it falls from the beaters, about 10 minutes. With the mixer at low speed, drizzle in the oil.
With a whisk or spatula, gently fold in the dry ingredients.

Spread the batter on the baking sheet. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool. Run a knife blade between the baking sheet and the cake to loosen it. Slide the parchment paper onto a work surface and let cool.
Sprinkle half the icing sugar over the cake and the rest (15 ml/1 tbsp) over a sheet of parchment paper. Turn the cooled cake out onto the parchment paper.
Filling: In a bowl, whip the cream, sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.
Carefully remove the parchment paper from the cake. Trim the two long edges of the cake to even it out.

Using a spatula, stir the fruit spread to soften it before spreading it over the entire cake, leaving a border of about 0.5 cm (¼ inch) all around. Spread the cream over it. Roll cake from the short side.
Place the cake on a serving dish. Refrigerate until ready to serve. Sprinkle with icing sugar if desired.

7281.title: Dairy-Free Frozen Raspberry Parfait
instructions: In a blender, purée the raspberries until smooth. Strain through a sieve. You'll need 250 ml (1 cup) of purée. Set aside.
Lightly oil a 25 x 10 cm (10 x 4 inch) loaf pan with a 1.5-litre (6-cup) capacity and line it with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.

In a saucepan off the heat, combine 55 g (¼ cup) of the sugar and the cornstarch. Add 1 egg white and the lemon juice. Whisk well. Stir in the raspberry purée. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the saucepan. Strain if desired. Set aside in a large bowl.

In another bowl, beat the other 3 egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add the remaining sugar (105 g/½ cup) and beat until the sugar has dissolved and the meringue forms stiff peaks.
Using a spatula or a whisk, gently fold the meringue into the still-warm raspberry mixture. Pour into the prepared pan. Freeze for about 8 hours or until the parfait is firm to the touch.
Run a knife blade under hot water. Slide the blade between the pan and the parfait, then unmould. Cut into slices. Garnish with fresh raspberries, if desired.

7286.title: Antipasti Cold Pasta Salad
instructions: Vegetables: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the mushrooms, eggplants and peppers for 3 to 4 minutes per side. Let cool. Peel the peppers, if desired. Cut all the vegetables into large strips.
In a large bowl, combine the oil, sun-dried tomato pesto, vinegar, oregano and chili flakes. Add the grilled vegetables. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate until the pasta is cooked.
Salad: In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta al dente. Drain and oil lightly. Add the pasta to the marinated vegetables and mix well. Adjust the seasoning.
Divide among the plates. Garnish with the cheese and basil.

7288.title: Apple Raspberry Squares
instructions: Crumble: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Butter a 33 x 23 cm (13 x 9 inch) rectangular pan and line it with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.
In a bowl, combine the dry ingredients. Add the butter and mix until the mixture holds together when pressed between your fingers.
Press half the mixture into the bottom of the pan.
Filling: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Spread the fruit mixture in the pan. Cover with the remaining crumble. Press lightly.
Bake for about 50 minutes or until the crumble is golden brown. Let cool completely. Cut into squares.

7289.title: Potato and Smoked Meat Focaccia
instructions: Dough: In a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook, or in a large bowl with a wooden spoon, combine the flour, sugar, yeast and salt. Add the water and stir until a soft ball forms. Knead the dough for about 5 minutes in the stand mixer or on a floured work surface until smooth.

Form the dough into a ball and place in a clean, lightly oiled bowl, turning to coat with the oil. Cover with a damp towel and let rise in a warm, humid place for at least 2 hours or until doubled in volume.
Topping: In a large non-stick skillet, bring the potatoes and milk to a boil. Cover. Cook over low heat for about 15 minutes, stirring often, or until al dente. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Oil a baking sheet of about 43 x 30 cm (17 x 12 inches) and line it with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.

Spread the dough over the entire baking sheet. Sprinkle with the garlic and cheese. Drain the potatoes lightly and spread them over the entire surface of the dough. Sprinkle with rosemary. Salt and pepper.
Bake for about 30 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown. Add the smoked meat and continue baking for 1 minute.

7293.title: Avocados with Homemade Sour Cream
instructions: In a bowl, combine the cream and lime juice. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Place the avocados on a plate. Season with salt and pepper and top with the cream mixture.
Serve as a side with skewers.

7298.title: Grilled Zucchini with Feta and Pomegranate
instructions: Herb Oil: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Set aside.
Zucchini: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
On a baking sheet, oil the zucchini and season with salt and pepper. Grill the zucchini for 2 minutes per side or until tender.
Arrange the zucchini on a platter or large serving plate. Sprinkle with the feta, pomegranate seeds and sumac. Drizzle with the herb oil.

7300.title: Piri-Piri Vodka Shrimp Skewers
instructions: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Thread the shrimp onto the skewers. Salt and pepper.
Grill the skewers for about 2 minutes per side or until cooked through. Delicious with the corn and herb coleslaw.

7309.title: Linguine with Clams and Chorizo
instructions: In a large pot over high heat, bring the clams and wine to a boil. Cover and simmer for about 5 minutes or until the clams open. Remove the clams from the broth (discard any that did not open).
Over a bowl, strain the broth through a sieve lined with a coffee filter or two layers of cheesecloth to remove any sand that may have settled at the bottom of the pot. Set aside.
Remove half the clams from their shells and keep them warm in a large bowl with the other half still in their shells (see note).
In a large skillet over high heat, brown the chorizo in 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the oil. Add the parsley and cook for 1 minute. Set aside on a plate.

In the same skillet over high heat, soften the peppers, onion and garlic in the remaining oil (30 ml/2 tbsp). Add 250 ml (1 cup) of the clam broth, the tomatoes, chili pepper and paprika. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 5 minutes or until the sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, in a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta until al dente. Drain and add the pasta to the sauce. Add the clams and mix well. Add clam broth if the sauce is too thick.
Divide the pasta among shallow bowls or on a large serving platter and top with the chorizo mixture.

7310.title: Chicken, Olive and Chorizo Skewers
ingredients: skinless, boneless chicken breasts or thighs
instructions: Skewers: In a bowl, combine the chicken, oil, spices and salt. On each skewer, alternately thread 4 cubes of chicken, 6 slices of chorizo and 6 olives.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the skewers for about 3 minutes on each side. Turn off one section of the barbecue and continue cooking over indirect heat for about 7 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through.
To Serve: Serve the skewers with lemon wedges, tzatziki sauce or hummus, if desired.

7311.title: Pork Tenderloin and Shrimp Salad
instructions: Salad: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

Lightly oil the pork tenderloin. Salt and pepper. Grill the meat for about 15 minutes, turning it regularly, or until a thermometer inserted in the meat reads 57 °C (135 °F). Place on a cutting board and let cool. Thinly slice the meat.

In a pot of boiling salted water, cook the sugar snap peas until al dente. Using a slotted spoon, remove the peas, plunge them into ice water, then drain. Split them in half lengthwise (into two pods). Set aside in a large bowl.

In the same pot of boiling salted water, cook the shrimp for about 2 minutes or until cooked. Plunge into ice water and drain. Cut the shrimp in half through their thickness. Add to the peas with the remaining ingredients.
Dressing: In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients. Add the dressing to the salad and toss gently. Salt and pepper.
Divide the salad and cold pork slices among the plates.

7313.title: Coconut Milkshake
instructions: Using a 30 ml (2 tbsp) ice cream scoop, shape 2 scoops of vanilla ice cream. Keep the scoops in the freezer until ready to serve.
In a blender, blend the remaining ice cream with the coconut milk, vanilla and cinnamon for about 1 minute or until the milk is frothy.
Pour into 1 or 2 frosted glasses. Add a scoop of ice cream. Serve with two straws.

7314.title: Coconut Cream Pie
instructions: Crust: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a food processor, grind the butter cookies to a powder. Add the coconut flour. Add the butter and process until the mixture is moistened.

Press the mixture into the bottom and up the sides of a 23 cm (9 inch) tart pan with a removable bottom. Bake until the crust is lightly browned and filling is hot, about 10 minutes. Let cool completely, about 1 hour.

Coconut Pastry Cream: In a saucepan off the heat, combine the sugar and cornstarch. Add the egg and egg yolks. Whisk until smooth. Add the coconut milk and cream. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the saucepan.

Remove from the heat, add the coconut and pour into the crust. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the cream and refrigerate for 4 hours or until the filling is completely cold. Remove the plastic wrap from the Pyrex dish.
Topping: In a bowl, whip the cream with the icing sugar until stiff peaks form. Spread over the pie. Sprinkle with coconut chips. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
The pie keeps for about 2 days in the refrigerator.

7316.title: Coconut, Apricot and Passion Fruit Bostock
ingredients: slices of homestyle or sandwich white bread
instructions: Frangipane: In a food processor, combine the ground almonds, coconut and sugar. Add the butter and process until the mixture forms a paste. Add the eggs and process until smooth and creamy. Set the frangipane aside.
Bostock: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, combine the apricot jam, passion fruit juice and apricots.
Place the bread slices on the baking sheet and butter them on both sides. Spread the apricot mixture on the bread, then spread the frangipane over it to cover the entire surface.
Bake for about 20 minutes or until the frangipane starts to brown. Garnish the bostock with coconut chips, if desired.

7317.title: Chocolate Coconut Macaroons
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
In another bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until frothy. Gradually add the sugar, beating until the meringue forms soft peaks.
Add the other ingredients and fold gently with a spatula.
Using a 15 ml (1 tbsp) ice cream scoop, shape balls without packing them and place them on the baking sheets.
Bake for about 10 minutes or until the macaroons are set on the outside but still soft in the centre. Let cool completely.
The macaroons keep for about 2 weeks in an airtight container.

7318.title: Coconut Chips
instructions: Open the coconut and remove the meat.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Using a vegetable peeler, cut the flesh into thin shavings.
In a bowl, sprinkle the shavings with the icing sugar and mix well. Spread on the baking sheet.
Bake for about 20 minutes or until dry and lightly golden. Stir halfway through. Let cool completely.

7320.title: Yogurt Lime Sauce
instructions: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

7321.title: Chocolate Sauce
instructions: In a small glass bowl, combine the chocolate and water.
Microwave for 30 seconds or until the chocolate has almost completely melted (a few pieces may remain). Stir until the sauce is smooth.
Serve right away, as the sauce sets quickly.

7322.title: Fruit Couscous
instructions: Pour 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the orange juice in a large bowl. Set aside.

In a small saucepan, bring the remaining juice to a boil. Remove from the heat and add the couscous. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes. Fluff the couscous with a fork. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
On a work surface, dice the peaches. Place in the bowl with the orange juice and toss well. Add the cooled couscous, yogurt and maple syrup and mix.
Divide among small bowls. Garnish with fresh fruit and serve.

7383.title: Rabbit with Mustard
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat, brown the rabbit in the butter. Salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate. Sprinkle the flour over the melted butter in the skillet and cook it, stirring, for 1 minute or until golden. Add the broth and bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Add the onion, garlic and bay leaf. Stir to combine. Return the rabbit to the skillet. Cover and bake for 1 hour, turning the rabbit halfway through.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the cream and mustard. Set aside.

Remove the skillet from the oven. Discard the onion, garlic and bay leaf. Set the rabbit aside on a plate. Using a whisk, stir the cream mixture into the cooking juices in the skillet. Return the rabbit to the skillet. Cover and bring to a boil. Continue cooking in the oven for 15 minutes or until the meat falls apart easily with a fork.
Delicious with the Brussels sprout tagliatelle.

7384.title: Brussels Sprout Tagliatelle
instructions: In a pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta until al dente. Drain and lightly oil. Set aside.

Meanwhile, place the Brussels sprouts, broth and butter in a large skillet. Bring to a boil, cover and cook for 5 minutes. Add the pasta and continue cooking until it has absorbed almost all the broth.
Delicious with the rabbit with mustard.

7396.title: Avocado and Cheese Stuffed Chicken
ingredients: skinless and boneless chicken breast halves
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

On a work surface, butterfly the chicken. To do this, slice the chicken breasts through their thickness and open them up without cutting all the way through. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Arrange the avocado slices and 4 slices of cheese on them. Close the breasts and place them on 4 sheets of aluminum foil. Drizzle the chicken with the oil. Top with the thyme sprigs, the remaining cheese and the lime wedges. Add a few drops of Tabasco. Close to seal the papillotes. Place the papillotes on a baking sheet.
Bake until the chicken is cooked through, about 40 minutes. Remove the stuffed chicken from the foil packet and serve with a green salad.

7414.title: Braised Pork Roast with Barley and Corn
instructions: Roast: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
In an enamelled cast-iron Dutch oven or a large ovenproof pot over medium-high heat, brown the meat on all sides in the oil. Salt and pepper. Set the meat aside on a plate.

In the same Dutch oven over medium heat, soften the vegetables. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 more minute, stirring constantly. Deglaze with the wine. Bring to a boil and reduce by half. Add the broth and the meat. Bring to a boil. Cover and bake for 3 hours or until the meat falls apart with a fork, turning it halfway through.

Place the meat on a plate. Remove the string. Set the vegetables aside for the barley stew. Strain the sauce through a sieve. Return the sauce to the same Dutch oven and, over medium-high heat, reduce it by half. Set aside.

Toasted Barley Stew: Meanwhile, in another large saucepan over medium-high heat, brown the barley and onion in the oil. Add the broth and bring to a boil. Simmer over medium heat for 40 minutes or until the barley is tender, stirring often. Add the reserved vegetables and the cream. Season with salt and pepper.

Topping: In a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the bacon in the oil. Drain the bacon on paper towels. Keep about 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the cooking fat in the skillet. Add the green onion and continue cooking for 2 minutes or until translucent. Add the arugula and corn. Cook for 2 minutes. Season with pepper. Return the bacon to the skillet and set aside.
Spread the barley stew on a large serving platter. Add the meat and cover with the bacon topping.

7452.title: Sour Cherry and Pear Jam
instructions: In a saucepan, combine all the ingredients. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium-low heat for 45 minutes or until the cooking juices are syrupy. Let cool.

Transfer into airtight containers or hot jars. To sterilize the filled jars of jam, allow 10 minutes in boiling water. They keep for 1 year at room temperature. Unsterilized jars of jam keep for 1 month in the refrigerator.

7455.title: Chocolate Pecan Pie
instructions: Shortcrust Pastry: In a food processor, combine the flour, sugar and salt. Add the butter and pulse a few seconds at a time until the mixture has a grainy texture. Add the ice water and vinegar. Pulse again, adding a little water if needed, until the dough starts to form a ball. Remove the dough from the food processor and form into a disc.
On a floured work surface, roll out the dough and line a 23 cm (9 inch) pie plate. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).

Filling: In a saucepan, melt the butter. Add the corn syrup and brown sugar. Warm up and remove from the heat. Add the chocolate and stir until completely melted. Add the eggs, whisking. Spread the filling in the cold pie shell. Arrange the pecans on the filling.
Bake for 45 minutes or until the filling is firm. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
Serve, or freeze at this stage. If the pie was frozen, let it stand for 4 hours before serving.

7465.title: Endive and Smoked Salmon Salad with Honey Vinaigrette
instructions: Honey Vinaigrette: In a large bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Salad: In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the potatoes until tender. Drain. Plunge into ice water until completely cooled. Drain. Cut in half and place in the bowl with the vinaigrette.
Add the spinach, endives and radishes. Salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
Divide the salad among the plates and top with the smoked salmon.

7520.title: Pappardelle with Veal Ragout and Cherry Tomato Confit
instructions: Veal Ragout: Place two racks in the middle of the oven. Preheat to 165 °C (325 °F).
In a large ovenproof non-stick skillet or Dutch oven over high heat, brown the meat in the oil. Salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate.

In the same skillet over medium-high heat, brown the vegetables and garlic. Add a little oil, if needed. Add the tomato paste and mix thoroughly. Deglaze with the wine, then add the broth. Return the meat to the skillet and bring to a boil.
Cover and bake for 2 hours or until the meat is fork tender. Remove from the oven. Skim the fat from the meat if needed, shred it and keep it warm in the sauce.
Cherry Tomato Confit: Meanwhile, line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Place the tomatoes cut side up. Drizzle with the oil. Salt and pepper.
Bake at the same time as the veal for 45 minutes or until the tomatoes start to caramelize. Set aside.
Pappardelle: In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta al dente. Set aside 1 cup (250 ml) of the cooking water. Drain the pasta. Oil lightly and set aside.
Meanwhile, in a large skillet over medium-high heat, soften the vegetables and garlic in the oil. Salt and pepper. Set aside.

Over medium-low heat, stir the cheese into the meat as you reheat it, until melted. Add a little of the pasta cooking water to thin the ragout, if needed. Stir in the pasta and basil. Top with the sautéed vegetables and cherry tomatoes.

7528.title: Tomato Rice
instructions: In the same pot over medium heat, soften the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the rice and chili powder. Stir to coat the rice well with oil. Add the water and tomato purée. Salt and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer over low heat for about 25 minutes or until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid.

7531.title: Nut-Free Baklava
instructions: Honey Syrup: In a small saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil and stir until the sugar has completely dissolved. Let cool.
Baklava: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Butter an 8-inch (20 cm) square, straight-edged baking pan.
In a bowl, combine the sunflower and sesame seeds with the sugar and cinnamon. Set aside.

Place a sheet of phyllo pastry in the pan. Using a brush, brush with butter. Cover with 3 more sheets, brushing each with butter. Spread a third of the sunflower mixture (80 g/1/2 cup) over them. Repeat this step twice, finishing with 4 sheets of phyllo pastry brushed with butter. Cut into 16 small squares.
Bake for 1 hour or until the pastry is golden brown.
As soon as it comes out of the oven, pour the honey syrup over the entire surface of the baklava, removing the lemon zest and cinnamon stick. Let cool at room temperature for 6 hours or overnight.
The baklava keeps for 7 to 10 days in an airtight container at room temperature.

7535.title: 40-Clove Garlic Chicken
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place the chicken in a large Dutch oven. Rub the chicken with the vinegar. Season with salt and pepper inside and out the chicken. Let rest for 15 minutes.

Place the garlic cloves around the chicken and add the wine. Cover and bake for 1 hour. Remove the lid. Baste the chicken with the cooking juices. Continue cooking, uncovered, for 45 minutes or until the meat comes away easily from the bone and the chicken is well browned.

7537.title: Miso-Maple Chicken Wings
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
On a work surface, cut the chicken wings at the joints to get three pieces. Discard the tips and keep only the other two pieces. Pat the wings dry with paper towel. Set aside.

In a bowl, combine the maple syrup, miso, garlic and chili. Add the chicken wings and coat them well. Spread on the baking sheet. Bake for 45 minutes or until well browned and the meat comes away easily from the bone.

7540.title: Chicken Noodle Soup
instructions: Broth: Place the chicken carcass in a large pot. Cover with the water. Bring to a boil. When the broth starts to boil, skim it until it releases almost no more impurities, about 5 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine the turmeric and oil, then stir into the broth.
Add the remaining ingredients, then simmer for 2 hours. Strain the broth through a sieve into another pot.

To remove the fat from the broth, let it cool slightly, then refrigerate it so the fat rises to the surface. Degrease the chilled broth before using or freezing. You can also remove the fat while it is still hot by lining a large colander with a layer of paper towels and straining the broth through it into another pot.
Take the meat off the chicken carcass (see note). Keep the meat. Discard the carcass and vegetables.

To Finish: Add the parsley to the broth. Bring to a boil. Add the vermicelli and continue cooking for 3 to 5 minutes or until cooked. Stir about 250 ml (1 cup) of cooked chicken, or to taste, into the broth. Keep the rest of the meat for another use.

7542.title: Veal Roast with Vegetables and Apple Jelly Sauce
instructions: Veal Roast and Sauce: In a small saucepan over high heat, bring half the water (125 ml/1/2 cup), the salt, sugar, garlic and juniper berries to a boil. Remove from the heat. Add the remaining water. Let cool slightly. Place the roast and the brine in a resealable bag. Refrigerate for 2 hours. Remove the meat from the brine. Pat the meat dry. Discard the brine.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In an ovenproof skillet over high heat, brown the meat in the butter. Continue cooking in the oven for 25 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the roast reads 52 °C (125 °F). Set the roast aside on a plate and cover with aluminum foil until the internal temperature of the meat reaches 55 °C (130 °F), about 15 minutes.
Deglaze the skillet with the broth and apple jelly. Reduce by half. Season with pepper. Keep warm.

Vegetables: Meanwhile, in another skillet over medium-high heat, soften the Swiss chard stems and fennel in the butter with the garlic. Add the cherry tomatoes and continue cooking for 2 minutes. Add the chard leaves and continue cooking until slightly wilted. Salt and pepper. Add the basil.
Slice the meat as thinly as possible. Line the plates with kohlrabi slices. Divide the vegetables among the centres of the plates. Top with the meat. Drizzle with the sauce.

7545.title: Chive Trout with Squash Purée
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the chives, garlic and 45 ml (3 tbsp) of the oil. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a pot of boiling salted water, cook the squash and potato for 20 minutes or until the vegetables are very tender. Drain the vegetables and return them to the pot.
With a masher, coarsely crush the potatoes and garlic with the butter. Salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Meanwhile, in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the fish in the remaining oil for 5 minutes or to the desired doneness. Set aside on a plate.
In the same hot skillet, cook the spinach until just wilted. Salt and pepper.
Divide the squash purée and spinach among the plates. Place the trout on top. Garnish with the chive mixture.

7546.title: Small Maple Cheesecake
ingredients: maple or plain dulce de leche
instructions: Crust: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Generously butter the sides of a 15 cm (6 inch) springform pan and line the bottom with parchment paper.

In a food processor, finely grind the oats with the flour, maple sugar and baking powder. Add the butter and pulse until the butter forms pea-sized pieces. Add the egg yolk. Process again until the dough is smooth. Remove the dough from the food processor and form into a disc. Spread the dough over the bottom of the pan.
Bake for 20 minutes or until the crust is golden. Remove from the oven. Let cool on a wire rack.
Filling: In a food processor, cream the cheese. Add the yogurt, maple sugar, flour, egg and egg white. Mix until the filling is just smooth. With a spatula, scrape down the sides a few times.
In a bowl, combine the dulce de leche and 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the cheese filling. Set aside.

Spread the remaining cheese filling over the crust. Drizzle the dulce de leche mixture over the cake. Using a small spoon, lightly swirl the two fillings together with small circular motions to create a marbled effect inside the cake.
Wrap the pan tightly in a double layer of aluminum foil, like a packet.

Bake for 1 hour 10 minutes or until the cake is cooked and the filling no longer jiggles in the centre. Remove the aluminum foil. Let cool for 1 hour on a rack. Cover and refrigerate for 6 hours or until the cake is completely cold.
Run the blade of a knife between the cake and the pan. Unmould. Serve with a drizzle of dulce de leche, if desired.

7557.title: Boston Cream Pie
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line the bottom of a 20 cm (8 inch) springform pan with parchment paper. Do not butter the pan.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat the eggs and sugar with an electric mixer for 10 minutes until the mixture triples in volume and forms a ribbon as it falls from the beaters.
Sift the dry ingredients over the eggs, gently folding in with a whisk. Spoon the batter evenly in the prepared pan.

Bake for 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool for 30 minutes on a rack, then turn the cake upside down while still in the pan and let cool completely, about 30 minutes.
Pastry Cream: In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the milk. Let bloom for 5 minutes.
In a saucepan over medium-low heat, gently heat the remaining milk, the cream and the vanilla seeds and pod.

In another saucepan off the heat, combine the sugar and cornstarch. Add the egg yolks and whisk well. Gradually whisk in the hot milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the pan until the mixture thickens. Add the gelatin mixture and stir until dissolved. Remove from the heat. Strain the cream.

Stir the butter into the pastry cream. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool slightly and refrigerate for 1 hour or until completely cold. When ready to use the pastry cream, stir it with a spatula to make it smooth again.

Assembly: Unmould cake. Cut the cake in half horizontally to have a total of two cake layers. Place the bottom layer on a serving plate. Spread the pastry cream over the entire surface. Top with the other cake layer. Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Ganache: In a bowl, place the chocolate. Set aside.
In a small saucepan, bring the cream to a boil. Pour the hot cream over the chocolate. Allow to melt for 1 minute without stirring. Using a whisk, stir the ganache until smooth. Let cool.
Take the cake out of the refrigerator. Spread the ganache over the top of the cake.
The cake will keep for 2 days in the refrigerator.

7560.title: Fried Shallots
instructions: In a small saucepan, heat about 2.5 cm (1 inch) of canola oil. Line a plate with paper towels. Set aside.
Dredge the shallots in the flour and shake to remove any excess. Fry the shallots until crisp and lightly golden brown. Drain on the paper towels. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

7571.title: Bruschetta Ricotta
instructions: In a bowl, stir the ricotta with a spatula to soften it. Salt and pepper. Drizzle with olive oil.

7600.title: Barbecued Oysters with Quick Kimchi
instructions: Quick Kimchi: In a bowl, combine the cabbage and salt. Let marinate for 15 minutes. Rinse under cold water. Drain the cabbage and pat it dry.
In another bowl, combine the cabbage and the remaining ingredients. Set aside until ready to serve.
Oysters: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Place the oysters on the grill and cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until they open slightly.
Open the oysters completely and place them on a serving plate. Serve with the quick kimchi.

7601.title: 8-Lemon Loaf
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter a 25 x 10 cm (10 x 4 inch) loaf pan with a 1.5-litre (6-cup) capacity and line it with a strip of parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.
In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream the butter, sugar and zest with an electric mixer. Add the eggs, one at a time, and beat until smooth.
In a small bowl, combine the lemon juice and milk.
At low speed, add dry ingredients alternately with the milk mixture. Pour the batter into the prepared pan.

Bake for 1 hour or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. As soon as it comes out of the oven, poke dozens of small holes in the cake with a small wooden skewer or toothpicks.
Syrup: Meanwhile, in a saucepan, bring the sugar, lemon juice and water to a boil to dissolve the sugar. Remove from the heat.

Lift out the still-warm cake with the parchment paper and place it in a shallow dish larger than the cake. Pour a third of the syrup over the top of the cake. Turn the cake onto one side and drizzle with a third of the syrup. Repeat on the other side of the cake with the remaining syrup. Using the parchment paper, return the soaked cake to the loaf pan. Collect the syrup that has pooled in the dish and gradually pour it over the entire surface of the cake. Cool completely in the pan. Unmould from the pan and place on a serving plate.
Glaze: In a small bowl, combine the icing sugar and lemon juice. Frost the cake.

7605.title: Candy Cane Shortbread Cookies
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the candy canes in a bowl. Set aside.
In another bowl, combine the flour and salt. Set aside.
In a third bowl, cream the butter with the icing sugar using an electric mixer. On low speed or with a wooden spoon, stir in the flour mixture, then the white chocolate.
Using an ice cream scoop of about 30 ml (2 tbsp) or your hands, shape balls of dough, then roll them in the candy, pressing lightly. Spread on the baking sheet.
Bake for 12 minutes or until the biscuits begin to brown. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet.
The shortbread keeps for 1 week in an airtight container at room temperature.

7615.title: Veal Cutlets with Roasted Squash and Cheesy Mushrooms
instructions: Vegetables: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

On the baking sheet, coat the squash wedges with the oil. Salt and pepper. Bake for 40 minutes. Turn the squash over. Sprinkle with half the cheese (50 g/1/2 cup). Continue cooking for 10 minutes or until the squash is tender and the cheese starts to brown. Set aside.

In a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the mushroom caps in the butter for 5 minutes or until tender. Fill the mushroom cavities with the remaining cheese (50 g/1/2 cup). Bake for 5 minutes or until cheese has melted. Keep warm.

Meat: On a work surface, flatten the cutlets slightly if needed. In a large skillet over high heat, brown two cutlets at a time in half the butter, about 1 minute per side. Salt and pepper. Set aside on a warm plate. Sprinkle the skillet with the flour and mix well. Deglaze with the broth and the garlic scape pesto. Bring to a boil, stirring, and let the sauce reduce by half. Adjust the seasoning.
Divide the meat and vegetables among the plates. Top with the sauce and sprinkle with parsley.

7624.title: Crane Berry
instructions: In a tall glass, place the thawed cranberries and add the parsnip gin.
Using a cocktail muddler, crush the cranberries until they burst slightly.
Add the spiced ginger simple syrup and the dashes of fir bitters.
Add the torn basil leaves.
Fill the glass three-quarters full with ice cubes and stir with a spoon.
Top up with sparkling water.
Garnish with a cranberry skewer or a fir sprig.

7626.title: Spaghetti with Cabbage
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
On the baking sheet, toss the cabbage with the bacon and oil. Salt and pepper. Bake for 40 minutes or until the bacon is well cooked, stirring halfway through.
Meanwhile, in a pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta al dente. Set 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the cooking water aside. Drain the pasta and return it to the pot.
Add the cabbage mixture, vinegar and chili pepper to the pasta. Season generously with salt and pepper. Add cooking water to taste.

7627.title: Dried Cranberry and Pear Oatmeal
instructions: In a small saucepan off the heat, combine all the ingredients except the pears. Over medium-high heat, bring to a boil, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon. Simmer, scraping the bottom and sides of the saucepan, for about 3 minutes or until the oatmeal has thickened but is still creamy.
Pour into a bowl. Top with the pears and a drizzle of maple syrup.

7648.title: Chocolate Rice Pudding
instructions: In a pot of lightly salted boiling water, cook the rice for 15 minutes or until tender. Drain and rinse under cold running water. Set aside.
In the same saucepan, cleaned, off the heat, combine the sugar and cornstarch. Add the eggs and whisk until smooth. Pour in the chocolate milk, whisking.

Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or a spatula and taking care to scrape the bottom and sides of the saucepan, until the custard thickens and coats the back of the spoon. Remove from the heat.
Stir in the rice. Transfer to a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface. Let cool slightly and refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight.
When ready to serve, whip the cream with the icing sugar until medium peaks form. Divide the chocolate rice pudding among bowls. Top with the whipped cream and grated chocolate.

7669.title: Plated Christmas Cake (Cranberries, Raspberries, Mascarpone and Pistachios)
ingredients: recipe Mascarpone and White Chocolate Cream
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a 20 cm (8 inch) square pan with a strip of parchment paper, letting it hang over each side. Butter the other two sides.

Spread the cake batter in the pan. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes or until the cake is golden and a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool and unmould. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
Trim the edges of the cake to even it out. Cut the cake into four 2.5 cm (1 inch) strips. Keep the rest of the cake for another use, or freeze it.

In a bowl, thin the cranberry and raspberry filling with a little water to give it the consistency of a sauce. Using a spoon, decorate each plate with a circular stroke of the cranberry and raspberry filling.

Using a pastry bag fitted with a plain tip of about 1 cm (½ inch) and filled with the mascarpone and white chocolate cream, pipe two straight lines side by side on each plate, the same length as the cake strips. Place the cake strips on top. Top with two lines of the mascarpone and white chocolate cream. Decorate with the cranberry and raspberry filling and the pistachio nougatine.

7693.title: Apple Strudel
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.

In a large bowl, combine the apples with the sugar. Soften in the microwave for 3 minutes, stirring halfway through. Drain over a bowl, pressing to extract the liquid. Keep the apple syrup for another use. Set the apples aside.
On a work surface, brush 1 sheet of phyllo pastry with butter using a brush, then dust with 15 ml (1 tbsp) of icing sugar through a sieve. Repeat, stacking the other sheets of pastry.

On the bottom third of the pastry, spread the breadcrumbs in a strip, leaving a 2.5 cm (1 inch) border. Spread the apples over the breadcrumbs. Roll up, packing the pastry tightly into a long log, without letting the filling escape. Place on the baking sheet. Tuck the ends of the pastry under the log and brush with butter.
Bake for 30 minutes or until the strudel is golden brown. Let cool slightly and cut into pieces.

7714.title: Herbed Cucumber Salad
instructions: In a bowl, combine the cucumbers, vinegar and salt. Season with pepper. Let rest for 5 minutes. Add the herbs. Delicious with lamb chops, grilled chicken or crispy pork tenderloin.

7722.title: Mulled Wine
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil, then continue cooking over medium heat for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and strain before serving.

7810.title: Savoury Yogurt with Cucumber and Toasted Almonds
instructions: In a bowl, combine the yogurt, grated cucumber and lime juice.
Top with the almonds, cucumber slices and a drizzle of oil. Sprinkle with fleur de sel and sumac, if desired. Serve immediately.

7829.title: Maple Walnut Cake
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter the sides of two 15 cm (6 inch) springform pans and line the bottoms with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour, walnuts, baking powder and salt. Set aside.

In a bowl, cream the butter with the brown sugar and maple sugar. Add the eggs, walnut oil and vanilla and beat until smooth. At low speed, add the dry ingredients alternately with the milk. Spoon the batter into the prepared pans.
Bake for 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Let cool completely on a wire rack. Unmould.
Maple Meringue: Place the egg whites and cream of tartar in a bowl. Set aside.
In a pot, bring the maple syrup to a boil. Cook without stirring until the thermometer reads 116 °C (240 °F). Remove from the heat.

Beat the egg whites and cream of tartar with an electric mixer on medium speed until foamy. Drizzle the hot maple syrup over the egg whites, avoiding the beaters. Increase the speed and continue to beat until the meringue forms stiff peaks, about 5 minutes.
Assembly: Place one cake on a plate. Spread 180 ml (3/4 cup) of the meringue over the cake. Top with the second cake. Cover the cake completely with the remaining meringue.
Using a small kitchen torch, lightly brown the meringue.

7830.title: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line one or two baking sheets with parchment paper or a silicone mat.
In a bowl, combine the oats, flour, raisins and baking soda.
In another bowl, cream the butter with the brown sugar and salt using an electric mixer. Add the egg and beat until smooth. At low speed or with a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients.
Using a 45 ml (3 tbsp) ice cream scoop, shape balls of dough and place 6 balls on each baking sheet.

Bake one sheet at a time for 12 minutes or until the cookies are lightly golden but still soft at the centre. Let cool completely on a wire rack. The oatmeal raisin cookies keep for 5 days in an airtight container at room temperature.

7832.title: Cream of Corn Soup with Lime and Chili
instructions: Cream of Corn Soup: In a large saucepan over medium-high heat, brown the onion in the butter. Add the corn and continue cooking for 2 minutes, stirring. Add the broth, milk, potato, chili powder and lime zest. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes or until the potato is tender.
In a blender, purée the soup until smooth. Salt and pepper. Strain through a sieve. Return to the saucepan and add the cream.
Topping: In a bowl, combine the popcorn and lime zest.
Serve the soup in bowls. Top with the sour cream and cilantro. Drizzle with a dash of lime juice. Serve with the popcorn.

7833.title: Cream of Cauliflower and Almond Soup
instructions: Cream of Cauliflower Soup: In a large pot over medium heat, soften the onion in the butter. Add the cauliflower, broth, almond beverage, potato and garlic. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes or until the vegetables are tender. Stir in the almond butter.
In a blender, purée the soup until smooth. Salt and pepper. Strain through a sieve.
Topping: Meanwhile, in a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the cauliflower in the butter. Remove from the heat and add the almonds. Salt and pepper.
Serve the soup in bowls. Top with the cauliflower mixture and sunflower sprouts.

7839.title: Choux Pastry
instructions: In a saucepan, bring the water, milk, butter, sugar and salt to a boil. Remove from the heat. Add the flour, all at once, and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough forms a smooth ball and pulls away from the walls.

Return the saucepan to medium heat and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes or until the dough dries out. This step is crucial for successful choux pastry. The dough is sufficiently dried out when a thin film coats the bottom of the pot. Transfer to a mixing bowl or to the bowl of a stand mixer.

Using a wooden spoon or the paddle attachment in the stand mixer, mix the dough for 5 minutes to cool it down and remove some of its humidity. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition, until the dough is smooth.

Transfer the dough to a pastry bag fitted with a large plain or star tip. The choux pastry is ready to be shaped and baked as directed in the recipe of your choice (éclairs, chouquettes, etc.) (see note). The choux pastry recipe is easily doubled.

7841.title: Lemon Meringue Éclairs
instructions: Lemon Pastry Cream: In a small saucepan off the heat, whisk together the sugar, cornstarch and lemon zest. Add the eggs and egg yolks and mix well. Stir in the lemon juice and water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the pan until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat. Strain the pastry cream through a sieve. Stir in the butter until smooth.
Pour the lemon pastry cream into a bowl. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap. Let cool, then refrigerate until completely chilled, about 2 hours.
Choux Pastry: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

Transfer the choux pastry to a pastry bag fitted with a 2 cm (3/4 inch) plain tip (see note). On the baking sheet, slowly pipe the dough into logs about 13 cm (5 inches) long and 2 cm (3/4 inch) wide, spacing them apart.
Bake for 25 minutes or until the éclairs are golden brown. Turn the oven off, prop the door ajar with a wooden spoon and let sit for 30 minutes. Let cool completely on the baking sheet.
Meringue: In the top of a double boiler, heat the sugar, egg whites, cream of tartar and vanilla, whisking constantly, until the sugar has dissolved. Remove the bowl from the double boiler.
Beat the mixture with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.

Assembly: Using a bread knife, cut the éclairs horizontally without separating the halves completely. Transfer the lemon pastry cream to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) plain tip and fill the éclairs.
Transfer the meringue to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) flat or star tip and pipe it over the tops of the éclairs. Using a small kitchen torch, brown the meringue.
Serve, or refrigerate until ready to serve. The éclairs are best the day they are made.

7842.title: Cilantro Pork
instructions: In a food processor, finely chop the cilantro, green onions, chili pepper, lime juice, oil and cumin. Salt and pepper.
Place the pieces of pork in the slow cooker and coat them with the cilantro mixture. Add the broth.
Cover and cook on Low for 8 hours. It can be maintained on Warm for up to 8 hours.

Remove the meat and cooking juices from the slow cooker. Shred the meat, taking care to remove the fat. Adjust the seasoning. Return to the slow cooker or to a serving dish with a little of the cooking juices.
Place the meat in the middle of the table with the sides and toppings.

7843.title: Pear, Ricotta and Blue Cheese Canapés
instructions: In a bowl, loosen the ricotta with a spatula. Salt and pepper.
Thinly slice the pear wedges crosswise. Drizzle lightly with lemon juice. Set aside.
Spread each crouton with ricotta. Divide the pear slices among all the Baguettes. Top with blue cheese. Drizzle with honey, if desired.

7844.title: Quick Salsa
instructions: In a food processor, chop the onion, chili pepper, garlic and cilantro.
Add the tomatoes, lime juice and cumin. Pulse again until the salsa has the texture you want, with larger or smaller pieces. Salt and pepper. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
The salsa keeps for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.

7846.title: Classic Guacamole
instructions: In a bowl, mash the avocado flesh with a fork. Add the remaining ingredients and mix well.
Serve, or cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate until ready to serve.

7847.title: Shrimp and Lime Canapés
ingredients: Boulangerie Grissol olive oil and sea salt Baguettes
instructions: In a bowl, mash the avocado with the lime juice using a fork. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
In another bowl, combine the shrimp, oil, lime zest and Sriracha sauce. Salt and pepper.
Spread the avocado purée on the Baguettes. Top with the shrimp mixture.

7848.title: Italian Sausage Canapés
ingredients: Boulangerie Grissol rosemary and olive oil Baguettes
instructions: Shape the sausage meat into small 5 ml (1 tsp) balls to make 24 meatballs and flatten them slightly.
In a small skillet over medium heat, heat the tomato sauce and sausage meatballs. Cover and cook the meatballs for 5 minutes or until cooked through.
Top each Baguette with a meatball and a little sauce. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Garnish with basil leaves.

7852.title: Broccoli and Sausage Stuffed Potatoes
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
Using a fork, prick the potatoes all over. Place on a plate. Cook in the microwave oven for 8 minutes or until tender, turning them over halfway through. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a pot of boiling salted water, cook the broccoli for 2 minutes. Plunge into ice water for 2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, cook the sausage meat in the oil until it starts to brown, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Set aside.
Cut the potatoes in half lengthwise. Slightly trim the rounded base of each potato half to stabilize them. Place the potatoes on the baking sheet.

Using a spoon, scoop out the potato flesh, leaving a 5 mm (1/4 inch) shell, and place it in a bowl. Mash the potato flesh with a fork. Add the milk and butter. Stir to combine. Add the broccoli, sausage and cheese. Salt and pepper. Spoon the filling into the potatoes.
Bake for 15 minutes or until the mash is lightly golden and the cheese has melted.

7853.title: Rum & Coke 2.0
instructions: In a tall glass half-filled with ice cubes, combine the rum, Campari, lime juice and grenadine syrup. Stir gently with a spoon. Top up with cola. Garnish with the maraschino cherries and the lime wedge.

7854.title: “Tractor Wheel” Glazed Doughnuts
instructions: Preheat the oil in the deep fryer to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with paper towels. Cut out 8 squares of parchment paper, 10 cm (4 inches) each.
Transfer the choux pastry to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) star tip. Pipe the dough into rings 7.5 cm (3 inches) in diameter on the parchment paper squares.

Gently lower 2 doughnuts at a time into the hot oil, paper side up, and cook for 1 to 1 1/2 minutes. Beware of splattering. Using tongs, remove the paper, then turn the doughnuts over. Continue cooking until golden, 1 to 1 1/2 minutes. Drain on the paper towels. Let cool completely.
In a bowl, whisk together the icing sugar, milk and vanilla. Place a wire rack on a baking sheet.
Dip the doughnuts in the glaze one at a time. Let the excess drip off and place on the rack. Let set for 10 minutes before serving. Best enjoyed the same day.

7855.title: Chouquettes
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, beat the egg with the water using a fork. Set the egg wash aside.
Transfer the choux pastry to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) plain tip. On the baking sheets, pipe balls of dough 2.5 cm (1 inch) in diameter, spacing them apart.
Using a brush, brush the balls of dough with the egg wash. Sprinkle generously with pearl sugar.
Bake one sheet at a time for 25 minutes or until the puffs are golden brown. Remove from the oven and let cool completely on the baking sheet.
Serve, or keep in an airtight container for 2 days at room temperature. Chouquettes are best the day they are made.

7860.title: Cream of Onion and Cheddar Soup with Apple and Bacon
instructions: Creamy Onion Soup: In a large saucepan over medium heat, soften the onions in the oil for 10 minutes, stirring often. Add the broth and potatoes. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender.
In a blender, purée the soup until smooth. Salt and pepper. Strain the soup through a sieve. Return to the saucepan. Add the cheese, whisking until melted.
Topping: Meanwhile, in a skillet over medium heat, brown the bacon in 5 ml (1 tsp) of the oil. Drain the bacon on paper towels.
In a bowl, combine the bacon, apple, chives and remaining oil.
Serve the soup in bowls. Top with the bacon mixture and drizzle with a little olive oil, if desired.

7861.title: Chocolate Religieuses
instructions: Light Chocolate Cream: In a pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar and cornstarch. Add the egg yolks and stir to combine. Stir in the milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the pan until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat. Strain through a sieve to remove any lumps, if necessary. Stir in the chocolate until it has melted and the mixture is smooth.
Pour the chocolate pastry cream into a bowl. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap. Let cool, then refrigerate for 2 hours or until completely chilled.
Choux Puffs: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Transfer the choux pastry to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) plain tip. On a baking sheet, pipe 12 balls of dough 2.5 cm (1 inch) in diameter, spacing them apart.
Bake for 25 minutes or until the puffs are cooked and golden brown. Let cool completely on the baking sheet.
On the second baking sheet, pipe 12 balls of dough 5 cm (2 inches) in diameter, spacing them apart.
Bake for 25 minutes or until the puffs are cooked and golden brown. Turn the oven off, prop the door ajar with a wooden spoon and let sit for 30 minutes. Let cool completely on the baking sheet.
Ganache: Place the chocolate in a bowl.

In a small saucepan, bring the cream to a boil. Pour the cream over the chocolate and let stand for 1 minute without stirring. Using a spatula, stir until the ganache is smooth and the chocolate has melted. Stir in the butter. Set aside at room temperature.

Assembly: Whisk the chocolate pastry cream to make it smooth again. In another bowl, whip the cream with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Transfer a third of the cream to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) star tip. With the tip, pierce the bottom of the small puffs and fill them. Set aside on a plate.

Fold the remaining whipped cream into the chocolate pastry cream and mix until the light cream is smooth. Transfer the light chocolate cream to the same pastry bag with the star tip. With the tip, pierce the bottom of the large puffs and fill them.

Dip the tops of the large puffs in the ganache. Place the puffs on a serving plate as you go. Dip the tops of the small puffs in the ganache and set them on top of the large ones. Decorate with chocolate pearls or sprinkles, if desired.
Serve, or refrigerate until ready to serve. Cream puffs are always best the same day.

7882.title: Sake-ito
instructions: Preheat a barbecue to high and grill the pineapple wedge for 1 minute per side. Allow to cool.
In a glass, combine the sake, aloe or pineapple juice, lime juice and cane syrup. Add a few ice cubes and the lime wedges.
Garnish with the pineapple wedge and a sprig of Thai basil.

7884.title: Crunchy Quinoa, Cabbage, Radish and Feta Salad
instructions: In a pot of salted boiling water, cook the quinoa for 10 minutes or until tender. Drain, oil lightly and set aside.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, combine the cabbage, salt, sugar and 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the rice vinegar. Let marinate for 15 minutes.
Stir in the radishes, grapefruit, parsley, oil and remaining vinegar. Salt and pepper.
Divide the quinoa among the plates. Top with the cabbage mixture, then sprinkle with the cheese and pumpkin seeds. Drizzle with olive oil.
Perfect for lunch, or delicious as a side with roast chicken.

7885.title: Chorizo Coleslaw
instructions: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.

7886.title: Radish and Cucumber Pickles
instructions: Using a mandoline, cut the cucumbers into thin ribbons. Place in a bowl. Slice the radishes into rounds of the same thickness and add them to the cucumbers.
Add the vinegar and sugar. Stir to combine. Let macerate for 15 minutes at room temperature. Drain before serving.

7891.title: Salmon Burgers with Radish and Cucumber Pickles
instructions: Salmon Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a food processor, coarsely chop the salmon. Place in a bowl. Add the remaining ingredients and stir to combine. Salt and pepper.
With your hands, shape the fish mixture into 6 large patties. Place them on a large, oiled plated.
Grill the patties for 2 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Toast the hamburger buns, if desired.
Assembly: Spread the insides of the buns with chermoula. Place the patties on them and top with mayonnaise and the radish and cucumber pickles. Close the burgers.

7896.title: Red Curry Grilled Fish
instructions: In a skillet over medium heat, brown the shallots in the oil. Add the red curry paste, lime juice and brown sugar. Cook for 1 minute. Add the coconut milk and continue cooking until the sauce thickens slightly. Set aside.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
With the tip of a knife, make three long crosswise cuts in the skin on each side of the fish. Oil lightly.
Grill for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, or until the flesh flakes off the bone.
Serve the fish whole, topped with the sauce. Delicious with rice.

7906.title: Black Tea and Star Anise Quail
instructions: In a glass dish, combine the quails, 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the soy sauce and the paprika. Let marinate for 15 minutes. Drain.

In a cup, steep the tea in the water for 10 minutes. Strain through a sieve into a small saucepan. Add the remaining soy sauce and the remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Simmer for 6 to 8 minutes or until the sauce is syrupy. Keep the glaze warm.
Thread 2 skewers through each quail, from the thigh to the opposite breast, to form an X. Although optional, this step makes the quails easier to handle.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

Grill the quails skin side down for 5 minutes, then turn them over and continue cooking for 5 minutes. Brush the quails with half the glaze and cook for 1 minute per side or until well caramelized. Place on a large plate and brush with the remaining glaze.

7907.title: Grilled Vegetables and Tofu in Broth
instructions: Vegetables and Tofu: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

In a glass dish, combine the zucchini and green onions with the soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, oil and sambal oelek. Grill the vegetables for 1 minute per side or until golden. Return them to the dish and let cool slightly.
Stir in the remaining ingredients except the tofu.
Broth: In a small pot, bring all of the ingredients to a boil.
Pour the broth into shallow bowls. Divide the grilled vegetable mixture and tofu cubes among them.

7909.title: Miso-Glazed Eggplant
instructions: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium-high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine the miso, soy sauce, rice vinegar, water and maple syrup.
In another bowl, cover the green onion with cold water. Let soak for 10 minutes. Drain.

On a work surface, cut the eggplants in half lengthwise. With the tip of a knife, score the flesh in a crisscross pattern without piercing the skin. Lightly oil the eggplants. Lightly season with salt and pepper.

Grill the eggplants flesh side down for 3 minutes or until golden. Turn the eggplants over and brush them with the miso mixture. Close the lid and continue cooking for 2 minutes or until the eggplants are tender.
Place the eggplants on a serving plate. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and garnish with green onion.

7910.title: Bitter Greens and Green Apple Salad
ingredients: bitter lettuce such as escarole or frisée
instructions: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Salt and pepper. Delicious with the croque-madame.

7911.title: Croque-Madame
instructions: Béchamel Sauce: In a saucepan over medium heat, cook the onion in the butter until translucent. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Whisk in the milk. Bring to a boil. Add the nutmeg. Salt and pepper. Simmer over medium-low heat for 5 minutes or until the sauce thickens, stirring often so it doesn't stick to the bottom of the saucepan.
Filling: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place 4 slices of bread side by side on the baking sheet. Spread each slice with 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the béchamel sauce. Top with the ham slices, then half the cheese (75 g/3/4 cup). Close the sandwiches. Spread the remaining béchamel and the remaining cheese on top. Bake for 15 minutes until lightly browned.

Meanwhile, in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, melt the butter. Gently crack the eggs into the skillet and cook on one side only for 2 to 3 minutes or until the whites are set and the edges are lightly golden. Salt and pepper.
Using a spatula, place an egg on each toasted sandwich. Serve with the bitter greens and green apple salad.

7926.title: Jar Lid Tartlet
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Turn the disk over inside the ring, metal side up.
On a lightly floured work surface, roll out the dough into a 10 cm (4 inch) circle. Place the dough in the lid and set the lid on a baking sheet. Prick the bottom of the dough with a fork.
Bake for 25 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown. Let cool completely.
In a bowl, combine the fruit and sugar. Let rest for 5 minutes.
When ready to serve, spread the yogurt in the bottom of the tartlet and top with the fruit.

7927.title: Pecan “Pets-de-Sœur” Rolls
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

On a lightly floured work surface, roll out dough into a 15-cm (6-inch) square. Spread the butter over the entire surface. Sprinkle with brown sugar and scatter the pecans over it, pressing them into the dough.

Using a knife, cut the dough into 4 triangles. Roll up each triangle, starting from the wide side and ending at the tip. Place the rolls on the baking sheet, tip side down. Using a brush, brush with milk.
Bake for 20 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown. Let cool.

7928.title: Soy Caramel
instructions: In a saucepan over medium heat, bring all the ingredients to a boil. Simmer for 10 minutes or until the sauce is syrupy.

7929.title: Beef Short Ribs with Soy Caramel
ingredients: kecap manis or homemade soy caramel
instructions: In a large bowl, combine 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the kecap, the pineapple, fish sauce and oil. Add the meat and coat well. Let marinate for 15 minutes. Discard the pineapple cubes.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium-high. Oil the grate.
Grill the meat for 5 minutes per side or until pink in the centre. Set aside on a large plate.
Top the short ribs with the remaining kecap. Garnish with fried onions and chives.

7931.title: Seafood-Free Paella
instructions: In a large saucepan, bring the broth, tomato paste and paprika to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes. Add saffron. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

In a large paella pan or large non-stick skillet over high heat, brown the chicken in the oil. Salt and pepper. Add the onion and garlic. Cook for 1 minute. Add the peppers and chorizo. Salt and pepper. Continue cooking for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the rice and stir to combine. Add the white wine and cook for 1 minute. Add the broth and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes without stirring.
Arrange the artichokes on top. Continue cooking for 15 minutes or until the rice is cooked but still slightly firm and the broth is thick but not completely absorbed.
Off the heat, add the peas. Cover and let rest for 3 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges.

7937.title: Cucumbers with Seasoned Salt
ingredients: kosher salt or coarse sea salt
instructions: In a spice grinder or a mortar, crush all the ingredients except the nori sheet and cucumbers. Add the nori sheet.
Sprinkle the cucumbers with the seasoned salt, to taste. The seasoned salt keeps for 1 month in an airtight container at room temperature.

7954.title: “Mojito” Cake
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F). Line the bottoms of three 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans with parchment paper. Do not butter the pans.
In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk together the egg yolks with 105 g (1/2 cup) of the sugar, the oil, lime zest and juice, salt and 1 drop of green food colouring. Set aside.
In a third bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add 1/2 cup (105 g) of the sugar and continue beating until stiff peaks form.

Add the dry ingredients to the egg yolk mixture to form the batter. Stir a quarter of the meringue into the batter. Using a spatula or a whisk, gently fold in the remaining meringue. Pour a third of the batter into one pan.
Add 2 drops of green food colouring to the remaining batter and mix well. Pour half the batter into a pan.
Add 2 drops of green food colouring to the remaining batter and mix well. Pour half the batter into a pan.
