Bake for 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Remove from the oven and immediately place them upside down on a wire rack. Let cool completely, about 2 hours. Run the blade of a knife between the cakes and pans, then unmould.

Frosting: Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, bring the milk and mint to a boil. Remove from the heat. Crush the mint in the milk with a wooden spoon. Cover and let steep for 10 minutes. Strain through a sieve, pressing on the mint.

In the same saucepan over medium heat, melt 55 g (1/4 cup) of the butter. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the mint milk and bring to a boil, whisking. Simmer for 1 minute, stirring.
Pour into a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool completely at room temperature, about 1 hour.
Add the sugar, lime zest and remaining butter and beat with an electric mixer for 5 minutes or until the frosting is smooth and creamy. Stir in the rum.
Syrup: In a blender, coarsely blend all the ingredients. Strain into a bowl.
Assembly: Cut and remove the crown of each cake. Using a brush, soak the cakes with the syrup.

Spread 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the frosting on each cake layer and stack them on a serving plate, from darkest to lightest. Cover the cake with a thin layer of frosting to trap the crumbs. Refrigerate for 15 minutes. Cover the cake completely with the remaining frosting. Top the cake with lime wedges and mint leaves. The cake will keep for 2 or 3 days, covered, at room temperature.

8066.title: Raspberry Cranberry Muffins
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line 12 muffin cups with paper or silicone liners.
In a bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal and baking powder. Set aside.

In another bowl, whisk together the eggs, sugar and oil. Stir in the dry ingredients. Add the yogurt and mix until the batter is smooth. Gently stir in the raspberries and cranberries. Spoon the batter into the prepared pans.

Bake for 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of a muffin comes out clean. Let cool on a wire rack. The muffins keep for 3 days in an airtight container at room temperature. Serve with plain yogurt, if desired.

8070.title: Cream of Potato Soup with Pancetta and Hazelnuts
instructions: Cream of Potato Soup: In a large pot over medium heat, soften the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the pancetta and continue cooking for 5 minutes or until the onion starts to brown. Add the potatoes, broth and milk. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. Add the parsley.
In a blender, purée the soup until smooth. Salt and pepper. Strain through a sieve.
Topping: Meanwhile, in a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the pancetta in the oil. Drain on paper towels.
In a bowl, combine the pancetta, hazelnuts, croutons and parsley.
Serve the soup in bowls. Top with the pancetta mixture and drizzle with a little olive oil, if desired.

8071.title: Almond Praline Cream Puffs
instructions: Craquelin: In a bowl, mix all the ingredients until the dough is smooth. Between two sheets of parchment paper, roll out the dough to a thickness of 3 mm (1/8 inch) and freeze for 30 minutes.

Remove the paper from the top. Using a 4 cm (1 1/2 inch) round cookie cutter, cut 10 circles from the craquelin dough. Using a 1.5 cm (3/4 inch) round cookie cutter, cut 20 circles from the craquelin dough. Keep in the freezer while you prepare the cream and the puffs.

Almond Praline Cream: In a pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar and cornstarch. Add the egg yolks and stir to combine. Stir in the milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the pan until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat.
Pour the pastry cream into a bowl. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap. Let cool, then refrigerate until completely chilled, about 2 hours.
Choux Puffs: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

Transfer the choux pastry to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) plain tip. On the baking sheet, pipe 10 balls of dough 4 cm (1 1/2 inches) in diameter, spacing them apart. Then pipe 20 small balls 1 cm (1/2 inch) in diameter, attaching them on either side of the large balls.
Place the craquelin disks (small and large) on the balls of dough (small and large).
Bake for 25 minutes or until the puffs are cooked and golden brown. Turn the oven off, prop the door ajar with a wooden spoon and let sit for 30 minutes. Let cool completely on the baking sheet.

Assembly: Beat the pastry cream with an electric mixer to make it smooth again. Stir in the almond butter. In another bowl, whip the cream until stiff peaks form. Using a spatula, fold the whipped cream into the praline cream. Transfer to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) star tip.
Using a bread knife, cut the puffs in half horizontally. Sprinkle the bottoms with half the almonds, fill with the almond praline cream, then finish with the remaining almonds. Close the choux.
Serve, or refrigerate until ready to serve. Cream puffs are always best the same day.

8072.title: Saint-Honoré
instructions: Light Vanilla Cream: In a small pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar and cornstarch. Add the egg yolks and mix well. Stir in the milk and vanilla seeds. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the pan until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat. Add the butter and stir until smooth.
Pour the pastry cream into a bowl. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap. Let cool, then refrigerate for 2 hours or until completely chilled.
Meanwhile, place the rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line two baking sheets with silicone mats or parchment paper.

Roll out the puff pastry into a 25 cm (10-inch) square. Cut out a 25 cm (10 inch) circle using a pan or a plate of the same size. Place the pastry circle on the first baking sheet. Prick the pastry with a fork.
Bake for 25 minutes or until the puff pastry is cooked and golden. Let cool completely on the baking sheet. Reduce the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Transfer the choux pastry to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) plain tip. On the second baking sheet, pipe 16 balls of dough 2.5 cm (1 inch) in diameter, spacing them apart.
Bake for 25 minutes or until the puffs are golden brown. Remove from the oven and let cool completely on the baking sheet.
Assembly: In a bowl, whip the cream and icing sugar with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Keep half the whipped cream in the refrigerator.

Stir the pastry cream with a spatula to make it smooth again. Fold in the remaining whipped cream. Transfer two thirds of the light vanilla cream to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) star tip. With the tip, pierce the bottom of the puffs and fill them. Set aside on a plate. Spread the remaining light vanilla cream over the entire surface of the puff pastry.
In a small saucepan, bring the sugar, corn syrup and water to a boil. Cook without stirring until the caramel is an amber colour. Remove from the heat.

Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat. Dip the tops of the filled puffs, one at a time, in the hot caramel. Careful, the caramel is extremely hot. Place the puffs, caramel side down, on the baking sheet. Allow to cool.
Place the puff pastry on a serving plate. Spoon the reserved whipped cream into the centre. Arrange the puffs, caramel side up, around the edge of the pastry, then place one puff in the centre.
Serve, or refrigerate until ready to serve. The Saint-Honoré is best the day it is made.

8081.title: Sherry-Braised Pork Cheeks
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In an ovenproof Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat, brown the cheeks in the butter. Salt and pepper. Turn the cheeks over, then add the bacon. Set the meat aside on a plate. Keep the fat in the Dutch oven.

Place the carrots and onion in the Dutch oven. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Deglaze with the sherry and let reduce for 30 seconds. Add the broth. Return the meat and bacon to the pot and bring to a boil. Cover and bake for 3 hours or until the cheeks are tender, turning them halfway through.
In a pot of boiling salted water, cook the pappardelle until al dente. Set aside 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the cooking water. Drain. Toss the pasta with oil and season with salt and pepper.

Remove the pork cheeks from the Dutch oven and set aside on a plate. Using a fork, shred the meat and return it to the sauce. Add pasta cooking water as needed to loosen the sauce. Toss about 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the sauce with the pasta.
Serve the meat, vegetables and sauce over the pappardelle. Garnish with the basil.

8082.title: Roasted Garlic Pork Belly
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 265 °F (130 °C).
Using a sharp knife, score the fat on the surface of the belly in a crisscross pattern without cutting into the meat.
On a work surface, mash the garlic with the salt and pepper using the flat side of a chef's knife until it forms a paste. Rub the garlic paste over the meat, except on the fat side.

Place the belly in an ovenproof non-stick skillet, fat side down. Add the wine. Bake for 4 hours 30 minutes. Halfway through, the wine will have completely evaporated. At the end of cooking, the meat will be very tender and the fat crisp.
The pork belly can be served hot or cold, on a charcuterie platter or in tacos.

8083.title: Pork Belly, Fennel and Pineapple Tacos
ingredients: thin slices of roasted garlic pork belly
instructions: Fennel salad: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Tacos: Soak the onion in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes. Drain. Add the lime juice. Set aside.

In a non-stick skillet over medium heat, warm the tortillas in a little oil. Using a fork, mash 1/6 of an avocado on each tortilla. Top with the fennel salad and 2 slices of pork belly. Add the pickled onions, chili pepper, pineapple and a little cilantro. Serve with a lime wedge.

8091.title: Smoked Trout, Yogurt and Herb Crackers
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the yogurt and horseradish. Salt and pepper.
Place the trout slices on the crackers. Top with the yogurt mixture and the herbs.

8134.title: “Prunetella” (Hazelnut Prune Spread)
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring the prunes and water to a boil. Simmer for 1 minute so the prunes plump up with water.

In a food processor, purée the hot prunes with the cooking water, hazelnut butter and maple syrup until smooth. Add water if the mixture is too firm, as needed. Transfer to an airtight container. Let cool and refrigerate for 3 hours or until completely chilled.
Delicious with apple wedges, cheese or on toast. The “prunetella” keeps for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.

8136.title: Prune Far Breton
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Generously butter a 20 cm (8 inch) square pan.

In a small saucepan, bring the prunes and rum to a boil. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes or until 30 ml (2 tbsp) of liquid remains. Drain the prunes, keeping the cooking liquid. Spread the prunes evenly over the bottom of the pan.

In a bowl, combine the flour and sugar. Add the eggs and whisk until the batter is smooth. Gradually add the milk, then the vanilla and the prune cooking liquid. Pour the milk mixture over the prunes.
Bake for 25 minutes or until the mixture has completely set. Let cool slightly on a rack, then refrigerate for 2 hours or until the far is completely cold. Unmould. Cut and serve.

8144.title: Tomato Ricotta Tartlets
instructions: Crust: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together the oil, mustard, salt, chili flakes and egg. Add the breadcrumbs and mix until just moistened.

Divide the mixture among 6 oiled tartlet pans with removable bottoms, about 10 cm (4 inches) in diameter, and press it into the bottoms and up the sides. Place on a baking sheet. Bake for 20 minutes or until the crust is golden. Let cool completely on a wire rack. Unmould and place on a plate.
Topping: Place the ricotta in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and mix well. Spoon into the crusts.
In another bowl, gently toss the tomatoes with the remaining ingredients. Salt and pepper. Top the tartlets with the tomato mixture.

8155.title: Chocolate Cherry Bread Pudding
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper. Butter a 20 cm (8 inch) square pan, 5 cm (2 inches) deep.
Spread the bread cubes on the baking sheet. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until the bread starts to dry out (without browning). Let cool slightly.

In a large bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, sugar and vanilla. Add the chocolate milk. Stir in the toasted bread cubes, chocolate and cherries, mixing gently to coat the bread well with the egg mixture. Let soak for 30 minutes. Pour the mixture into the pan.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes or until the pudding is slightly puffed and golden. Let cool slightly before serving.

8181.title: Breaded Pork Cutlets with Red Endive Salad
instructions: Salad: In a large bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Pork: On a work surface, place the chops between two sheets of plastic wrap and flatten them to 5 mm (1/4 inch) with a mallet or a rolling pin. Salt and pepper.
In a shallow dish, place the flour. In a second shallow dish, lightly beat the eggs. In a third shallow dish, place the breadcrumbs.
Dredge the chops in flour. Shake to remove any excess. Dip the pork in the eggs and let the excess drip off. Press into the breadcrumbs to coat well. Set aside on a plate.

In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, heat the butter and oil. Cook the chops one at a time for 4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on paper towels. Serve with the salad and lemon wedges.

8192.title: Warm Pork Tenderloin, Beet and Orange Salad
instructions: Place the beets in a saucepan and cover with water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium-low heat for 45 minutes or until tender. Cool under cold water and drain. Peel and cut into thin wedges. Set aside.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the garlic, ginger, salt and pepper. Add the pork and coat thoroughly. Let marinate for 10 minutes.

In an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat, brown the pork tenderloins in the oil. Roast for 10 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the meat reads 57 °C (135 °F). Place on a plate and let rest for 20 minutes. On a work surface, thinly slice the pork tenderloins.
In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise, horseradish, mustard and lemon juice.
On a large serving platter, arrange the beets, beans and oranges. Top with the mayonnaise mixture. Sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds and chives. Add in the meat.

8207.title: One-Pan Gnocchi in Tomato Sauce
ingredients: fresh basil, stem and leaves separated
instructions: In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes without letting it brown. Add the water and continue cooking for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, strained tomatoes and basil stem. Cover with a splatter screen and continue cooking for 15 minutes, stirring a few times (if you don't have a splatter screen, use a high-sided pot). Salt and pepper.

Place the gnocchi in the sauce. Cover and cook for 2 minutes. Turn them in the sauce and scatter the bocconcini over them. Cover again and cook for 2 minutes or until the gnocchi are cooked and the cheese has melted. Sprinkle with the basil leaves and Parmesan shavings, if desired.

8214.title: Port-Roasted Leg of Lamb
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F).
In a small bowl, combine the jam, port and mustard. Set aside.
On a work surface, untie the leg of lamb and open it flat, fat side up. With the tip of a knife, score the fat in a crisscross pattern. Season with salt on all sides.

In a Dutch oven over medium-high heat, brown the meat, fat side down, in the oil until crisp, 2 to 3 minutes. Turn the meat over and continue cooking for 2 minutes. Add the onions and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes or until golden. Turn the leg fat side up. Deglaze with the jam mixture. Bring to a boil.
Cover and bake for 2 hours, basting the meat halfway through. Remove the lid and continue cooking for 30 minutes or until the meat is tender and the juices have reduced slightly.
Delicious with mashed potatoes and roasted root vegetables.

8222.title: Lemon Cranberry Vodka
instructions: Place the ice cubes and cranberries in a whisky glass (lowball). Add the cranberry juice and lemon vodka and top up with sparkling water.

8223.title: Yogurt with Carrot Jam
instructions: In a small saucepan over medium-high heat, bring the orange juice, sugar, carrot and cardamom to a boil, stirring. Simmer for 5 minutes or until the jam is syrupy. Let cool completely.
Divide the jam among 6 airtight containers. Add the yogurt. Serve or refrigerate. The yogurt jars keep for 1 week in the refrigerator.

8245.title: Scallops with Edamame Hummus and Grapefruit Salad
instructions: Edamame Hummus: In a pot of boiling salted water, cook the edamame for 7 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold running water.

In a food processor, finely grind the edamame and cilantro with the lime juice, tahini and sambal oelek. Add the oil and water. Process until smooth. Salt and pepper. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed. The hummus keeps for 1 week in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

Scallops: In a non-stick skillet over high heat, brown one side of the scallops well in the oil for 3 minutes. Turn them over and continue cooking for 1 to 2 minutes to the desired doneness. Salt and pepper. Transfer to a plate.
Grapefruit Salad: In a bowl, gently toss all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread 30 ml (2 tbsp) of hummus on each plate. Top with the scallops and grapefruit salad.

8246.title: Banana with Caramelized Sesame
instructions: Place the banana in a bowl and drizzle with the juice of the lime wedge. Sprinkle with the sesame wafers.

8250.title: Vegetable Demi-Glace
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

On a non-stick baking sheet, toss the vegetables with the oil. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring twice, or until the vegetables are well browned. Remove from the oven. Add the tomato paste and mix thoroughly. Continue roasting for 3 to 5 minutes or until the tomato paste is well caramelized.

Place the roasted vegetable mixture in a saucepan. Deglaze the baking sheet with the wine, scraping the bottom well to collect all the caramelized juices. Pour the purée back into the pan. Add the broth, spices and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer until the broth has reduced by half and the demi-glace coats the back of a spoon, about 20 minutes. Stir in the nutritional yeast until dissolved. Strain through a sieve. Adjust the seasoning.
Use the demi-glace in the recipe of your choice, such as onion soup or sauces. The demi-glace keeps for 2 weeks in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

8256.title: Slow Cooker Vegetable Soup with Cheese Curds
instructions: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, soften the vegetables in the oil for 10 minutes, stirring a few times. Transfer to the slow cooker. Add the broth, beans, tomatoes, bay leaf and thyme. Salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low for 4 hours (see note). It can be maintained on Warm for up to 6 hours. Remove the bay leaf and thyme sprig.
Add the kale and parsley. Mix well. Place the cheese curds in bowls. Pour in the hot soup. Serve with bread, if desired.

8259.title: Victoria Sponge Cake
instructions: Whipped Cream: In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over the water. Let bloom for 5 minutes.
Add 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the cream to the gelatin mixture and heat in the microwave 30 seconds at a time or until the gelatin has completely dissolved.
In another bowl, combine the remaining cream, the sugar and the gelatin. Refrigerate for 3 hours or until the chocolate cream has completely chilled.
Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line the bottoms of two 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans with parchment paper. Do not butter the pans.
In a bowl, combine the flour with the baking powder and salt.
In a large bowl, whisk together the egg yolks with 105 g (1/2 cup) of the sugar, the cream and the vanilla. Stir in the dry ingredients.

In a third bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add the remaining sugar (105 g/1/2 cup), beating until stiff peaks form. Stir a quarter of the meringue into the batter. With a spatula, gently fold in the remaining meringue. Spoon the batter into the prepared pans.
Bake for 25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Turn the pans upside down on a rack and let cool completely. Unmould.

Jam: Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, bring the raspberries and sugar to a boil. Simmer over medium-low heat for 10 minutes or until the jam coats the back of a spoon and is syrupy. Transfer to a bowl. Let cool. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour or until the jam is completely cold.
Assembly: In a bowl, whip the cold cream with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.

Place one of the cakes upside down on a serving plate so the bottom of the cake faces up. Spread the jam over it, then the whipped cream. Top with the second cake, domed side up. Refrigerate for 1 hour. Dust with icing sugar. The cake keeps for 2 days under a cake dome in the refrigerator.

8260.title: Trout Escabeche with Fennel Salad
instructions: Trout Escabeche: Place the trout pieces in a 20 cm (8 inch) square glass dish.

Using a mortar and pestle, coarsely crush the coriander, cumin and fennel seeds with the peppercorns. Place in a small saucepan with the remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil. Gently pour the boiling mixture over the fish. Let cool for 30 minutes. Cover and refrigerate for 4 hours or overnight. Remove the trout pieces from the marinade. Strain the marinade through a sieve. Discard the aromatics. Keep the marinade for the fennel salad. Once removed from the marinade, the trout keeps for 2 days in the refrigerator.
Quick Sour Cream: In a small bowl, combine the cream and vinegar. Salt and pepper. Let stand for 5 minutes, until the cream thickens.
Salad: In another bowl, combine all the ingredients. Add 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the escabeche marinade. Adjust the seasoning.
Divide the salad among four plates and serve. Place the trout pieces on top. Drizzle with the quick sour cream, to taste.

8262.title: Flank Steak with Maître d'Hôtel Butter
instructions: Maître d'Hôtel Butter: In a bowl, using a spatula, mix the butter with the remaining ingredients. Salt and pepper.

Lay a sheet of plastic wrap on a slightly moistened work surface. Spread the butter along one end of the plastic wrap. Roll up into a log about 2.5 cm (1 inch) in diameter. Close the log by twisting both ends of the plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 2 hours or until the butter is firm.

Flank Steak: In a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the meat in the oil and butter for 3 minutes per side for rare. Salt and pepper. Transfer to a plate and let rest for 5 minutes. Slice and divide among the plates.

Remove the plastic wrap from the butter. Using a hot knife, cut the butter into rounds of the desired thickness. Keep the remaining broccoli for another use. Place on the meat and sprinkle with fleur de sel. Serve with the herbed green salad.

8263.title: Herbed Green Salad
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the lettuce and herbs. Add the oil and vinegar. Season with salt and pepper and mix well. Serve immediately.
Serve with the flank steak.

8274.title: Pork and Cassis Terrine
instructions: In a skillet over medium heat, soften the onion and garlic in the oil until they start to brown. Deglaze with the rum and reduce until dry. Allow to cool.

Fit the meat grinder with the coarsest plate for a coarse grind. Place a large bowl under the grinder. Feed a few cubes of belly and butt at a time into the grinder, pressing them down with the pusher (see note).
On a work surface, chop the pork liver with a chef's knife. Add it to the bowl of ground meat.
Using a mortar and pestle, finely grind the peppercorns and juniper berries with the salt. Add to the meat with the crème de cassis, blackcurrants, egg and onion mixture. Shake vigorously.

Fill a terrine mould or loaf pan of about 750 ml (3 cups) with the mixture in three layers, pressing lightly to remove the air from each layer. Using a spatula, round the top. Place the bay leaf on top. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Refrigerate for 8 hours or overnight.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Remove the plastic wrap, then place the terrine mould in a baking dish. Pour boiling water into the dish halfway up the sides of the mould.

Bake for 1 hour 10 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the terrine reads 74 °C (165 °F). Remove the mould from the water and let cool slightly on a rack. Cover and refrigerate for 12 hours.
Cut the terrine into slices. Serve with croutons, sour pickles and Dijon mustard, if desired. The terrine keeps for 1 week, tightly wrapped in plastic wrap, in the refrigerator.

8276.title: Italian Anise Cookies (Ciambelline all'Anice)
instructions: In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder.

In another bowl, stir the wine and 55 g (1/4 cup) of the sugar until the sugar has dissolved, about 1 minute. Add the oil, anise, vanilla, fennel and lemon zest. Stir to combine. Stir in the dry ingredients with a wooden spoon. The dough should form a smooth ball and be slightly sticky. Cover in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

Divide the dough into 16 equal pieces and shape them into balls. On a smooth surface, roll one piece at a time into a rope 1 cm (1/2 inch) in diameter and 20 cm (8 inches) long. Bring the two ends of the rope together, pressing them lightly against each other to form a loop.
Place the remaining sugar in a shallow dish. Gently place one cookie at a time in the sugar and coat it well. Place on the baking sheet, spacing them evenly.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until the cookies are golden. Let cool on the baking sheet.

8277.title: Kulfi Ice Cream Bars
instructions: Frozen Bars: In a small saucepan, bring the cream to a boil with 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the sugar and the cardamom. Remove from the heat. Cover and let steep for 5 minutes.
In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over the water. Let bloom for 5 minutes.

In another bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the remaining sugar. Pour the hot cream mixture over the yolks, whisking. Return to the saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the custard coats the back of a spoon. Remove from the heat. Add the gelatin, stirring until dissolved. Strain through a sieve into a bowl. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 8 hours or overnight.
Nougatine: Meanwhile, line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a small saucepan, bring the sugar and water to a boil. Cook without stirring until the caramel is an amber colour. Remove from the heat.
Add the nuts and stir to combine. Immediately spoon on the baking sheet. With a spatula, quickly spread the caramel. Let cool completely. On a work surface, coarsely chop the nougatine with a knife.
Assembly: Line a 20 cm (8 inch) square pan with parchment paper, letting it hang over all four sides.

With an electric mixer, whip the chilled cream until soft peaks form. Using a spatula, fold in the chopped nougatine. Pour into the prepared pan. Cover and freeze for 6 hours or until firm. Unmould. On a work surface, cut into bars and serve right away.

8280.title: Teff Molasses Cookies
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 180 °F (350 °C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the teff flour and baking powder.

In another bowl, combine the butter, molasses, ginger and spices. Heat in the microwave for 45 seconds. Whisk the mixture. Add the tahini, brown sugar and egg, then mix again. Stir in the flour mixture with a spatula, finishing with your hands, until the dough is smooth.
With a 2 tbsp (30 ml ) ice cream scoop, shape dough balls. Using your hands, roll into balls. Place on the baking sheet, spacing them out. Flatten slightly and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake for 12 minutes or until the edges of the cookies are slightly firm. Let cool.

8285.title: Indian-Style Pork (Vindaloo)
ingredients: boneless pork shoulder, trimmed of fat
instructions: Masala (Spice Mix): In a large bowl, combine all the ingredients.
Pork: Add the vinegar to the masala and mix. Add the meat and coat it well with the mixture. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 4 hours.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C).

In an ovenproof Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat, cook the onions in the butter until tender and golden, about 10 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes. Cook, stirring, until they start to break down. Add the pork and marinade, water, sugar, chili pepper, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil.

Cover and bake for 1 hour. Remove the lid. Stir and return to the oven, uncovered, for 1 hour or until the meat falls apart with a fork and the sauce has thickened. Let cool for 15 minutes before serving.
Serve with rice, naan bread or boiled potatoes and a green vegetable.

8286.title: Turbot Fillets Meunière
instructions: Pat the fish fillets dry with paper towels. Lightly oil them on each side. Salt and pepper.
Place the flour on a large plate. Dredge the fillets in the flour and shake off the excess.

In a large non-stick skillet over high heat, melt 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the butter with the remaining oil until it turns nut-brown. Cook the fillets on one side until golden brown, about 3 minutes. Gently turn them over and continue cooking for 1 minute. Set the fillets aside side by side on a serving plate.

In the same skillet over medium-high heat, melt the remaining butter until it stops foaming. It will turn nut-brown. Pour over the fillets. Drizzle with lemon juice. Serve with extra lemon wedges. Garnish with parsley leaves.

8296.title: Chocolate Mousse with Caramel Whipped Cream
instructions: Chocolate Mousse: In the top of a double boiler, off the heat, whisk the eggs and sugar. Set over a saucepan of simmering water and whisk constantly for 6 to 8 minutes or until the sugar has completely dissolved and the mixture is thick and creamy. Remove from the heat and add the chocolate. Let melt for 1 minute without stirring. Mix well. If the chocolate hasn't completely melted, set it over the simmering water again and melt the chocolate without overheating the mixture. Remove from the heat and let sit for 5 minutes.

With an electric mixer, whip the cream until stiff peaks form. Stir half the cream into the chocolate mixture. The cream should cool the mousse enough. Gently fold in the remaining cream with a spatula. Transfer to a large bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight.
Caramel Whipped Cream: In a saucepan over high heat, heat the brown sugar and water. Cook without stirring until the mixture caramelizes and starts to smoke slightly.

Remove the pan from the heat and add cream. Watch out for splattering. Return the saucepan to the heat and simmer over medium heat, stirring, until smooth. Pour into a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight.

When ready to serve, whip the caramel cream mixture with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Divide the chocolate mousse among dessert cups and top with the caramel whipped cream. Delicious with ladyfinger-style butter cookies or plain biscuits.

8300.title: White Bean Purée and Smoked Duck Canapés
ingredients: aged cheddar and harissa crackers (such as Lesley Stowe Raincoast)
instructions: In a small food processor, finely grind the beans, Parmesan, lemon juice, oil, water and harissa until smooth. Salt and pepper.
Spread the bean purée on the crackers. Top with the smoked duck and basil leaves.

8301.title: Fresh Goat Cheese and Roasted Grape Canapés
ingredients: Parmesan and chive crackers (such as Lesley Stowe Raincoast)
instructions: In a large skillet over medium heat, roast the grapes in 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the oil for 3 to 4 minutes or until they start to burst. Set aside and let cool completely.
In a small bowl, combine the remaining oil with the pumpkin seeds and curry powder. Heat in the microwave for 30 seconds.
Spread the goat cheese on the crackers. Top with the roasted grapes, pumpkin seeds, herbs and sprouts.

8302.title: Warm Roasted Vegetable and Kamut Salad with Kefir Dressing
instructions: Salad: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

In a pot of boiling salted water, cook the kamut with the baking soda over medium heat for 35 minutes or until the kamut is almost cooked but still quite crunchy. Add the eggs and continue cooking for 8 minutes. Drain the kamut and eggs. Rinse the kamut and plunge the eggs into cold water for 5 minutes. Peel and cut into wedges.

Meanwhile, on a non-stick baking sheet, toss the potatoes, celery root, parsnip, carrots and shallots with the oil. Salt and pepper. Roast for 30 minutes or until the vegetables are tender and golden, stirring halfway through.
Dressing: In a bowl, blend all the ingredients with a whisk. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide the roasted vegetables, kamut and watercress among the plates. Top with the hard-boiled egg wedges and drizzle with the dressing.

8303.title: Buttered Lemon Cabbage with Sausages
ingredients: sausages such as knackwurst, weisswurst, boudin blanc, etc.
instructions: In a large bowl, massage the cabbage with the lemon juice and salt with your hands for 2 minutes. Let stand for 15 minutes, stirring from time to time. Drain and discard the liquid.

In a large pot over medium-high heat, soften onion in butter. Add the cabbage and apple. Continue cooking for 5 minutes, stirring frequently. Add the wine and spices. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring a few times during cooking. Arrange the sausages and kielbasa on the cabbage. Cover and continue cooking for 10 minutes.
Serve the cabbage and sausages with whole-grain mustard and steamed potatoes.

8306.title: Herb Butter
instructions: Place all the ingredients in a jar of about 1 litre (4 cups). Close to seal.
Shake vigorously until the butter separates from the water, about 10 minutes.
Drain the butter. Serve on grilled meats.

8352.title: Pineapple Elderflower Iced Tea
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring 500 ml (2 cups) of the water to a boil.
Off the heat, add the tea bags and let steep for 5 minutes. Remove the tea bags without squeezing them too much.
Pour into a pitcher with the remaining ingredients except the ice cubes. Refrigerate for 12 hours or overnight. Serve with ice.

8355.title: Chili Nachos
ingredients: leftover homemade or store-bought cheese sauce
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place half the chips on the baking sheet. Top with half the chili and cheese sauce. Cover with the remaining chips, then the chili and cheese sauce.
Bake for 10 minutes or until the cheese sauce is lightly browned.
As soon as it comes out of the oven, sprinkle with the remaining ingredients. Serve with lime wedges, sour cream and salsa, if desired.

8356.title: Chili Dogs to Share
instructions: Chili: In a saucepan over medium-high heat, cook the meat in the oil, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Add the onion and garlic. Continue cooking until the vegetables and meat are browned. Salt and pepper. Add the remaining ingredients and simmer for 20 minutes or until the chili thickens. Keep warm until ready to serve.

Cheese Sauce: In another saucepan off the heat, combine the cheese with the cornstarch and chili powder. Add the evaporated milk and sambal oelek. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the saucepan, until the mixture thickens, about 10 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Assembly: Cut the baguettes in half horizontally without separating them completely. Warm them slightly.

Spread a quarter of the cheese sauce inside each baguette. Arrange the merguez sausages, overlapping them. Spread the chili, then the remaining cheese sauce, in each baguette. Sprinkle with the green onions. Close the bread, then cut into pieces.

8362.title: Spinach Sour Cream Dip
instructions: In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, soften the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the spinach and continue cooking for 30 seconds or until just wilted. Salt and pepper. Drain on paper towels. Let cool.
In a bowl, combine the cream cheese and sour cream. Stir in the spinach mixture. Adjust the seasoning. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 1 hour or until the dip is completely cold.
Serve with raw vegetables or crackers.

8392.title: Chicken Skewers with Barbecue Peanuts
ingredients: skinless and boneless chicken breast halves
instructions: On a work surface, cut the chicken breast in half through its thickness, then cut each half into long strips about 5 mm (1/4 inch) thick.

In a bowl, combine the brown sugar, soy sauce, oil, vinegar, ginger and garlic powder. Season with pepper. Add the chicken and mix well to coat it with the marinade. Cover and let macerate for at least 12 hours or overnight in the refrigerator. Drain the chicken and discard the marinade.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium-high. Oil the grate.
Thread the chicken onto skewers in a zigzag. Grill the skewers for 2 to 3 minutes per side, turning them with tongs. Place on a serving dish.
Drizzle the honey over the chicken and sprinkle with the peanuts. Serve with lime wedges, to taste.

8411.title: Chocolate Meringue Cookies
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line two baking sheets with silicone mats or parchment paper.
In a bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add half the sugar (130 g/1 cup) and keep beating until stiff peaks form.
Sift the cocoa and the remaining sugar over the bowl of meringue. Add the chocolate and combine. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Using a 15 ml (1 tbsp) ice cream scoop, shape cookies and place them on the baking sheets, spacing them apart.
Bake one sheet at a time for 8 minutes or until the cookies crackle, with crisp edges and a centre that is still soft. Let cool completely on the baking sheet.

8412.title: Vanilla Sheet Cake with Raspberry Topping
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a 43 x 30 cm (17 x 12 inch) rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides. Butter the paper and the unlined sides.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt.

In another bowl, beat the eggs and sugar with an electric mixer for 10 minutes until the mixture triples in volume and forms a ribbon as it falls from the beaters. Sift the dry ingredients over the egg mixture and gently fold in using a whisk. Spread the batter evenly on the prepared sheet.

Bake for 15 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cake comes out clean. As soon as it comes out of the oven, sprinkle the top of the cake with sugar. Let cool completely in the pan, about 1 hour.
Coulis: In a blender, purée the raspberries and sugar until smooth. Strain through a sieve. Set aside.
Assembly: In a bowl, whip the cream with the sugar and vanilla using an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.

Sprinkle a large cutting board with 15 ml (1 tbsp) of sugar. Turn the cake out onto the board. Remove the parchment paper from the top. Spread three quarters of the coulis over the cake. Spread the whipped cream over the coulis, then top with the fresh raspberries. Finish with the remaining coulis.

8413.title: Honey Jalapeño Syrup
instructions: In a small pot over medium heat, bring all of the ingredients to a boil. Let simmer for 5 minutes. Strain.
Pour into an airtight container. Let cool, cover and refrigerate. The honey jalapeño syrup keeps for 1 month in the refrigerator.

8424.title: Strawberry, Cucumber and Feta Salad
instructions: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.

8425.title: “Neapolitan” Cake
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter the sides of three 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans and line the bottoms with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.

In another bowl, cream the butter and sugar with an electric mixer. Add the eggs, one at a time, and beat until smooth. On low speed, add the dry ingredients alternately with the buttermilk and vinegar.

Divide the cake batter among 3 bowls. Add the vanilla to the first bowl and mix well. Add the strawberries and red food colouring to the second bowl and mix well. In a small bowl, dissolve the cocoa in the water, then stir it into the third bowl of batter. Spread the batters evenly in the pans. If you don't have 3 springform pans, cover the batter with plastic wrap and keep it at room temperature while you bake the cakes one at a time. Let each cake cool for 15 minutes before unmoulding. Wash and dry the pans well before continuing with the remaining batter.
Bake together for 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Let cool completely on a wire rack, about 2 hours. Unmould.

Frosting: Meanwhile, in a small saucepan over medium heat, melt 55 g (1/4 cup) of the butter. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the strawberry purée. Bring to a boil, stirring with a whisk. Simmer gently for 1 minute, stirring.
Pour into a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool completely at room temperature, about 1 hour.
Add the sugar and the remaining butter. Whip using an electric mixer until creamy and smooth, about 5 minutes. Set aside 45 ml (3 tbsp) of the strawberry frosting for decoration.
Ganache: Place the chocolate in a bowl.

In a small saucepan, bring the cream to a boil. Remove from the heat and pour over the chocolate. Allow to melt for 1 minute without stirring. With a whisk, stir until the ganache is smooth. Let cool at room temperature until set. Set aside 45 ml (3 tbsp) of the ganache for decoration.
Assembly: Cut and remove the crown of each cake.

Place the chocolate cake on a serving plate. Spread the remaining ganache over it, then cover with 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the frosting. Top with the strawberry cake, then spread 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the frosting over it. Top with the vanilla cake. Cover the cake completely with the remaining frosting. Using an ice cream scoop, shape scoops of the reserved ganache and strawberry frosting and place them on the cake. Finish with an ice cream cone. The cake keeps for 2 to 3 days under a cake dome in the refrigerator.

8441.title: Mango Cake
instructions: Curd: In a saucepan off the heat, combine the sugar and cornstarch with a whisk. Add the eggs, egg yolks, mango purée and lemon juice. Stir to combine. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the saucepan, until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat. Stir in the butter until smooth. Strain, if needed.
Pour into a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool slightly and refrigerate for 4 hours or until the curd is completely cold.
Cake: Meanwhile, place the rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F). Line the bottoms of two 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans with parchment paper. Do not butter the pans.
In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Set aside.
In another bowl, whisk together the egg yolks with 105 g (1/2 cup) of the sugar, the oil, milk and salt. Set aside.
In a third bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add the remaining sugar, beating until stiff peaks form.

Add the dry ingredients to the egg yolk mixture to form the batter. Stir a quarter of the meringue into the batter. Using a spatula or a whisk, gently fold in the remaining meringue. Spoon the batter into the prepared pans.

Bake for 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Remove from the oven and immediately place them upside down on a wire rack. Let cool completely, about 3 hours. Run the blade of a knife between the cakes and pans, then unmould.
Assembly: Cut and remove the crown of each cake. Halve each cake horizontally to obtain 4 layers.
Stir the curd with a spatula to soften it. Spread the curd over 3 cake layers and stack them on a serving plate.
In a bowl, whip the cream and sugar with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Cover the cake completely with a thin layer of whipped cream.

Divide the remaining cream among 3 bowls. Stir 1 drop of yellow food colouring into the first bowl of cream, and gradually increase the amount of colouring in the other two bowls so that the last one is close to the colour of a ripe mango.

Using a large offset spatula, spread the palest cream over the top of the cake, turning the cake to spread it evenly. Let it spill over the sides of the cake to create a band around the top third of the cake. Then add the middle colour, turning the cake to form another band of colour around the middle of the cake, the same width as the first. Finish with the darkest colour at the base of the cake. Refrigerate for 1 hour before serving. The cake keeps for 2 to 3 days under a cake dome in the refrigerator.

8442.title: Lactose-Free Orange Creamsicle Cake
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F). Line the bottoms of two 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans with parchment paper. Do not butter the pans.
In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk together the egg yolks with 105 g (1/2 cup) of the sugar, the oil, orange zest and juice, salt and orange food colouring. Set aside.
In a third bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add the remaining sugar, beating until stiff peaks form.
Stir the dry ingredients into the egg yolk mixture, then incorporate one-quarter of the meringue. Using a spatula, gently fold in the remaining meringue. Divide the batter between the prepared pans.

Bake for 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Remove from the oven and immediately place them upside down on a wire rack. Let cool completely, about 3 hours. Run the blade of a knife between the cakes and pans, then unmould.
Assembly: In a bowl, whip the cream and sugar with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.
Halve each cake horizontally to obtain 4 layers.

Spread the whipped cream over the cake layers and stack them on a serving plate. Using a large offset spatula, spread the cream that oozes out over the sides to cover the cake in a thin layer, like a naked cake.
Decorate the top of the cake with sugar sprinkles or orange zest, as you like. The cake keeps for 2 to 3 days under a cake dome in the refrigerator.

8443.title: Blueberry Cake
instructions: Cake: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter the sides of two 20 cm (8 inch) springform pans and line the bottoms with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, cream the butter and sugar with an electric mixer. Add the eggs, one at a time, and beat until smooth. At low speed, add the dry ingredients alternately with the milk and vanilla. Spoon the batter into the prepared pans.
Bake for 35 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cakes comes out clean. Let cool completely on a wire rack, about 3 hours. Unmould.

Frosting: Meanwhile, in a small saucepan over medium heat, melt 55 g (1/4 cup) of the butter. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the blueberry purée and lemon juice. Bring to a boil, stirring with a whisk. Simmer gently for 1 minute, stirring.
Pour into a bowl and cover the surface directly with plastic wrap. Let cool completely, about 1 hour.
Add the sugar and the remaining butter. Whip using an electric mixer until creamy and smooth, about 5 minutes. Set aside.

Compote: In a saucepan off the heat, combine the sugar and cornstarch. Add the blueberries and lemon juice. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes or until the mixture thickens. Pour the blueberry filling into a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool slightly, then refrigerate for 1 hour or until completely cold.
Assembly: Cut and remove the crown of each cake. Halve each cake horizontally to obtain 4 layers.

Place one cake layer on a serving plate, then spread 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the blueberry frosting over it, making a raised border to hold in the blueberry filling. Top with a third of the blueberry compote. Repeat with two more cake layers, stacking them one on top of the other. Place the last layer on top. Cover the cake completely with the remaining frosting. Refrigerate for 1 hour before serving. The cake keeps for 2 to 3 days under a cake dome in the refrigerator.

8445.title: Frozen Cassis Cocktail
instructions: Cassis Granita: In a flat airtight container of about 2 litres (8 cups), combine the water and crème de cassis. Cover and place in the freezer for 6 hours or until completely frozen.
Place 4 coupe glasses in the freezer 1 hour before serving.
Cocktail: In a small pitcher, combine all the ingredients except the flowers.
Using a fork, scrape the surface of the granita to break it into crystals.
Divide the cocktail among the chilled glasses, then the cassis granita. Decorate with edible flowers, if desired.

8446.title: Pork Terrine in Aspic
instructions: Pork Hocks: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Place all ingredients in a large pot. Bring to a boil. Cover and bake for 2 hour and 30 minutes.
Remove the meat from the Dutch oven. Let cool slightly on a plate. Shred the meat, taking care to remove the bones and fat. Strain the broth. Set the meat and broth aside separately.
Terrine: Meanwhile, in a pot of boiling salted water, cook the carrot for 20 minutes or until tender. Drain. Let cool. Cut into rounds 3 mm (1/8 inch) thick. Set aside.

In a small saucepan, sprinkle the gelatin over the water and let bloom for 5 minutes. Add the pork broth and bring to a boil, whisking until the gelatin has completely dissolved. Add the vinegar. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Line a 25 x 10 cm (10 x 4 inch) terrine mould or loaf pan with two layers of plastic wrap, letting it hang over each side.

Spread a third of the meat, carrots, broth and herbs in the mould. Repeat with the remaining ingredients to make 3 layers. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap and press lightly to even it out. Refrigerate for 6 hours.
Unmould the terrine. Slice and serve. The pork terrine in aspic keeps for 10 days in an airtight container in the refrigerator. It can be frozen.

8447.title: Grilled Cornish Hens with Fennel and Lemon
instructions: Hens: On a work surface, using a chef's knife or kitchen shears, cut out the backbone of the hens. Cut between the two breasts to get 4 half hens.
Sprinkle the hens with the salt and rub them with the cut side of the lemon. Oil the hens and coat them with the fennel fronds and chili pepper.
Preheat one side of the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

Lay the hens flat on the turned-off section of the barbecue, skin side down. Close the barbecue lid. Cook for 25 minutes. Turn the hens over and continue cooking for 10 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the thigh, without touching the bone, reads 82 °C (180 °F). Finish cooking on the lit section to give the hens nice grill marks.

Herb and Lemon Butter: Meanwhile, in a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter with the garlic until the butter turns nut-brown. Add the lemon juice. Watch out for splattering. Remove the garlic. Add the parsley and fennel. Cook for 1 minute. Salt and pepper.
When ready to serve, drizzle the hens with the lemon herb butter. Delicious with the vegetables en papillote.

8448.title: Vegetables en Papillote
instructions: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high.
In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Layer two large sheets of aluminum foil. Place the vegetable mixture in the centre. Close and tightly seal the papillote.
Place the foil packet on the grill. Close the lid and cook for 20 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.
Remove from the grill. Open the foil packet and gently toss the bean mixture.

8450.title: Blueberry Buttermilk Cream Tart
instructions: Crust: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).

In a food processor, lightly grind the spelt flakes. Add the flour, brown sugar, baking powder and salt. Add the butter and pulse until the butter forms pea-sized pieces. Add the buttermilk and pulse again until the dough just begins to form. Remove the dough from the processor.

Spread the dough evenly in a 28 cm (11 inch) tart pan with a removable bottom. Press firmly onto the bottom and edges of the plate. Cover with aluminum foil, then fill with dried peas or ceramic pie weights.
Bake for 25 minutes. Remove the peas and foil. Bake for another 10 minutes or until the dough is lightly golden. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
Buttermilk Cream: In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the milk. Let bloom for 5 minutes.

In a small pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar, flour and cornstarch. Add the eggs and mix well. Stir in the buttermilk and the remaining milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the pan until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat. Stir in the butter and vanilla. Add the gelatin mixture and stir until dissolved. Strain through a sieve to remove any lumps, if necessary.

Pour the buttermilk cream into the cooled crust. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool slightly, then refrigerate for 4 hours or until the cream is completely cold and set.
When ready to serve, unmould and top with the blueberries. Drizzle with honey.

8451.title: Mango with Passion Fruit
instructions: On a work surface, cut the mango on each side of the pit. With the tip of a knife, score the flesh in a criss-cross pattern without piercing the skin.
Cut the passion fruit in half. Sprinkle the sugar over both halves and stir to loosen the seeds and dissolve the sugar. Spoon the passion fruit over the mango. Serve immediately.

8454.title: Pear Bites with Cheddar and Lemon
instructions: Arrange the pear slices on a plate. Top the pear slices with the cheese and peel.

8463.title: Parsnip Chips
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). Place a wire rack over a baking sheet.

In a bowl, toss the parsnips with the oil. Salt and pepper. Spread on the rack without overlapping them. Bake for 25 minutes or until golden and crisp. Remove from the oven and let cool completely. The parsnip chips keep for 1 week in an airtight container at room temperature.

8467.title: Hemp-Cocoa Crumble with Pan-Fried Pears and Ice Cream
instructions: Crumble: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a food processor, grind the almonds, hemp and oats into fine crumbs. Add the remaining ingredients and pulse until the crumble just starts to clump together. Spread on the baking sheet.

Bake for 25 minutes, stirring halfway through. As soon as it comes out of the oven, break the crumble into pieces with a wooden spoon. Let cool completely. The crumble keeps for 10 days in an airtight container at room temperature.
Pears: In a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the pears in the butter for 3 minutes.
Divide the hot pears among the plates, then top with a scoop of ice cream and crumble, to taste. Sprinkle with hemp seeds.

8503.title: Lamb Shanks with Tomato and Lentils
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
In a large ovenproof Dutch oven over medium-high heat, brown the shanks on each side in the butter. Set aside on a plate.

In the same Dutch oven over medium heat, soften the onion. Add the tomato paste and mustard. Cook for 1 minute while stirring. Deglaze with the wine. Add the tomatoes, broth and shanks. Bring to a boil. Cover and bake for 2 hours, turning the meat halfway through cooking. Remove the lid and continue cooking for 1 hour, turning the meat once. Skim the fat from the sauce.
Meanwhile, in a pot of boiling salted water, cook the lentils with the bay leaves until al dente, about 30 minutes. Drain.
Add the lentils to the Dutch oven and continue cooking in the oven for 15 minutes so they absorb the sauce.

8527.title: Orange Iced Tea with Lemon Ice
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring the water and 55 g (1/4 cup) of the sugar to a boil. Remove from the heat. Add the tea bags. Cover and let steep for 20 minutes.
Remove the tea bags. Add a few ice cubes to cool the liquid. Squeeze the juice of the lemon over the saucepan of tea. Set aside.
Cut the lemon halves into pieces, removing the seeds. Place the remaining sugar in a small bowl. Rub the rims of tall glasses with a piece of lemon, then dip them in the sugar.

In a food processor, finely grind the lemon pieces. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed. Add the remaining ice cubes and pulse until crushed. Divide the lemon ice among the glasses, pour in the tea, then top up with the orange soft drink.

8593.title: Pickled Jalapeños
instructions: On a work surface, cut the peppers in half lengthwise. Remove the white membranes and seeds (see note). Place in a 500 ml (2-cup) glass jar.

In a small saucepan, bring the remaining ingredients to a boil and simmer for 1 minute. Pour the boiling liquid over the peppers in the jar, up to 5 mm (1/4 inch) from the rim. Seal the jar. Let cool and refrigerate. Let macerate for at least 24 hours before serving so the flavours can develop.
You can keep the pickled peppers for 3 months in the refrigerator.

8609.title: Red Curry Paste
instructions: In a small food processor, purée all the ingredients until smooth.
Transfer the curry paste to an airtight container. The curry paste keeps for one week in the refrigerator or 3 months in the freezer.

8636.title: Carrot Cake-Style French Toast Croissants
instructions: Croissants: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter a 23 x 13 cm (9 x 5 inch) loaf pan with a 1.5-litre (6-cup) capacity and line it with a strip of parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.
Spread the croissant cubes on a non-stick or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until they start to dry out and are lightly golden. Let cool.
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, carrots, brown sugar, currants, pineapple and spices.

Add the toasted croissant cubes and mix gently to coat them well with the egg mixture. Let soak for 30 minutes. There will be almost no liquid left. If there is, remove the excess. Pour the mixture into the loaf pan.
Toppings: In a small bowl, combine the brown sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle over the top of the croissants.
Bake for 45 minutes (or 55 minutes if the loaf pan is glass) or until the top is slightly puffed and golden. Let cool completely. Unmould and cut into slices about 2.5 cm (1 inch) thick.
In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown half the French toast slices at a time in the butter for 3 to 4 minutes, turning them halfway through.
Serve with carrot jam, yogurt whipped cream and pecans.

8637.title: Yogurt Whipped Cream
instructions: In a bowl, whip the cream with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Using a spatula, fold in the yogurt.
Delicious with pancakes, fresh fruit or the carrot cake-style French toast croissants.

8645.title: Sous Vide Duck Confit
instructions: Preheat the water with the precision cooker to 68 °C (155 °F).
In a bowl, sprinkle the salt and pepper over the duck leg. Rub for 1 minute. Place everything in a resealable bag with the remaining ingredients.
Place in the preheated water. Cook for 36 hours. Add water as needed to make sure the meat stays submerged.

8672.title: Irish Cream Chocolate Sauce
instructions: Place the chocolate in a bowl.
In a small saucepan, bring the creams to a boil. Pour the hot liquid over the chocolate. Let melt for 2 minutes. Whisk the chocolate until the sauce is smooth. Add the cinnamon and stir. Let cool.
Serve the Baileys chocolate sauce with gluten-free cinnamon doughnuts, pancakes, waffles or simply ice cream.

8709.title: Carrot Ginger Rum Cocktail
instructions: In a blender, purée the carrot with the rum, ginger syrup, triple sec and lemon juice until smooth. Strain through a fine sieve.
Pour into a whisky glass (lowball) filled with ice cubes. Garnish with carrot ribbons.

8747.title: Orecchiette with Beans, Pan-Fried Mushrooms and Olive Oil Breadcrumbs (Orecchiette con Fave, Funghi e Mollica di Pane)
instructions: Place the beans in a large saucepan. Add the bay leaves and 2 whole garlic cloves. Cover with cold water. Cook over medium heat, uncovered, for 1 hour or until the beans are tender, skimming from time to time and adding water as needed to keep them covered (keep 1 cm [1/2 inch] of water above the beans at all times). Do not drain the beans.

Remove the bay leaf. Season generously with salt and pepper, then add 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the oil. With an immersion blender, purée the beans until smooth. Set aside in a bowl. This step can be done up to 4 days ahead.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook the mushrooms, the remaining garlic and the chili flakes in 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the oil until golden. Season with salt. Set aside on a plate.
In the same skillet over medium heat, brown the bread cubes on all sides in the remaining oil. Salt and pepper. Use as is, or grind into fine crumbs in a food processor. Set aside.

Meanwhile, in a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta until al dente. Set aside 1 cup (250 ml) of the cooking water. Drain the orecchiette and toss with a little oil. Return the pasta to the pot. Stir in the bean purée and add cooking water as needed to loosen the sauce. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve the orecchiette on plates. Top with the mushroom mixture and sprinkle with breadcrumbs, to taste.

8755.title: Pasta with White Bolognese Sauce (al Ragù Bianco)
ingredients: mezze rigatoni, garganelli or other short pasta with large holes
mascarpone cheese or fresh Parmesan cheese (optional)
instructions: In a large skillet over high heat, cook the onion, celery and carrot in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Set the vegetables aside in a bowl.

In the same skillet over medium-high heat, cook the pancetta and pork, breaking up the meat with a wooden spoon, until golden. Deglaze with the wine and reduce by half. Add the broth, rosemary and sage. Return the reserved vegetables to the skillet. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer over low heat for 1 hour, stirring a few times, or until three quarters of the liquid has been absorbed. Remove the rosemary and sage sprigs.

In a pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta until very al dente. Set aside 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the cooking water. Drain. Add the pasta to the sauce. Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring to coat the pasta in the sauce. Add the reserved pasta cooking water to thin out the sauce as needed. Off the heat, add the mascarpone or Parmesan, if desired.

8836.title: Panettone Like a Baba (Panettone Ubriaco with Limoncello)
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring the sugar, water and limoncello to a boil. Remove from the heat and let cool for 5 minutes.
Place the panettone slices on plates. Generously drizzle the slices with the syrup. Serve with pineapple slices and ice cream.

8996.title: Trout Tartare Canapés with Gin and Maple Jelly
ingredients: very fresh skinless rainbow trout fillet
instructions: Gin and Maple Jelly: In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the water and let bloom for 5 minutes.

In a small saucepan, bring the remaining water and the maple syrup to a boil. Salt lightly. Remove from the heat. Add the remaining ingredients and the gelatin, stirring until it has dissolved. Pour the mixture into a dish of about 13 x 13 cm (5 x 5 inches). Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Tartare: Place a bowl in the freezer for 15 minutes. This will help keep the fish very cold while you prepare the tartare.

Remove the bowl from the freezer. On a work surface, cut the fish into small dice, placing the diced fish in the bowl as you work. Add the chives, shallot, oil, lemon juice and Tabasco. Season with salt and pepper and mix well.
Assembly: Using a knife, cut the jelly into small cubes.
Divide the tartare among the crackers. Top with a spoonful of jelly and fish roe. Garnish with pieces of chive.

8997.title: Beet and Goat Cheese Terrine on Canapés
instructions: Place the beets in a saucepan. Cover with water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil and simmer for 45 minutes or until tender. Add water during cooking as needed. Drain and peel under cold water.
On a work surface, slice the yellow beets, then the Chioggia beets, into rounds 5 mm (1/4 inch) thick. Set aside separately.
In a bowl, mix the cheeses with a fork until smooth.

On a work surface, lay out a sheet of plastic wrap about 33 cm (13 inches) long. Using a small offset spatula, spread one fifth of the cheese mixture, about 30 ml (2 tbsp), into a 15 x 4 cm (6 x 1 1/2 inch) layer in the centre of the plastic wrap. Cover with half the yellow beets (about 5 slices). Season with salt and pepper. Repeat, layering the cheese and beet slices and alternating Chioggia and yellow beets. Finish with a layer of cheese. Fold the plastic wrap over the terrine and seal it tightly. Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Remove the plastic wrap and place the terrine on a work surface. Sprinkle all four sides with chives. Cut into 12 slices, wiping the knife blade between each cut.
Place a slice of terrine on each cracker. Using a brush, coat the top with a thin layer of oil. Garnish with microgreens.

8998.title: Sweet Canapés with White Chocolate, Figs and Candied Lemon
instructions: Lemon Peel and Syrup: Using a vegetable peeler, remove long strips of zest from the entire lemon, then cut them into julienne.
Place the lemon zest in a small saucepan. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Drain and repeat twice.

Return the zest to the saucepan. Add the sugar, water and corn syrup. Bring to a boil and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes or until the zest turns translucent. Let cool. Add the lemon juice (see note). Lift out the zest and place it on a plate lined with paper towels. Set the zest and syrup aside separately.
White Chocolate Cream: Meanwhile, place the chocolate in a bowl.

In a small pot, bring the cream to a boil. Pour the hot cream over the white chocolate and let rest 1 minute without stirring. Whisk until the cream is smooth. Cover the surface of the cream directly with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 1 hour or until the cream is completely cold.
Assembly: Beat the chilled chocolate cream with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form, but not so much that it becomes unspreadable.
Spread the crackers with the chocolate cream. Top with the fig slices, then lightly brush them with the lemon syrup. Garnish with the lemon peel and mint leaves.

9000.title: Caramelized Onion, Artichoke and Olive Crackers
ingredients: olive oil and rosemary Melba Toast-style crackers
instructions: In a large saucepan over medium heat, cook the onions in the oil, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until well caramelized, about 20 minutes, taking care to scrape the bottom of the saucepan. Stir in the anchovy paste, if desired. Generously season with salt and pepper. Let cool.
In a bowl, combine the artichokes, olives and parsley.
Spread the crackers with the caramelized onions. Top with the artichoke mixture.

9002.title: Avocado and Egg Crackers
ingredients: green or red Tabasco-style hot sauce
instructions: Place a steaming basket in the bottom of a pot. Add enough water to just reach the bottom of the steamer. Cover and bring to a boil. Place the eggs in it. Cover and steam for 12 minutes, making sure there is always water in the saucepan. Remove the eggs and plunge them into an ice bath to stop the cooking. Let cool for 15 minutes. Drain. Peel the eggs and slice them. Set aside.
Meanwhile, in a shallow dish, mash the avocados with a fork. Stir in the lime juice, Tabasco and cumin. Salt and pepper.
Spread the crackers with the avocado mixture, then top with egg slices. Sprinkle with paprika and fleur de sel. Serve immediately.

9070.title: Potato Waffle Sandwiches
instructions: Lemon Mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Poivrer. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Sandwiches: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Spread the potato waffles on a non-stick or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 15 minutes. Turn them over and continue baking for 5 to 10 minutes or until golden brown.

Meanwhile, in a large non-stick skillet over medium-low heat, cook the eggs in the butter on one side only for sunny-side up, or carefully turn them over and cook lightly on the other side, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny. Salt and pepper. Set aside.

Spread one side of 12 waffles with the lemon mayonnaise. Divide the lettuce, bacon and tomato slices among 4 waffles. Salt and pepper. Cover each with a second waffle. Top with the avocado slices and an egg. Close the sandwiches with the remaining waffles.

9071.title: Potato, Sausage and Broccoli Frittata
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Butter an ovenproof non-stick skillet about 23 cm (9 inches) in diameter.

Spread the potato sticks on one side of a non-stick or parchment-lined baking sheet. Place the sausages on the other half. Drizzle with the oil. Bake for 10 minutes. Turn the potato sticks and sausages over. Continue baking for 5 minutes, until golden brown. Cut the sausages into slices.
Reduce the oven temperature to 350°F (180°C).

In a bowl, whisk the cream with the eggs. Add the cheese and green onion. Season with salt and pepper and mix well. Pour the egg mixture into the skillet. Top with the broccoli, sausages and potatoes.
Bake for 30 minutes or until the eggs are cooked through and lightly golden. Serve the frittata with toasted crusty bread, if desired.

9205.title: Puffed Omelette (Pascade) with Mushrooms and Arugula Salad with Fresh Goat Cheese
instructions: Place the rack in the middle of the oven and set an enamelled cast-iron skillet about 25 cm (10 inches) in diameter on it. Preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
In a large measuring cup, using an immersion blender, blend the eggs, milk, flour and sugar until smooth. Season with salt.

Remove the skillet from the oven. Using a silicone brush, brush the inside of the skillet with 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the butter. Pour the eggs into the skillet. Carefully return the skillet to the oven. Bake for 12 minutes or until the omelette is puffed, the centre is just set and the edges are golden.

Meanwhile, in another large skillet over medium-high heat, brown half the mushrooms at a time in 30 ml (2 tbsp) of the butter for 4 minutes. Salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate. Return all the mushrooms to the skillet. Add the chives.
In a bowl, toss the arugula with the olive oil and vinegar. Salt and pepper.
Spread the mushrooms over the omelette. Top with the cheese and arugula salad. Serve immediately.

9422.title: Roasted Carrot Spread Canapés
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
On a non-stick or parchment-lined baking sheet, toss the orange carrots, bell pepper and garlic with 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the oil. Salt and pepper.
Roast for 25 minutes or until the carrots and pepper are very tender and starting to brown. Let cool. Peel the pepper and the garlic cloves. Compost the peels.

In a small food processor, purée the roasted carrots, pepper, garlic and almonds. Add the remaining oil, the vinegar and the harissa. Pulse until just coarse. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed. Adjust the seasoning.
Spread the carrot spread on the crackers. Top with the purple carrot rounds and garnish with dill fronds. Serve immediately.

9424.title: Radish Canapés with Tarragon Butter
instructions: In a bowl, using a spatula, mix the butter and tarragon until the butter is smooth. Salt and pepper.
In another bowl, toss the radish and cucumber slices with the vinegar and mustard. Salt and pepper.
Spread the crackers with the tarragon butter. Top with the radish salad. Garnish with tarragon leaves and radish microgreens, if desired. Serve immediately.

9510.title: Sausage Burgers with Tomato Sauce and Spinach
instructions: Mayonnaise: In a small bowl, whisk together all the ingredients. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium-high. Oil the grate.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook the spinach in the oil until just wilted. Salt and pepper. Place a sieve over a bowl. Place the spinach in it and let cool slightly.
Grill the sausage patties until cooked through, about 5 minutes per side. Place a slice of cheese on each patty and let melt for 1 minute. Toast the buns.

Spread the bottom halves of the buns with the tomato sauce. Top with the sausage patties and the spinach. Spread the inside of the top halves with the mayonnaise. Close the burgers and serve right away.

9543.title: Pressure Cooker Vegetable Broth
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven's broiler. Spread the vegetables on a non-stick or foil-lined baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes or until the vegetables are golden. Place the vegetables in the pressure cooker pot.
Add the remaining ingredients. Cover and select the Soup function. Set the machine to cook for 25 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally (about 15 minutes), and remove the lid. Strain the broth through a sieve, then compost the vegetables and aromatics.

9585.title: Maple Apple and Pepper Chutney
instructions: In a saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil. Simmer over medium heat for 25 minutes or until the mixture is jammy and the cooking juices have reduced almost completely and are syrupy. Adjust the seasoning. Transfer to an airtight container and let cool. Cover and refrigerate. The chutney keeps for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.

9600.title: Gluten-Free Tagliatelle with Lemon Sauce
instructions: In a bowl, combine the flour and salt. In another small bowl, lightly beat the eggs and egg yolk.

In a small saucepan, bring the water to a boil. Pour the boiling water into the bowl of flour and mix with a fork until the water is completely absorbed. Pour in the eggs and mix with a fork. Mix with your hands until the dough starts to come together.
Place the dough on an unfloured work surface. Knead with your hands until smooth, about 5 minutes. The dough will be moist but won't stick to your fingers.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap. Let rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.

On a lightly floured work surface, divide the dough into 4 pieces and shape them into rectangles. Using a rolling pin, roll out the rectangles of dough to a thickness of 1 cm (1/2 inch). Cover them with a clean cloth or plastic wrap to keep them from drying out.

Using a pasta machine (hand-cranked roller), roll out one rectangle of dough at a time, without flouring it too much so it stays slightly sticky, thinning it gradually (to setting 3 or 4, or to about 2 mm/1/16 inch thick). Place the rolled-out sheets of dough on a work surface. Cover them with a clean cloth or plastic wrap to keep them from drying out.

Lightly flour the sheets of pasta and cut them into 23 cm (9 inch) long strips. Stack three strips of dough, then fold them in half lengthwise. Using a chef's knife, cut into 1 cm (1/2 inch) wide tagliatelle. Place on a lightly floured baking sheet and shape into small nests. Continue with the remaining strips of dough. Reuse any dough scraps. Freeze at this point, if desired.
In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta for 2 minutes or until very al dente. Set aside 1 cup (250 ml) of the cooking water. Drain the pasta.

Lemon Sauce: Meanwhile, in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, melt the butter with the lemon zest and chili flakes. Season generously with pepper. Add 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the cooking water. Bring to a boil. Over low heat, add the pasta, Parmesan, lemon juice and herbs. Mix well. Add the reserved pasta cooking water to thin out the sauce as needed. Adjust the seasoning. Serve immediately.

9675.title: Apple-Ginger Spritz
instructions: Place the sugar on a small plate. Rub the rim of a spritz cocktail glass or a large wine glass with the lemon wedge. Dip the rim of the glass in the sugar.
Place the ice cubes in the glass. Pour in the bitter citrus liqueur, apple must, ginger beer and lemon juice. Garnish with the orange half-slice and the basil leaf.

9691.title: Meatless Keftas with Grilled Vegetable Couscous Salad
instructions: Keftas and Couscous: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a pot, bring the water to a boil. Remove from the heat and add the couscous. Cover and let sit for 5 minutes. Fluff the grains of couscous with a fork. Salt and pepper.

In a large bowl, combine the meat substitute with 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the rehydrated couscous, the green onions, 15 g (1/3 cup) of the cilantro and the spices. Salt and pepper. Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions. Shape each portion into a slightly elongated log. Place the keftas on one half of the baking sheet. Place the vegetables and garlic on the other half of the baking sheet. Coat the keftas, vegetables and garlic with the oil.
Bake for 15 minutes or until the keftas and vegetables are golden brown, turning the keftas halfway through cooking.
In a bowl, combine the remaining couscous and cilantro with the olives, mint, lemon juice and vegetables. Salt and pepper.
Sauce: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
