Divide the keftas and couscous salad among plates. Sprinkle the keftas with a little curry powder. Serve with the sauce.

9708.title: Pineapple, Lime and Ginger Cocktail
ingredients: egg white or 3 drops vegan foamer
instructions: In a shaker, vigorously shake the pineapple juice, whisky, cane syrup, lime juice, egg white, ginger, Angostura and ice cubes for 1 minute.

Fill a whisky glass (lowball) with ice cubes. Place pineapple slices against the side of the glass. Strain the cocktail into the glass through a small sieve. Using a small grater, garnish the glass with nutmeg and lime zest.

9791.title: Crab and Citrus Canapés
ingredients: fresh or frozen snow crab meat
instructions: In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise, dill, orange and lemon zest, lemon juice and garlic. Salt and pepper.
Spread the crackers with the seasoned mayonnaise. Top with the crab meat and orange pieces. Garnish with dill fronds. Serve immediately.

9792.title: Ham, Arugula and Egg Canapés
instructions: Place the eggs in a saucepan and cover with lukewarm water. Bring to a boil. Cover and remove from the heat. Let rest for 10 minutes. Drain the eggs and fill the pot with cold water. Return the eggs to the pot and let cool for 15 minutes. Peel the eggs under cold running water and pat dry. Cut the eggs into wedges. Compost the shells.
In a small food processor, purée the arugula with the oil, lemon juice and chili flakes until more or less smooth. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
Divide the ham among the crackers. Top with the arugula purée. Add the egg wedges. Salt and pepper. Garnish with arugula leaves. Serve immediately.

9878.title: Acerum and Pineapple Granita
instructions: Granita: In a blender, purée all the ingredients until very smooth. Pour into an 8-inch (20 cm) square glass baking dish. Cover and freeze for 6 hours or until the granita is completely frozen.
Meanwhile, place 8 cups or glasses that hold at least 180 ml (3/4 cup) each in the freezer for serving.
With a fork, scrape the granita into icy crystals. Return to the freezer until ready to serve.

Assembly: In a bowl, beat the cream with the sugar using an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. While beating, drizzle in the acerum until the whipped cream forms stiff peaks again. Refrigerate until ready to serve, as needed.
Divide the granita among the chilled cups, about 125 ml (1/2 cup) per cup. Top with the whipped cream. Sprinkle with the coconut and a little lime zest (see note). Serve immediately.

9907.title: Vegetable Shortening Pie Dough
instructions: In a bowl, whisk the egg white until foamy. Set aside.
In another bowl, combine the egg yolk, water and vinegar.

In a large bowl, combine the flour and salt. Add the shortening. Using a pastry blender or two knives, cut in the shortening until it is the size of small peas. Make a well in the centre of the mixture. Pour the egg yolk mixture into the well. Using a fork, gradually mix the dough until the flour is completely moistened. Add the egg white and mix gently.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces. Shape each portion into a disc with your hands. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 1 hour or freeze. Thaw completely in the refrigerator before using.

10095.title: Pappardelle with Red Wine Meat Sauce
ingredients: Italian sausage meat or medium ground pork
instructions: Sauce: In a saucepan over medium-high heat, cook the sausage meat in the oil, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until golden brown. Add the onion and garlic. Continue to cook for 2 minutes while stirring. Add the tomato paste and cook for 30 seconds, stirring. Pour in the red wine and simmer for 5 minutes or until reduced by half.

Add the broth, rosemary and chili flakes. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes or until the sauce has thickened slightly, regularly scraping the bottom of the saucepan with a wooden spoon. Remove and compost the rosemary.

Garnish: Meanwhile, in a large skillet over high heat, brown the garlic in the oil. Add the rapini and continue cooking for 3 to 4 minutes or until the stems are al dente and the leaves are tender, stirring frequently. Salt and pepper. Set aside.

In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta until al dente. Set aside 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the cooking water. Drain the pasta. Add them to the sauce with the Parmesan. Stir to coat the pasta well with the sauce. Continue cooking for 2 minutes or until the pasta has absorbed the sauce. Add the reserved pasta cooking water to thin out the sauce as needed.
Serve the pasta in shallow bowls. Top with the rapini and salami. Sprinkle with the parsley and Parmesan (see note).

10106.title: Pickled Raisins
instructions: In a small saucepan over medium heat, dry-toast the mustard and coriander seeds, stirring constantly, until the mustard seeds start to pop. Remove from the heat.

Add the remaining ingredients except the crackers. Stir. Bring to a boil and simmer for 1 minute. Transfer to an airtight glass container and let cool slightly. Cover and let marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight before enjoying. The raisins keep for 1 month in the refrigerator. Serve the raisins with crackers and as an accompaniment to a cheese platter.

10107.title: Olive and Almond Relish
instructions: In a small food processor, chop the almonds, parsley and garlic. Add the oil, molasses and vinegar. Mix well. The mixture should remain grainy. Salt and pepper. Transfer to an airtight container.

Add the olives and coat them well with the almond mixture. Cover and let marinate in the refrigerator for 3 hours or overnight before enjoying. The olives will keep in the refrigerator for 2 weeks. Serve the olives with crackers and as an accompaniment to a cheese platter.

10108.title: Maple Shallot and Apple Chutney
instructions: In a skillet over medium heat, cook the shallots in the oil until lightly golden. Deglaze with the vinegar and brandy. Let the liquid reduce by half. Remove from the heat.

Add the remaining ingredients except the crackers. Season generously with salt and pepper and mix. Simmer over low heat, stirring often, until the liquid has almost completely evaporated and the shallots are meltingly soft, about 15 minutes. Transfer to an airtight glass container and let cool slightly. Cover and refrigerate for 3 hours before enjoying. The chutney keeps for 1 month in the refrigerator. Serve the chutney with crackers and as an accompaniment to a cheese platter.

10128.title: Ricotta-Stuffed Sandwich Loaf
instructions: In a skillet over medium heat, soften the garlic in the oil for 1 minute. Add the spinach and continue cooking for 2 minutes or until the spinach has wilted. Drain and let cool. Squeeze the spinach to extract as much liquid as possible.

Meanwhile, on a work surface, using a bread knife, cut off the top of the loaf. Hollow out the inside of the bread and the top, leaving a shell about 1.5 cm (1/2 inch) thick. Dice the crumb and set aside 55 g (1 1/2 cups). Keep the remaining crumb for another use.

In a food processor, purée the artichokes. Add the spinach, ricotta and Parmesan. Process again until the mixture is smooth but still textured. Transfer the mixture to a bowl. Using a spatula, stir in the pistachios and the reserved crumb. Salt and pepper.

Spread the inside of the bread and the top with the pepper spread. Line the inside of the bread with three quarters of the deli meat slices. Add the ricotta mixture, then cover with the remaining deli meat slices. Close the bread. Wrap in aluminum foil or plastic wrap. Set aside in a glass dish. Place a weight (cans, plates, etc.) directly on the bread to press the ingredients together. Refrigerate for 8 hours or overnight.
Assembly: In a bowl, toss the arugula with the olive oil and vinegar. Salt and pepper. Spread the salad on a serving plate.
On a work surface, remove the stuffed bread from the foil. Cut the bread into slices about 2 cm (3/4 inch) thick, wiping the blade between each cut. Arrange the sandwich slices over the salad.

10221.title: Dill and Sweet and Sour Onion Dip
instructions: Sweet and Sour Onions: In a medium skillet over medium heat, cook the onions in the oil for 5 minutes or until translucent. Add the vinegar and let reduce for 1 minute, stirring. Add the honey and continue cooking for 2 minutes or until the liquid thickens. Salt and pepper. Transfer to a small bowl and let cool. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour or until completely cooled.

Yogurt dip: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Add half the onion mixture. Season generously with pepper and mix well. Transfer to a shallow bowl. Top with the remaining onion mixture. Sprinkle with Parmesan and dill sprigs. Serve with croutons and crudités.

10301.title: Salmon and Corn Chowder au Gratin
instructions: In a large saucepan over medium heat, soften the onion and leek in the butter until translucent, about 5 minutes. Season with salt. Sprinkle with the flour and cook for 1 minute while stirring. Pour in the clam juice and milk. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.

Add the potatoes. Simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes or until the potatoes are al dente, stirring a few times. Salt and pepper. Add the corn, cream and salmon. Continue cooking for 4 minutes or until the salmon is just cooked. Remove from the heat. Adjust the seasoning.
Meanwhile, in a small skillet over medium heat, brown the bacon until well coloured but still tender. Drain the bacon on a plate lined with paper towels. Add three quarters of the bacon to the soup.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven's broiler.

Place ovenproof bowls on a baking sheet. Divide the soup among them and sprinkle with the cheese. Broil for 2 minutes or until the cheese is lightly golden. Garnish with the remaining bacon and the chives.

10472.title: Birthday Cake
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Butter the sides of an 8-inch (20 cm) springform pan and line the bottom with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the icing sugar, flour, sprinkles, baking powder and salt.

In a large bowl, beat the eggs with the oil, milk and vanilla using an electric mixer for 1 minute. With the machine running on low speed, stir in the dry ingredients. Spread the batter out in the prepared pan.
Bake for 55 minutes to 1 hour or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool on a wire rack. Unmould and let cool completely, about 3 hours.
Place the cake on a serving dish. Using a spatula, spread the icing over the top of the cooled cake. Decorate with sprinkles. The cake will keep for 3 days, covered, at room temperature.

10474.title: Smoked Salmon Dip
ingredients: mullet roe or other fish roe
instructions: Pickled Vegetables: Place the radishes and fennel stalk in a bowl.
In a small saucepan, bring the sugar, water, vinegar, fennel seeds and salt to a boil, until the sugar and salt dissolve.
Pour the boiling liquid over the vegetables in the bowl. Cover and let marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour or until the vegetables are completely cooled. Drain before serving.
Fennel Oil: Pour the oil into a tall, straight container such as a measuring cup and add the fennel fronds. Using a hand blender, purée until smooth.
Strain the oil through a sieve set over a bowl. Compost the residue.
Yogurt dip: On a work surface, remove the skin from the salmon. Using a fork, flake the fish.

In a bowl, whip the cream until soft peaks form. Using a spatula, fold in the sour cream, lemon juice, cayenne pepper and fish. Salt lightly. The dip will keep for 3 days in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

Place the dip in a serving bowl or shallow dish, making decorative waves in the surface with a spoon. Pour the fennel oil into the grooves. Garnish with the pickled vegetables, mullet roe and dill sprigs. Serve with shrimp chips.

10485.title: Breakfast Banana Split
instructions: Spread the granola in an oval bowl. Place the banana slices lengthwise on each side.
Spoon the yogurt into three mounds on the granola. Top with the berries.

Hold a piece or bar of chocolate in one hand and the vegetable peeler in the other. “Peel” the chocolate along its narrowest (thinnest) side. You will get small chocolate curls. Decorate the banana split with the chocolate curls and the cherry. Serve immediately.

10498.title: Smashed Potatoes with Cotija Cheese
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
On a non-stick or parchment-lined baking sheet, lightly oil the potatoes. Salt and pepper. Bake for 20 minutes or until tender when pierced with the tip of a knife.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the oil with the spices. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Remove from the oven. Using a measuring cup, flatten the potatoes to a thickness of 1 cm (1/2 inch). Using a brush, brush the potatoes with half (45 ml/3 tbsp) of the oil mixture. Continue to bake for 15 minutes.
Remove from the oven. Turn the potatoes over. Brush them with the remaining oil mixture. Continue baking for 15 minutes or until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, in a small food processor, purée the sour cream with the cilantro and lime zest and juice until smooth. Season with salt. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Spread the sour cream mixture on a large serving plate. Top with the potatoes and jalapeño rounds. Sprinkle with the cheese. Serve with lime wedges. Serve immediately.

10499.title: Melty Baked Cheese with Sautéed Mushrooms
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

Place the cheese on a square of aluminum foil about 15 cm (6 inches) wide. Fold the foil up around the cheese to keep it from collapsing during baking. Place the cheese in a baking dish. Bake for 15 minutes or until the cheese is runny.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the vinegar, maple syrup and mustard.
In a skillet over high heat, cook the mushrooms and shallot in the butter until golden brown. Salt and pepper. Deglaze with the vinegar mixture and mix well. Remove from the heat.
Add the chives and mix. Adjust the seasoning.

Carefully remove the cheese from the foil and place it on a serving plate. Using a paring knife, carefully slice off the top rind of the cheese. Top with the sautéed mushrooms. Serve with toasted bread slices. Serve immediately.

10615.title: Stuffed Mini Loaves with Two Dips (Onion-Olive and Ham-Mustard)
instructions: Loaves: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).

On a work surface, using a bread knife, cut off the tops of the loaves. Remove the crumb from the bottom of the loaves to make a cavity. Set the crumb aside for another use. Set aside the loaves and tops for assembly.
In a bowl, combine the cheese with the mayonnaise and sour cream. Set aside.
Onion-Olive Dip: In a non-stick skillet over medium heat, cook the onions in the oil for 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until golden brown. Transfer to another bowl and let cool for 10 minutes.
Add the olives, anchovy paste and half the cheese mixture. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Ham-Mustard Dip: Add the ham, mustard, shallot and garlic to the bowl with the remaining cheese mixture. Mix well. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

Assembly: Pour each dip into the cavity of a loaf. Place each loaf on a large sheet of aluminum foil. Place the reserved tops on the loaves. Wrap the loaves completely in the foil. Place the loaves on a baking sheet.
Bake for 50 minutes or until the dips are piping hot.
Serve the onion-olive dip with the endive leaves and apple wedges. Garnish the ham-mustard dip with the chives and serve with the cauliflower and broccoli florets.

10616.title: Warm Date, Bacon and Cheddar Crostini
instructions: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
Spread the bread slices on the baking sheet. Oil lightly. Bake for 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
Meanwhile, in a small skillet over medium-high heat, brown the bacon. Add the green onions and continue cooking for 1 minute, stirring. Remove from the heat. Add the dates and mix well.
Sprinkle the toasts with the cheese. Fill with the bacon mixture. Bake for 4 minutes or until the cheese has melted.
Garnish with parsley. Serve immediately.

10639.title: Vegan Lime Pie
instructions: Filling: Place the cashews in a bowl. Cover with the boiling water. Let soak for 2 hours to soften them. Drain.

Crust: Meanwhile, in a food processor, combine the flour, icing sugar, cornstarch and spices. Add the coconut oil and pulse until the mixture has a sandy texture. Add the water and pulse again until the dough just begins to form. Add more water as needed. Remove the dough from the processor.
Press the dough evenly along the bottom and up the sides of a 9-inch (23 cm) round, 1 inch (2.5 cm) deep tart pan with removable bottom. Prick the dough with a fork. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cover the dough with a piece of foil and fill with dried beans or ceramic pie weights.
Bake for 20 minutes. Gently remove the pie weights and foil. Return to the oven and bake for another 4 to 5 minutes or until golden. Let cool on a wire rack.
In a blender, purée the cashews with the lime zest and juice, coconut milk and brown sugar for 3 to 4 minutes or until creamy and velvety. Pour into a pot.

Over medium-high heat, bring to a boil, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the saucepan, until the mixture thickens. Simmer for 1 minute. Spoon into the crust. Smooth the surface of the filling with a small offset spatula. Refrigerate, uncovered, for 4 hours.

In a bowl, whip the whipped cream substitute with the sugar using an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Spread in the centre of the pie. Decorate with lime zest. The pie will keep for 2 to 3 days in the refrigerator.

10970.title: Kale Salad with Turkey and Roasted Vegetables
instructions: Vegetables and Turkey: Place one rack in the bottom of the oven and another in the middle. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

Spread the onions and sweet potatoes on the baking sheet. Coat them with half the oil (15 ml/1 tbsp). Salt and pepper. Roast on the bottom rack for 40 minutes, stirring the vegetables halfway through cooking.

Meanwhile, in an ovenproof non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the turkey on each side in the remaining oil (see note). Roast on the middle rack for 20 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the meat reads 82 °C (180 °F). Let rest for 10 minutes on a plate.
Dressing: Meanwhile, in a blender, purée all of the ingredients until smooth. Salt and pepper.

Salad: Place the kale in a large bowl. Season with salt. Massage the kale with your hands until it softens. Add the chickpeas, raisins and half the vinaigrette (125 ml/1/2 cup). Mix well. Add the roasted vegetables and toss gently. Adjust the seasoning.
On a work surface, slice the turkey. Divide the salad among four plates. Top with the turkey slices and avocado. Drizzle with the remaining dressing.

11034.title: “Snow Globe” Gin and Tonic
instructions: Ice Cube and Tree: Using scissors, cut the rosemary sprig to about 10 cm (4 inches) long.

Cut a 7.5 cm (3 inch) square from a sheet of paper. Using a toothpick, poke a hole in the centre of the square. Insert the base of the rosemary sprig (the woody end of the stem) into the hole in the paper square.

Pour the water into a stemless red wine glass. Add the cranberries. Place the rosemary in the glass, needles down, so the paper rests on the rim of the glass (the paper holds the rosemary in place while it freezes). Place the glass in the freezer for 4 hours or until the water is completely frozen.
Gin and Tonic: When ready to serve, remove the glass from the freezer. Remove the paper. Pour the gin and tonic water into the glass. Add the orange zest. Serve immediately.

11035.title: Beet, White Bean and Fennel Salad
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).

Place the beets on a sheet of aluminum foil. Wrap in a foil packet. Place on a baking sheet. Bake for 40 minutes or until the beets are tender. Let cool. Peel the beets and cut them in half or into quarters.
In a bowl, combine the oil and vinegar. Season with salt. Add the beets, white beans, herbs and fennel. Mix well. Adjust the seasoning.
Divide the salad among four plates. Top with the cheese.

11036.title: White Bean Casserole with Pancetta and Zucchini
instructions: Shallot Relish: In a small bowl, combine the shallot and vinegar. Let marinate for 5 minutes. Drain the shallot and discard the liquid. Add the parsley and oil. Season with salt and mix.
Casserole: In a large skillet over medium heat, brown the pancetta in the oil. Set aside on a plate lined with paper towel.

In the same large skillet over medium-high heat, soften the shallots and garlic with the chili pepper in the cooking fat. Add the zucchini and continue cooking for 8 minutes or until cooked and they have released their water, stirring a few times during cooking. Add more oil as needed.

Add the broth and cream. Continue cooking, stirring, until the sauce starts to thicken. Add the pancetta, white beans and Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes. Adjust the seasoning.
Divide the white bean mixture among bowls. Garnish with Parmesan shavings, parsley leaves and the shallot relish. Serve with toasted bread slices.

11037.title: Magie Marier's Delicata Squash with Whipped Goat Cheese and Dukkah
instructions: Goat Cheese Cream: In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over the water. Let bloom for 5 minutes.
In a saucepan, bring half the cream (180 ml/3/4 cup) to a simmer. Remove from the heat.

Add the goat cheese and gelatin. Whisk, or blend with an immersion blender, until smooth. Stir in the remaining cream. Transfer to a bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours or until completely chilled.
Dukkah: Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

On a non-stick or parchment paper-lined baking sheet, combine all of the ingredients. Add fleur de sel. Bake for 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the seeds are golden and the honey has caramelized. Let cool completely. Increase the oven temperature to 400°F (200°C).

Squash: On another non-stick or parchment-lined baking sheet, coat the squash and garlic with the oil, honey and spices. Salt and pepper. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until the squash is tender and lightly golden, turning halfway through cooking.
Dressing: Meanwhile, in a skillet over medium heat, cook the bacon until cooked through and golden. Using a slotted spoon, remove the bacon and set it aside on a plate lined with paper towels.
In the same skillet with the cooking fat, infuse the oil with the lemon zest and thyme for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring. Poivrer. Set aside in a bowl and let cool.
On a work surface, chop the bacon and add it to the bowl. Add the remaining ingredients and mix well. Adjust the seasoning.
Assembly: Using an electric mixer, whip the goat cheese cream until it forms firm but still soft peaks. Salt and pepper.
Spread the whipped goat cheese cream on a serving plate. Top with the warm squash and drizzle with the vinaigrette. Sprinkle with the dukkah and thyme leaves. Poivrer.

11038.title: Luca Cianciulli's Sage and Orange Veal Shoulder with Tuscan Kale
ingredients: bone-in veal blade roast, 1.8 to 2 kg
instructions: Veal: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
On a plate, season the meat with salt and pepper.
In a large Dutch oven or ovenproof pot over medium-high heat, brown the meat for 5 minutes per side in half the butter (15 ml/1 tbsp) and half the oil (15 ml/1 tbsp). Set aside on another plate.

In the same pot, soften the carrot, celery, leek and bell pepper in the remaining butter and oil. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Deglaze with the wine. Add the veal stock, the orange zest and juice, and the sage leaves. Return the meat to the pot. Bring to a boil. Cover and bake for 3 hours or until the meat falls apart easily with a fork. Remove the bones and large pieces of orange zest, then compost them.
Let rest for 30 minutes before serving. Adjust the seasoning.

Sage and Orange Relish: Meanwhile, in a skillet over medium heat, heat the oil with the breadcrumbs, sage, garlic and orange zest. Cook until the breadcrumbs and garlic start to brown. Remove the garlic clove and compost it. Transfer the breadcrumb mixture to a bowl.
Add the orange segments and vinegar. Season with salt and mix. Set aside.
Kale: Meanwhile, in a large pot of salted boiling water, blanch the kale for 10 minutes. Drain and let cool.
In a large skillet over medium heat, heat the oil and garlic. Add the kale and continue cooking for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring. Salt and pepper. Remove the garlic clove and compost it.
Assembly: Divide the kale and meat among plates. Top with the sauce and vegetables. Serve with the sage and orange relish.

11041.title: Minh Phat Tu's Celebration Cake with Mango Jam and Chrysanthemum Whipped Cream
ingredients: ripe, firm mangoes, peeled and sliced into large julienne
instructions: Chrysanthemum Whipped Cream: In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over the water. Let bloom for 5 minutes.
In a saucepan, bring half the cream (500 ml/2 cups) and the sugar to a boil. Remove from the heat.
Add the gelatin and whisk until completely dissolved. Add the flowers and mix. Cover and let infuse for 10 minutes.

Strain the cream mixture through a sieve set over a large measuring cup or bowl, pressing on the flowers with the back of a ladle to extract as much liquid as possible. Compost the flowers. Stir in the remaining cream. Pour into a bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 5 hours or until the cream is cold.

Mango Jam: Meanwhile, in a pot, combine all of the ingredients. Bring to a boil and simmer over low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring frequently. Using a potato masher, lightly crush the mango pieces. Transfer to a bowl and let cool. Cover and refrigerate for 4 hours or until completely chilled.
Cake: Meanwhile, place the rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F). Line the bottom of a 23 cm (9 inch) springform pan with parchment paper. Do not butter the pan.
In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the milk. Stir in the flour. Drizzle in the oil and whisk until smooth.
In another bowl, beat the egg whites with the vinegar using an electric mixer until foamy. Gradually add the sugar and beat until stiff peaks form.

Vigorously stir one third of the meringue into the batter. Using a spatula, gently fold in the remaining meringue. Spread the batter out in the prepared pan. Lightly tap the pan on a work surface to remove any air bubbles.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean.
As soon as it comes out of the oven, turn the pan upside down on a rack and let cool completely, about 3 hours.
Assembly: Using an electric mixer, whip the cream until stiff peaks form. Transfer half the whipped cream at a time to a piping bag fitted with a large basketweave or star tip.
On a work surface, unmould the cake. Cut the cake in half horizontally to make 2 layers.

Place one cake layer on a serving dish. Using the piping bag, pipe a border of whipped cream around the edge of the cake. Fill the centre with half the mango jam. Top with the other cake layer. Spread the remaining mango jam over the top using a spatula.

Using the piping bag, cover the side of the cake with strips of whipped cream, from bottom to top, then pipe a border around the top edge of the cake. Decorate the centre of the cake with the mango slices. The cake will keep for 3 days, covered, in the refrigerator.

11044.title: Jonathan Rassi's Antipasto Lasagna
ingredients: artichoke bottoms or hearts in oil
instructions: Confit Tomatoes: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
Using a knife, make an X-shaped incision at the base of the tomatoes, without removing the stem.

In a pot of boiling water, blanch 4 tomatoes at a time for 30 seconds or until the skin starts to crack. Using a slotted spoon, remove the tomatoes and plunge them into a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking. Once the tomatoes have cooled, the skin comes off very easily when pulled from the incision. Then remove the stem. Compost the peels and stems.

On a work surface, cut the tomatoes into quarters. Remove the cores and seeds, then compost them. Place the tomato flesh in a bowl. Add the oil, garlic and thyme. Season with salt and pepper and mix well.
Place the tomatoes on a parchment-lined baking sheet, rounded side up. Bake for about 1 hour.
Remove the tomatoes from the oven. Increase the oven temperature to 400°F (200°C).

Artichoke Cream: Meanwhile, in a skillet over medium-high heat, soften the shallots in the butter. Deglaze with the wine and lemon juice. Reduce until almost dry. Add the cream and thyme. Bring to a boil. Reduce by half. Add the artichokes. Season with salt and pepper.
Ricotta: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Lasagna: On another parchment-lined baking sheet, place the lasagna noodles and pour the artichoke cream over them. Coat the noodles well with the cream. Over the noodles, arrange the ricotta mixture, confit tomatoes and roasted peppers, alternating them at random. Salt and pepper.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until the noodles are golden and crisp. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Salad: Meanwhile, in a large bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve the lasagna with the salad. Sprinkle with the ricotta salata.

11045.title: Giant Duck and Fennel Sandwich
instructions: Mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with pepper. Set aside.
Salad: In another bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Salt and pepper. Let marinate for 5 minutes. Drain the fennel in a sieve.

Sandwich: On a work surface, slice the baguette in half horizontally. Spread the inside of the bread with the mayonnaise. Top the bottom half of the bread with the duck and salad. Garnish with the gherkins. Close the sandwich (see note). Cut into eight pieces.

11046.title: Cheese-Stuffed Bread with Two Toppings (Pear-Blue Cheese and Mushroom)
instructions: Cheese Filling: Place one rack in the bottom of the oven and another in the middle. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
On a work surface, slice the baguette in half horizontally. Remove some of the crumb to make cavities inside the bread. Save the crumb for another use. Place both baguette halves on a baking sheet.

In a bowl, combine the ricotta and Parmesan. Salt and pepper. Spread the cheese mixture over each baguette half. Bake on the middle rack for 15 minutes or until the cheese is melted and the baguette is crisp.

Pear-Blue Cheese Topping: Meanwhile, spread the pancetta slices on the other baking sheet. Bake on the bottom rack for 10 minutes or until crisp. Drain on a plate lined with paper towels. Let cool. Break each slice into 3 or 4 pieces.
Meanwhile, in a small saucepan over low heat, bring the pear, maple syrup and vinegar to a boil. Simmer for 4 minutes or until the pear is tender. Let cool. Drain.
Top one cheese-filled baguette half with the pear, pancetta and blue cheese. Garnish with more parsley leaves.
Sautéed Mushrooms: In a large skillet over high heat, brown the mushrooms in the butter until golden brown. Add the chives. Season with salt and pepper.
Top the other cheese-filled baguette half with the mushrooms. Garnish with Parmesan shavings.
Cut each baguette half into 8 pieces. Serve immediately.

11047.title: Colombe St-Pierre's Christmas Rack of Pork in Salt Dough with Black Garlic Vinaigrette
ingredients: rack pork loin, 4 bones, about 2.2 lb
instructions: Pork: On a work surface, using a metal skewer, pierce the meat just below the ribs from one end of the rack to the other. Insert the sweetgrass into it (see note). Season the meat with salt and pepper. Place a small rack on a small baking sheet.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the meat on all sides in the oil and butter. Place the lamb on the grill.

In the same skillet, add the molasses, thyme and half the nutmeg (1 ml/¼ tsp). Bring to a boil and reduce over medium heat until slightly syrupy, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool. Remove and compost the thyme sprigs.
Using a brush, brush the molasses mixture over the entire rack of pork. Sprinkle with the remaining nutmeg. Refrigerate for 1 hour.

Salt Dough: Meanwhile, in a bowl, lightly beat the egg whites. Add the remaining ingredients. Using a wooden spoon, mix until the dough is smooth. Add a little water or flour, as needed. Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Egg Wash: In a bowl, combine the egg yolk and milk. Set aside.

Assembly: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Make 2 rolls of aluminum foil and place them side by side in the centre of the baking sheet.
On a lightly floured work surface, roll out the dough into a 30 cm (12 inch) square, or to fit the rack of pork, about 1 cm (1/2 inch) thick.

Place the cooled rack of pork on the dough. Cover the meat with the dough, leaving the bones exposed. With your fingers, pinch the edges of the dough to seal it well. Place on a strip of parchment paper.
Using a brush, brush the top of the dough with the egg wash. Using the parchment paper, place the rack of pork on the foil rolls on the baking sheet, bones up.

Bake for 55 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the centre of the meat reads 50 °C (122 °F). Let rest for 10 minutes or until the temperature in the centre of the meat reaches 57 °C (135 °F) for pink meat, or 63 °C (145 °F), depending on the desired doneness.
Black Garlic Vinaigrette: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Using a knife, open the salt crust and remove the rack of pork. Careful, the salt crust and the pork will be very hot. Compost the salt dough.
On a work surface, slice the rack between the ribs. Transfer the pork to a serving dish. Serve with the vinaigrette and a vegetable purée, if desired.

11048.title: Magie Marier's Spicy Chili-Citrus Condiment (Chili Crisp)
instructions: In a saucepan, off the heat, combine the oil and garlic. Cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes or until the garlic is golden brown, stirring a few times. Using a slotted spoon, remove the garlic and set it aside on a plate.

In the same saucepan with the oil, add the shallots, citrus zest, star anise and cinnamon sticks. Cook over medium-low heat for 8 to 9 minutes or until the shallots are golden brown, stirring a few times. Using a slotted spoon, remove the citrus zest, star anise and cinnamon sticks, then compost them. Remove the shallots and set them aside on the plate with the garlic.
In the same saucepan with the oil, add the sesame seeds and chili flakes. Cook for another 30 seconds. Remove from the heat. Add the sugar and stir until dissolved. Let cool for 15 minutes.

Transfer the oil mixture to a 750 ml (3 cup) jar. Add the garlic, shallots, soybeans and soy sauce. Mix well. Cover and refrigerate. The chili crisp will keep for 1 month in the refrigerator. This recipe is used in the Parmesan Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Herb Salad.

11049.title: Magie Marier's Parmesan Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Herb Salad
instructions: Roasted Brussels Sprouts: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Salt and pepper. Spread the mixture out in the baking sheet. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes or until the vegetables are tender and the breadcrumbs are crisp and golden, stirring two or three times during cooking.
Salad: In a large bowl, whisk together the oil, lime juice, maple syrup and garlic. Salt and pepper. Add the remaining ingredients and the roasted Brussels sprout mixture. Adjust the seasoning.
Transfer the salad to a large serving bowl. Sprinkle with Parmesan shavings and herb leaves. Top with the spicy chili-citrus condiment.

11050.title: Christmas Orange Sour
instructions: Rub the rim of a small cocktail coupe with the orange zest.
In a shaker, vigorously shake the orange and lemon juices, Grand Marnier, cane syrup, egg white and ice cubes. Strain into the coupe.
Using a fine grater, garnish with freshly grated cinnamon.

11090.title: Chicken, Crispy Rice and Pear Salad with Peanut Dressing
instructions: Peanut Dressing: In a personal blender, coarsely chop the peanuts. Set aside on a plate.
In the personal blender, purée the remaining ingredients until smooth. Add water to thin the dressing, as needed. Season with salt.
Crispy Rice: In a bowl, combine the rice, soy sauce and green onions.

In a large skillet over medium-high, heat the oil. Spread the rice to cover the bottom of the skillet. Let brown for 2 minutes, without stirring, until the rice is crisp. Stir and let the rice brown for 2 more minutes, without stirring. Repeat this step a third time. Transfer the rice to a large bowl.
Salad: Add the spinach, chicken and pears to the bowl with the rice. Stir to blend gently.
Serve the salad in shallow bowls. Drizzle with the dressing. Sprinkle with the peanuts and Thai basil or mint leaves.

11091.title: Potato, Asparagus and Smoked Salmon Salad
instructions: Oven Fries: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).

Place the potatoes in a pot. Cover with cold water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes or until just tender. Drain the potatoes and let cool slightly. On a work surface, cut the potatoes in half lengthwise.

On a non-stick or parchment paper-lined baking sheet, coat the potatoes with the oil. Salt and pepper. Place them cut side down on the baking sheet. Roast for 30 minutes or until the cut side is golden and crisp. Let cool.
Salad: Meanwhile, using a skimmer or slotted spoon, gently lower the eggs into a saucepan of simmering salted water. Cook for 6 minutes.

Add the asparagus and continue to cook for 2 minutes. Drain the eggs and asparagus. Fill the pot with cold water. Return the eggs and asparagus to the saucepan and let cool for 5 minutes. Peel the eggs under cold running water. Compost the shells. Drain and pat dry the eggs and asparagus. On a work surface, coarsely chop the eggs. Place the eggs and asparagus in a large bowl.

Add the remaining ingredients and the potatoes to the bowl. Mix well. Salt and pepper. Divide among shallow bowls and sprinkle with herbs. This potato salad is delicious served warm, but just as tasty cold the next day for lunch.

11092.title: Lesley Chesterman's Spicy Sausage and Pepper Rigatoni
instructions: In a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, cook the sausage meat in the oil for 5 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon.

Add the onion and continue cooking for 2 minutes, stirring, or until tender. Add the bell peppers and cook for 5 minutes. Salt and pepper. Add the tomatoes and water. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta until al dente. Set aside 1 cup (250 ml) of the cooking water. Drain the pasta.

Add the pasta to the skillet of sauce. Mix well. Add the cream and half the cheese (35 g/1/2 cup). Stir to coat the pasta well in the sauce. Cook until the pasta has absorbed the sauce and the cheese is slightly melted. Add the reserved pasta cooking water to thin out the sauce as needed. Adjust the seasoning.
Place the skillet at the centre of the table. Drizzle with oil and serve with the remaining cheese.

11093.title: Lesley Chesterman's Toast with Escargot Butter
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven's broiler. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
In a bowl, stir the butter with a wooden spoon until creamy. Add the garlic, parsley, lemon zest and juice, and salt. Season with pepper and mix well.

Place the two baguette halves side by side on the baking sheet, cut side up. Spread the butter over them. Broil for 2 to 3 minutes or until the bread is lightly golden. On a work surface, cut each baguette half into 8 pieces.

11095.title: Luca Cianciulli's Burrata, Nordic Shrimp and Shishito Pepper Pizzas
instructions: Dough: In a small bowl, combine the water, oil and yeast.

In a large bowl, using a wooden spoon, combine the flours and salt. Add the water mixture and mix with the spoon for 2 minutes. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm, humid place for about 2 hours or until the dough has doubled in volume.

On a lightly floured work surface, cut the dough in half. Shape each portion into a ball and place them in two other lightly oiled bowls. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 8 hours or up to 48 hours. Let stand at room temperature for 30 minutes before using.
Pizzas: Meanwhile, place a pizza stone in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F) for 45 minutes.
On a non-stick or parchment-lined baking sheet, toss the peppers with 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the oil. Season with salt. Roast for 13 to 15 minutes or until the peppers start to blacken slightly. Let cool.
In a large bowl, combine the peppers, shrimp, basil leaves, and lemon zest and juice with 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the oil. Season with salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, by hand or with a fork, lightly crush the tomatoes with the remaining oil and the oregano. Season with salt. Set aside.

On a floured work surface, press one ball of dough at a time with your hands into a disc about 23 cm (9 inches) in diameter, forming a thick rim. Remove any excess flour. Place the dough on a piece of parchment paper. Spread half the tomato mixture (about 125 ml/½ cup) over it. Drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle with half the grated cheese (100 g/1 cup).
Using a pizza peel or inverted baking sheet, slide one pizza at a time with the parchment paper onto the hot pizza stone. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until the crust is golden brown.
As soon as they come out of the oven, top each pizza with half the burrata. Top with half the shrimp salad. Drizzle with oil and sprinkle with fleur de sel. Cut into slices and serve immediately.

11097.title: Gochujang-Braised Cabbage
ingredients: roasted black and white sesame seeds
instructions: Cabbage: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the cabbage wedges on each side in the oil. Add the broth. Bring to a boil. Cover and cook for 12 minutes, adding broth as needed.
Remove the lid and continue cooking over high heat until the broth has completely evaporated and the cabbage is tender. Remove from the heat.
Butter: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine all of the ingredients.
Add the butter to the skillet and let it melt. Cook over medium-low heat for a few minutes, basting the cabbage wedges with the butter to coat them well. Adjust the seasoning.
Arrange the cabbage wedges on a large serving plate. Sprinkle with the green onion and sesame seeds. Serve with jasmine rice, poultry, pork or grilled beef, if desired.

11098.title: Magie Marier's Gnudi with Sausage Rougail
instructions: Gnudi: In a bowl, combine the ricotta, Parmesan, egg, salt, pepper and nutmeg. Stir in the flour until smooth. Cover with plastic wrap and let rest in the refrigerator for 1 hour.

Shape the cheese mixture into balls, using 15 ml (1 tbsp) for each one (see note). Place the gnudi on a floured baking sheet so they don't stick. Refrigerate until ready to cook. Freeze at this point, if desired.
Sauce: Meanwhile, in a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook the sausage meat in the oil, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until golden brown.

Add the onion and bell pepper. Cook until the vegetables are tender. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and bay leaf. Continue to cook for 1 minute while stirring. Mix in the tomatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Using a wooden spoon, crush half the tomatoes. Add the cilantro. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Chili Relish (optional): In a bowl, combine the chilies, onion, garlic, vinegar and lime juice.
In a small skillet over medium heat, cook the chili mixture in the oil for 5 minutes or until the vegetables are tender, without browning them. Season with salt. Transfer to a bowl. Set aside.

In a large pot of simmering lightly salted water, cook a third of the gnudi at a time for 3 minutes or until they rise to the surface. Using a skimmer or slotted spoon, remove the gnudi and place them on another baking sheet. Oil lightly.

In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, melt a third of the butter at a time. Cook until golden and no longer foaming. Immediately pour into a heat-resistant bowl. Add a third of the gnudi at a time and warm them for 2 minutes, stirring gently to coat them well with the butter. Watch out for splattering. Salt and pepper.
Divide the sauce and gnudi among shallow bowls. Garnish with cilantro leaves. Serve with the chili relish.

11101.title: Minh Phat Tu's Vietnamese Chicken Soup (Pho Style)
instructions: Broth: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
On a non-stick or parchment-lined baking sheet, place the onion quarters and pieces of ginger. Roast for 40 to 45 minutes or until the vegetables start to blacken.

Meanwhile, place the chicken in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Remove from the heat and drain the chicken. Rinse under cold water and drain well. Wash out the pot. Return the chicken to the clean pot.
Meanwhile, in a small skillet over medium heat, dry-toast the cinnamon sticks, star anise, coriander seeds and peppercorns until fragrant. Remove from the heat.

Add the blackened vegetables, spices, water and garlic to the pot with the chicken. Slowly bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 1 hour or until the chicken is cooked. Using a small sieve or slotted spoon, skim the broth, especially at the start of cooking. Let the chicken cool slightly in the broth.
Place a strainer over another pot. Line the colander with a layer of paper towel or a coffee filter. Strain the broth.
Debone the chicken. Compost the vegetables, spices, and the chicken skin and bones. Shred the chicken. Set aside.
Add the sugar and fish sauce to the pot with the broth. Mix well. Keep warm.
Green Onion and Ginger Relish: Meanwhile, in a heatproof bowl, combine the green onions, ginger, chili flakes and salt.
In a small saucepan, heat the vegetable oil until very hot. Pour the hot oil over the green onion mixture. Add the sesame oil and mix.
To Serve: In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the noodles until tender, about 1 minute. Drain the noodles.

Divide the noodles among bowls and top with the shredded chicken. Add the hot broth. Garnish with bean sprouts, Thai basil leaves, cilantro leaves, hot sauce and the green onion and ginger relish, to taste. Serve with lime wedges.

11103.title: Green Curry Coconut Chicken Soup
ingredients: skinless and boneless chicken breast halves
instructions: Curry Paste: In a blender or a personal blender fitted with the grinding blade, purée all the ingredients.

Soup: In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the chicken on each side in the oil for 5 minutes. Season with salt. Add the curry paste and continue cooking for 1 minute, stirring. Add the coconut milk and broth. Bring to a boil. Simmer over medium heat for 6 minutes or until the chicken is cooked, stirring a few times.

Meanwhile, in a pot of salted boiling water, cook the udon for 2 minutes, stirring to separate the noodles. Using tongs and a skimmer, remove the noodles and add them to the broth. Cook for 1 minute. Stir in the lime juice. Adjust the seasoning.
In the same pot of salted boiling water, blanch the broccoli for 2 minutes. Drain the broccoli.
Divide the noodles, chicken and broth among bowls. Garnish with the broccoli, bean sprouts, green onion and cilantro leaves.

11104.title: Baked Omelette Breakfast Sandwiches
instructions: Omelette: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 150 ˚C (300 ˚F). Butter a 28 x 20 cm (11 x 8 inch) glass baking dish.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the salt. Add the water and mix well. Pour the egg mixture into the dish.
Prepare a Water Bath: Place the dish in a large glass baking dish. Pour cold water into the large baking dish to come 1 cm (1/2 inch) up the side of the smaller dish (see note).
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until the eggs are just set. Remove from the oven. Remove the pan from the water bath. Let cool on a wire rack.
Cut the omelette into 6 squares. Refrigerate the omelette squares at this point, if desired (see note).

Sandwiches: For each sandwich, on a work surface, spread the inside of an English muffin with mayonnaise. Top with an omelette square and a slice of cheese. Add toppings of your choice. Serve immediately.

11108.title: Roast Pork Belly
instructions: On a work surface, using a metal skewer or the tip of a paring knife, prick the entire surface of the pork belly. Using a sharp knife, score the fat on the surface of the belly in a crosshatch pattern without cutting into the meat.
Rub all sides of the pork belly with the salt. Place the pork belly in a 33 x 23 cm (13 x 9 inch) glass dish, fat side up. Refrigerate, uncovered, for 12 hours or up to 24 hours.
Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Place a rack on a 46 x 33 cm (18 x 13 inch) baking sheet.
Pat the pork belly dry with paper towels, removing any excess salt that has not dissolved, as needed. Place the pork belly on the rack, fat side up. Bake for about 1 hour.
Reduce the oven temperature to 150 °C (300 °F). Continue cooking for 1 hour 30 minutes or until the fat is crisp and the meat is tender.

Remove from the oven and let rest for 15 minutes. On a work surface, slice the meat. Serve in the Glazed Pork Belly Burgers with Slaw. Also delicious served in small bao buns, as a topping for ramen or with mashed potatoes.

11109.title: Glazed Pork Belly Burgers with Slaw
instructions: Glaze: In a bowl, whisk together all of the ingredients. Set aside 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the mixture in a small bowl for serving.
Dressing: In a large bowl, whisk together all of the ingredients. Season with salt. Set aside 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the dressing in another small bowl for serving.
Coleslaw: Add all the ingredients to the large bowl with the dressing. Toss to coat the vegetables with the dressing. Adjust the seasoning.

Burgers: In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the pork belly slices for 5 minutes per side, until crisp. Pour in the glaze and coat the meat well. Continue cooking for 2 minutes, until the meat is nicely caramelized.
Spread the bottom halves of the buns with the reserved glaze. Top with the pork belly slices and the slaw. Spread the inside of the top halves with the reserved dressing. Close with the bun tops.

11110.title: Sheet Pan Sweet Potato Fries with Spicy Honey
ingredients: homemade or store-bought spicy chili crisp
instructions: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, toss the sweet potatoes with the oil. Season with salt. Spread out on the baking sheet.
Bake for 12 minutes. Remove from the oven. Add the honey and the spicy condiment. Toss to coat the sweet potatoes well. Continue baking for 5 minutes or until the fries are golden brown.
Remove from the oven. Sprinkle the sweet potatoes with fleur de sel. Serve with the Glazed Pork Belly Burgers with Slaw, if desired.

11111.title: Air Fryer Cajun Salmon Sandwiches with Coleslaw
ingredients: milk bread, or other bread of your choice
instructions: Salmon: In a bowl, combine the baking powder and Cajun spice mix. Coat the salmon cubes with the spice mixture. Add the oil and toss to coat the fish cubes.
Place the salmon cubes in the air fryer basket lined with parchment paper. Cook at 200 °C (400 °F) for 7 minutes for pink fish, or longer depending on the desired doneness.
Cajun Mayonnaise: Meanwhile, in another small bowl, whisk together all the ingredients. Set aside.
Sandwiches: In a large bowl, toss the cabbage and onion with the oil, vinegar and mustard. Season with salt.

Spread one side of the bread slices with the Cajun mayonnaise. Place the salmon cubes on half the bread slices. Top with the coleslaw. Close the sandwiches. Serve with chips or a green salad, if desired.

11112.title: Air Fryer Shrimp Burgers with Celery Root Rémoulade
instructions: Patties: In a food processor, chop the shrimp. Pulse a few seconds at a time so they aren't chopped too finely. Transfer to a large bowl.

Add the egg, breadcrumbs, lemon juice and hot sauce. Season with salt and mix well. With lightly oiled hands, shape the mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate. Lightly oil the patties. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Remoulade: Meanwhile, in a large bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.

Burgers: Using a brush, brush the patties with the oil. Place the patties in the air fryer basket lined with parchment paper. Cook at 200 °C (400 °F) for 8 minutes (see note). Turn the patties over and continue cooking for 6 minutes, until cooked through and golden brown.
Spread the inside of the buns with mayonnaise. Top the bottom halves of the buns with a shrimp patty and rémoulade. Add the lettuce leaves and close the burgers.

11113.title: Jonathan Rassi's Chicken in Herbed Yogurt Sauce with Vermicelli Rice
instructions: Chicken: In a large bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Cover and let marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Herb Purée: Meanwhile, in a blender, purée all the ingredients until smooth. Season with salt. Set aside.
Yogurt Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk the cornstarch and 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the broth until smooth. Set aside.

In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown half the chicken at a time on each side in half the oil (15 ml/1 tbsp). Season with salt. Add the remaining broth and simmer for 15 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through.

Add the cornstarch mixture and yogurt. Mix well. Continue cooking for 1 minute or until the sauce thickens. Add 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the herb purée, or more to taste, and the lime juice. Adjust the seasoning.
Vermicelli Rice: Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In an ovenproof saucepan over medium-high heat, toast the vermicelli in the butter for 2 to 3 minutes or until golden brown, stirring constantly. Remove 90 ml (6 tbsp) of the vermicelli and set aside in a bowl to garnish the rice.

Add the rice to the saucepan and continue cooking for 30 seconds, stirring to coat it well with the butter. Add the water and bay leaf. Season with salt. Bring to a boil. Cover and bake for 15 minutes or until the liquid is completely absorbed.
Remove from the oven and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Remove the lid and fluff the rice with a fork. Remove and compost the bay leaf.
Garnish: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the cabbage, radishes and white parts of the green onions with the oil and lime juice. Salt and pepper.
Divide the rice among shallow bowls. Add the yogurt chicken. Top with the reserved vermicelli and the cabbage mixture. Serve with the lime wedges.

11115.title: Lesley Chesterman's Braised Pork Cheeks with Potato and Parsnip Purée
instructions: Pork Cheeks: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
In a large Dutch oven or ovenproof pot over medium-high heat, brown the cheeks on each side in the oil. Salt and pepper. Set the meat aside on a plate. Keep the cooking fat in the pot.

In the same pot, soften the carrots, onion, celery and leek in the cooking fat for 2 minutes. Add more oil as needed. Add the garlic and continue to cook for 1 minute while stirring. Add the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.

Deglaze with the wine and let reduce by half. Add the veal stock, thyme and bay leaves. Return the meat to the pot. Bring to a boil. Cover and bake for 2 hours 30 minutes or until the cheeks are tender, turning them halfway through cooking.

Remove the pot from the oven. Remove the meat from the pot and place it on a plate. Over medium-high heat, reduce the cooking liquid by a third, 7 to 8 minutes, if desired. Remove the thyme and bay leaves, then compost them. Return the meat to the sauce to reheat it.

Purée: Meanwhile, place the potatoes and parsnips in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil and simmer for 25 minutes or until the vegetables are tender and fall apart easily with a fork. Drain the vegetables. Return to the saucepan.
In another small saucepan, heat the milk and cream.
Off the heat, using a potato masher or food mill, mash the vegetables until smooth. Stir in the milk mixture and butter. Add nutmeg. Season with salt.
Garnish: Meanwhile, in a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook the onions in the oil and butter, stirring almost constantly, until golden brown, 10 to 15 minutes. Salt and pepper.
Divide the vegetable purée and pork cheeks among plates. Top with sauce and garnish with the caramelized onions.

11159.title: Blueberry Oat Almond Squares
instructions: Blueberry Filling: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter an 8-inch (20 cm) square pan and line with a strip of parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.

In a pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar and cornstarch. Add the blueberries and lemon juice. Bring gently to a boil, stirring often, until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat and let cool.
Crumble: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the oats, ground almonds, flour, baking soda and salt.
In another bowl, mix the butter with the brown sugar using a spatula. Add the egg and whisk until smooth. Stir in the dry ingredients. Press two thirds of the crumble into the bottom of the pan.
Spread the blueberry filling over the crumble in the pan. Sprinkle with the remaining crumble, coarsely crumbling it over the fruit.
Bake for 40 minutes or until the crumble is golden brown. Let cool.
Unmould. On a work surface, cut into squares.

11160.title: Confetti White Chocolate Squares
instructions: Cookie: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter an 8-inch (20 cm) square pan and line with a strip of parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.

In another bowl, whisk together the butter, brown sugar and sugar. Add the egg and vanilla. Mix until smooth. Using a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients. Add the chocolate and sprinkles. Press the dough into the pan (see notes).
Bake for 18 minutes or until the cookie is lightly golden around the edges but still very soft in the centre. Let cool completely in the pan, about 2 hours.

Frosting (optional): In a bowl, beat the butter with the icing sugar using an electric mixer for 3 minutes or until pale and creamy. Using a spatula, scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl as needed. Add the strawberry jam, lemon juice and food colouring. Mix well.

Unmould the cookie. On a work surface, spread the frosting over it with a spatula. Sprinkle with the sprinkles. Cut into 9 squares. The cookies will keep for 3 days in an airtight container at room temperature.

11161.title: Sheet Pan Sausage Gnocchi with Arugula Pesto
ingredients: mild or hot Italian sausage meat
instructions: Gnocchi: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
On a non-stick baking sheet or in a large baking dish, coat the tomatoes, gnocchi and onion with the oil. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
With your hands, break the sausage meat into pieces and scatter them over the gnocchi mixture. Bake for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the water, sun-dried tomatoes, tomato paste and garlic. Salt and pepper.

Remove from the oven. Spread the sun-dried tomato mixture over it. Mix well. Continue baking for 10 minutes or until the sausage is lightly browned, the gnocchi are tender and the sauce has reduced. Adjust the seasoning.
Pesto: Meanwhile, in a small food processor, blend all the ingredients until smooth. Salt and pepper.
On the baking sheet, scatter the cheese among the gnocchi. Top with the pesto. Serve immediately.

11178.title: Minh Phat Tu's Mapo Tofu
ingredients: dried Thai or bird's eye chili pepper
instructions: In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, soften the white parts of the green onions and the garlic with the Sichuan pepper and chili in the oil for 1 minute. Add the pork and cook, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, for 6 minutes or until it starts to brown.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, dissolve the cornstarch in 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the water.
Add the soybean paste, soy sauces, oyster sauce, rice wine and remaining water to the skillet with the meat mixture. Cook for 7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the cornstarch mixture and continue cooking for 1 minute or until the sauce thickens, stirring. Add the tofu and mix gently to coat it with the sauce.
Spread the mapo tofu on a large serving plate. Sprinkle with the greens of the green onions. Serve with white rice, if desired.

11179.title: Minh Phat Tu's Baby Bok Choy with Tofu Dip
instructions: Bok choy: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
On the baking sheet, coat the baby bok choy with the oil. Salt and pepper. Bake for 12 minutes, stirring halfway through. Let cool.
Yogurt dip: In a food processor, blend all the ingredients except the tofu until smooth. Using a spatula, scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed.
Add the tofu to the food processor and purée until smooth. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed. Season with salt.
Spread the dip on a serving plate. Top with the baby bok choy.

11183.title: Colombe St-Pierre's Maple Tarte Tatin
ingredients: medium Honeycrisp, Empire or Cortland apples
instructions: Dough: In a bowl, combine the flour and butter, rubbing the butter into the flour with your fingertips until it is the size of small peas. Make a well in the centre of the flour mixture. Add the egg white and sparkling water to it. Pulse again until the dough just begins to form. Add more sparkling water, as needed. Shape into a disc with your hands. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Apples: Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F).

In a 25 to 30 cm (10 to 12 inch) cast-iron skillet, bring the maple syrup and butter to a boil. Add grated tonka bean and continue cooking for 2 minutes, stirring. Drizzle with the lemon juice. Remove from the heat.

Add the apples and arrange them core side up, overlapping them and starting from the outside of the skillet. Continue to arrange the apples in tight concentric circles to cover the entire bottom of the skillet. Continue cooking until the syrup thickens. Remove from the heat.
Assembly: On a floured work surface, roll out the dough into a 30 cm (12 inch) circle.
Place the circle of dough over the apples, tucking the edge of the dough inside the skillet. Using a fork, prick the dough in a few places. Bake for 45 minutes.

Remove the skillet from the oven. Tilt the skillet slightly to verify the quantity of liquid remaining. The liquid should be very thick and syrupy, but not completely evaporated. If there is too much liquid, continue to bake, checking on the quantity of liquid every 5 minutes. Remove the skillet from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes.
Run a thin blade between the apples and the skillet. Flip the tarte out onto a serving plate. Be careful, the handle of the skillet will still be hot. Let the tarte cool for 30 minutes.
Toppings (optional): In a bowl, whip the cream with the sugar, thyme and lemon zest using an electric mixer until firm but still soft peaks form.
In a small saucepan, gently heat the alcohol. Remove from the heat and flambé with a long match. Carefully pour it over the tart right away.

Cut the tart into wedges. Serve with the whipped cream. Although the pie will keep for 2 days in the refrigerator, it is best enjoyed warm the same day it is made. Let sit out at room temperature before serving.

11201.title: Beef Flat Iron Steak with Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Sauce
instructions: Sauce: In a blender, purée all of the ingredients until smooth. Season with salt. Set aside.
Tomatoes: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt. Set aside.
Flat Iron Steak: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Place the steak on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Grill the meat for 3 minutes on each side for rare or until the desired doneness. Set the meat aside on another plate. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes. On a work surface, slice the meat against the grain.
Spread the sauce over the bottom of a large serving plate. Add the meat and top with the tomato mixture. Serve with the Patatas Bravas-Style Crispy Sweet Potatoes, if desired.

11202.title: Patatas Bravas-Style Crispy Sweet Potatoes
instructions: Sweet Potatoes: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a saucepan of salted boiling water, cook the sweet potatoes for 5 minutes or until al dente. Drain the sweet potatoes.
In a large bowl, toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, cheese and starch. Salt and pepper. Place the sweet potatoes on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 30 minutes or until the sweet potatoes are golden and crisp, stirring halfway through cooking.

Tomato Sauce: Meanwhile, in a small saucepan over medium heat, soften the shallots and garlic in the oil. Add the tomato paste and spices. Cook for 1 minute while stirring. Add the remaining ingredients and continue cooking for 7 minutes, stirring a few times. Salt and pepper.
In a blender, purée the sauce until smooth. Set aside.
Garlic Mayonnaise: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the mayonnaise and garlic.
Assembly: Spread the sweet potatoes on a serving plate. Top with the tomato sauce and garlic mayonnaise (see note). Sprinkle with the green onions.

11203.title: Jonathan Rassi's Squid Balls with Dashi and Soba Noodles
instructions: Meatballs: On a work surface, separate the head from the squid tubes. Using a knife, cut off the head. Remove the beak and the cartilage inside the tube. Compost the head and cartilage.

Cut off the fins and remove the skin. Clean the tubes and tentacles under cold water. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. Cut 100 g (3 1/2 oz) of the tubes into small dice. Set aside. Coarsely cut the remaining tubes and the tentacles into pieces.

In a food processor, purée the squid pieces until smooth. Add the bread, egg whites, cream, ginger, sesame oil and sambal oelek. Mix until smooth. Using a spatula, scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed. Transfer the mixture to a bowl. Add the reserved diced squid and the white part of the green onions. Season with salt and pepper.
Using a 15 ml (1 tbsp) ice cream scoop, shape the squid mixture into balls and place them on a baking sheet or a large plate (see note). Set aside in the refrigerator.
Dashi: Meanwhile, pour the water into a large saucepan and add the kombu sheets. Let infuse for 20 minutes.
Bring the infusion to a simmer. As soon as it starts to boil, remove the kombu and compost it.
Add the bonito flakes to the same saucepan and remove the saucepan from the heat. Let steep for 6 to 8 minutes or until the bonito settles at the bottom of the saucepan.
Strain the broth through a sieve set over a large measuring cup. Compost the bonito. Return the broth to the saucepan. Add the soy sauce.
Cook the squid balls in the broth over medium-low heat (see note). When the balls rise to the surface, simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and carrot to the broth with the balls. Cook for 3 minutes. Remove from the heat.

Garnish: Meanwhile, in a pot of salted boiling water, cook the soba noodles until al dente, about 2 minutes. Drain the noodles and rinse them quickly under cold water. Toss the noodles with a little oil.
Divide the soba noodles, hot broth with the balls, mushrooms and carrot among bowls. Garnish with the green onions, nori and cilantro leaves.

11207.title: Ashley Thornton's Carrot Ginger Bundt Cake
instructions: Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Generously butter a 10 to 12-cup (2.5 to 3 litres) Bundt pan.
In a bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and spices.

In another bowl, beat the eggs with the sugar using an electric mixer until smooth. Add the oil, buttermilk and vanilla. Add the carrots, apple and ginger. Mix well. With the machine running on low speed or with a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients. Spread the batter out in the prepared pan.
Bake for 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool for 15 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 80 °C (175 °F).
Unmould cake, flipping on a wire rack. Let cool completely, about 1 hour.
Carrot Chips: Meanwhile, spread the carrot ribbons on a baking sheet lined with a silicone mat, without overlapping them.

Bake for 1 hour, depending on the thickness of the ribbons, or until the carrots are dry but still tender, without letting them roast. Using a small sieve, dust the carrot chips with the icing sugar. Sprinkle lightly with fleur de sel. Let cool on the baking sheet, about 30 minutes.

Candied Pecans: Meanwhile, in a pot, bring the pecans and syrup to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until the syrup crystalizes around the pecans, about 3 to 4 minutes.

Spread the pecans out in a baking sheet. Sprinkle with more fleur de sel, to taste. Let cool completely, about 30 minutes. The pecans will keep for 3 weeks in an airtight container at room temperature.
Frosting: In a bowl, cream the cheese with the orange zest using an electric mixer. On low speed, gradually add the maple syrup until the frosting is smooth and creamy.
Place the cake on a serving dish. Cover the top of the cake with the icing. Decorate with sugared pecans and carrot chips. The cake will keep for 3 days, covered, at room temperature.

11210.title: Marc Maulà's Pappardelle with White Chicken Bolognese (Ragù Bianco)
instructions: Bolognese: In a saucepan over high heat, cook the chicken in the oil, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, for 5 minutes or until lightly browned. Salt and pepper.

Add the mushrooms, onions, celery, garlic, rosemary, fennel seeds and chili flakes. Cook for 5 minutes. Add the mustard and continue cooking for 1 minute, stirring. Sprinkle with the flour. Continue to cook for 1 minute while stirring. Add the wine and reduce by half.
Pour in the broth. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium-low heat, uncovered, for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring a few times. Adjust the seasoning (see note).
Pappardelle: Meanwhile, in a pot of salted boiling water, cook the pasta until al dente. Set aside 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the cooking water. Drain the pasta and return to the pot.

Add the sauce and stir to coat the pasta well. Continue cooking for 2 minutes or until the pasta has absorbed the sauce. Add the reserved pasta cooking water to thin out the sauce as needed. Remove from the heat.
Add the Parmesan, cream cheese, chives, and lemon zest and juice. Mix well. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve the pasta in shallow bowls sprinkled with Parmesan.

11211.title: Marc Maulà's Gluten-Free Chocolate and Caramelized Buckwheat Cookies
instructions: Caramelized Buckwheat: Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

In a skillet over medium-high heat, cook the buckwheat and sugar, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, for 6 to 7 minutes or until the sugar melts, turns grainy and coats the buckwheat groats. Spread on the baking sheet and let cool. Crush into small pieces. The caramelized buckwheat keeps for 1 week in an airtight container at room temperature (see note).
Cookies: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line two baking sheets with silicone mats or parchment paper.
In a glass bowl set over a double boiler, or in the microwave, melt half the chocolate (150 g/5 1/3 oz).
In another bowl, combine the flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt.

In a third bowl, cream the butter with the brown sugar and vanilla using an electric mixer. Add the eggs and beat for 2 minutes or until fluffy. Add the melted chocolate and mix. On low speed or with a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients, the remaining chopped chocolate and the caramelized buckwheat.
Using a 45 ml (3 tbsp) ice cream scoop, shape balls of dough and place them on the baking sheets, spacing them apart (see note). Freeze at this point, if desired (see note).

Bake one sheet at a time for 10 to 11 minutes or until the cookies are puffed and cracked on top but still soft in the centre, rotating the sheet halfway through. Let cool slightly on the baking sheets.

11214.title: Sushi-Style Salmon
ingredients: roasted black and white sesame seeds
instructions: Rice: Place rice in a bowl and cover with cold water. Gently rinse rice until water becomes cloudy. Drain and repeat four to five times or until water runs completely clear. Leave rice in a sieve until it is well drained.
Place the rice and water in the rice cooker bowl. Close the lid. Select the White Rice function. The rice is ready when the machine switches to the Warm function.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the vinegar, sugar and salt just until the sugar and salt have dissolved.

Place the cooked rice in a bowl. Add the vinegar mixture and stir with a spatula until all the rice is well coated with the vinegar mixture (watch out for the steam). Make a hole in the centre of the rice and let rest for 5 minutes.
Mayonnaise: Meanwhile, mix all the ingredients until smooth. Set aside.
Salmon: Meanwhile, place the rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the sesame seeds on a small plate.

On a work surface, starting at the thinnest end, slice the salmon portions horizontally and open them up without cutting all the way through, to make a long strip of fish. Season with salt. Lay 1 ½ strips of nori along the length of each portion. Roll each portion up into a tournedos. Roll the sides of the tournedos in the sesame seeds. Place the tournedos on the baking sheet.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until pink, depending on the thickness of the fillet. Serve with the rice and the Sesame-Lemon Tempura Vegetables, if desired.

11215.title: Sesame-Lemon Tempura Vegetables
instructions: Sesame Lemon Salt: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Set aside.

Tempura Vegetables: Preheat the oil in a deep fryer to 350°F (180°C). Place a rack on a baking sheet or line it with paper towels. Preheat the oven to 95 °C (200 °F) to keep the vegetables warm as they are fried.

In a bowl, combine 1 cup (120 g) of the flour with the salt and baking soda. Gradually whisk in the water and vinegar, whisking just until the batter is smooth. Add sparkling water to thin the batter, as needed. Set the bowl of batter over another bowl two-thirds full of ice cubes.
Place the remaining flour in a large shallow dish. In another shallow bowl, place the rice cereal.

Dredge the carrot spirals, lettuce leaves and cilantro sprigs in the flour, a few at a time, and shake off the excess. Dip the vegetables in the batter one at a time, holding them by one end. Immediately dredge them in the rice cereal. Lower them into the deep fryer, gently shaking the basket so they don't stick. Fry a few vegetables at a time for 2 to 3 minutes or until golden brown, turning them halfway through. Drain on the baking sheet. Sprinkle the vegetables with the sesame lemon salt.
Arrange the tempura vegetables and avocado wedges on a serving plate. Delicious with the Salmon Sushi.

11249.title: Lemon, Lavender and Amaretto Cocktail
instructions: Lavender Syrup: In a small pot, bring the water and sugar to a boil until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat. Add the lavender flowers. Cover and let infuse for 15 minutes.

Strain the syrup through a sieve placed over a bowl, pressing on the flowers with the back of a ladle to extract as much liquid as possible. Compost the flowers. Cover and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 1 hour (see note).
Cocktail: Rub the rim of an old fashioned glass with the lemon zest. Place the large ice cube in the glass.

In a shaker, combine the amaretto, lemon juice, lavender syrup and foamer. Add the ice cubes, then shake vigorously. Strain into the glass. Garnish the rim of the glass with the lemon zest and a lavender stem.

11250.title: Colombe St-Pierre's Beluga Lentil Dal
instructions: Dal: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the onion and garlic in the oil. Salt and pepper. Add the lentils and cook for 1 minute, stirring to coat them with the oil. Add the curry powder and mix. Add the tomatoes. Bring to a boil. Simmer gently for 10 to 15 minutes or until the lentils are al dente, stirring frequently.
Add the coconut milk and mix. Continue cooking for 10 to 12 minutes or until the lentils are tender. Adjust the seasoning.
Salsa: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Assembly: Spread the dal in a shallow serving dish. Top with the salsa, sour cream and herbs. Serve with the lemon wedges and basmati rice, if desired.

11251.title: Lesley Chesterman's Herbed Basmati Rice
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold running water until the water runs clear. Drain well. Place the rice in a bowl. Cover with cold water and let soak for 2 hours at room temperature.
In a large pot of boiling lightly salted water, cook the rice for 6 to 7 minutes. Drain the rice and rinse it under lukewarm water.

In the same pot or a large skillet over medium-high heat, melt the butter with the oil. Soften half the green onions and half the dill for 1 minute. Add half the rice, covering the herb mixture. Season with salt. Remove from the heat.
Sprinkle the rice with the remaining green onions and dill. Cover with the remaining rice. Season with salt. Using the handle of a wooden spoon, poke a few holes in the rice.

Wrap the lid of the pot in a clean tea towel and place it on the pot (this keeps condensation from dripping back into the rice and making it soggy). Cook over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes or until the rice is tender.
Transfer the rice to a serving bowl, taking care to loosen the crisp crust from the bottom of the pot. Delicious with the Salmon with Herbed Cream Sauce.

11252.title: Lesley Chesterman's Salmon with Herbed Cream Sauce
ingredients: dry white wine or fish stock
instructions: Salmon: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
On a plate, season the salmon portions with salt and pepper.

In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the fish, flesh side first, in the butter and oil for 3 minutes. Carefully turn the fish portions over and continue cooking for 1 to 2 minutes to brown the skin. They should still be raw in the centre.
